title: Bar builders & series rendering (time/tick/volume/range/renko)
body:
## Context
CandleViewer does not trust the exchange to define what a bar is. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §2 states it plainly: "Exchange klines are a **cross-check and a cold-start backfill**, not the primary bar source: CandleViewer builds its own bars from trades (§3) so that time/tick/volume/range/delta/renko all share one code path." Every order-flow surface that follows in R2 — footprint (E18), profiles (E19), Deep-Stats (E20), CVD (E23) — is computed per bar, so the bar is the substrate of the whole product. If bars are wrong, everything downstream is wrong in a way no amount of rendering polish can hide.

This Epic delivers two halves that must agree exactly:

1. **Backend bar builders (module M8)** — the six `BarBuilder` implementations of `24-internal-schemas.md` §3 (time, tick, volume, range, delta, renko), each consuming `TradeEvent` only so that **live and replay produce byte-identical bars** (the tardis-machine property, §11 of the same document), plus `BarBuilderSet` multi-spec fan-out, `snapshot()`/`restore()` mid-bar resumption, the `bars_*` QuestDB tables of `21-database-schema.md` §4.8, the `/market/klines` and `/market/bars` REST endpoints of `22-api-openapi.yaml`, and the `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` WS topic of `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.
2. **Frontend series rendering (module M7, `packages/chart-engine`)** — candlestick, OHLC bar, line, area, baseline and Heikin-Ashi series drawn through the E11 chassis, the min/max-preserving LOD ladder of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6, forming-vs-closed bar semantics driven by the `confirm` flag, the volume column sub-pane, and symbol/timeframe/bar-mode switching that reuses the engine instead of tearing it down.

`30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criterion 4 is the acceptance bar for the whole Epic: **"All five bar types produce identical results to a reference implementation on a recorded fixture day, byte-for-byte on OHLCV."** §13 places E12 on the critical path `E02 → E06 → E11 → E12 → E18 → E26 → E38 → E44 → E46 → GA`; §12 lists Renko and range bars as the second rung of the descoping ladder, so those two builders are deliberately scheduled last within the Epic and are the only cuttable scope.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Stories (US ids from `11-user-stories.md` domains CHART and MKT):**
- **US-MKT-008** Historical OHLCV backfill (Must) — paged `/v5/market/kline` backfill, cache-first paint, rate-limit backoff.
- **US-CHART-001** Candlestick rendering (Must) — the candle series itself and the deep-zoom LOD behaviour.
- **US-CHART-002** Alternative chart types (Should) — OHLC bars, line, area, baseline, Heikin-Ashi, volume column pane.
- **US-CHART-003** Order-flow bar modes (Must) — volume bars and tick bars from the shared ingestion path.
- **US-CHART-004** Range, Renko, delta bars (Should/Could) — P&F explicitly deferred out of this Epic.
- **US-CHART-005** Timeframe switching (Must) — standard ladder, sub-minute, custom intervals, no engine teardown.

(Chart chassis stories US-CHART-006/007/008/010/014 belong to **E11**, not here; US-CHART-012 templates belong to E15; US-CHART-013 overlays to E31.)

**Screens/components:** SCR-030 chart panel, SCR-041 symbol/interval quick-switcher, SCR-042 interval / bar-mode menu, SCR-047 chart empty / no-data state, SCR-151 empty-state pattern · CMP-219 SymbolPicker, CMP-220 IntervalPicker, CMP-221 ChartToolbar, CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle, CMP-226 BarCountdown, CMP-041 Menu, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-021 Skeleton, CMP-026 EmptyState.

**API/WS:** `GET /market/klines`, `GET /market/bars`, `GET /instruments` (consumed), WS topic `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` with `BarsBatch` payload kind 4.

**Tables:** QuestDB `bars_time`, `bars_tick`, `bars_volume`, `bars_range`, `bars_renko`, `bars_delta`; Postgres `chart_settings.bar_mode` (`21-database-schema.md` §1869–1909).

**Internal schemas:** `BarSpec`, `Bar`, `BarUpdate`, `BarBuilder`, `BuilderState`, `BarBuilderSet`, `BarSeries.densify()`.

## Out of scope
- Point & Figure bars (`pnf`) — the API and WS enums reserve the value; no builder ships in R1 (descoping-ladder rung 2 neighbourhood, Could-level in US-CHART-004).
- Footprint cells, profiles and Deep-Stats rows built *per bar* — E18/E19/E20.
- The indicator runtime that consumes bars — E13.
- The recorder that produces the trade tape the builders consume — E16.
- Chart chassis (scale math, pan/zoom, crosshair, axes, DOM-mirror a11y) — E11.
- Replay-driven bar construction — E26 reuses these builders unmodified; no replay-specific code here.
- Android/mobile clients — out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All bar types match the reference on a recorded fixture day
  Given the version-controlled BTCUSDT fixture day and a reference implementation
  When every builder (time, tick, volume, range, delta, renko) replays that day
  Then OHLCV is byte-identical to the reference for every bar of every spec
  And the total volume across bars equals the total traded volume (invariant BI-1)

Scenario: Live and replay agree
  Given the same trade sequence delivered live and then via replay
  Then the resulting Bar objects are identical including spec_hash (invariant BI-4)

Scenario: Switching bar mode does not tear down the engine
  Given a BTCUSDT chart on 5m time bars with drawings and indicators applied
  When I switch to "volume bars, 1500"
  Then the same engine instance re-binds to the new series within 200 ms of data arrival
  And drawings remain anchored by timestamp, and no WebGL context is recreated

Scenario: History is shallower than the requested window
  Given the recorder holds only 3 days of prints for the symbol
  When a tick-bar series is requested over 30 days
  Then bars are built for the available window only
  And an explicit partial-history marker names the timestamp where tick data begins
  And no REST klines are silently substituted for the missing tick-accurate region
```

## Technical notes / design
- Builders live in the backend (`M8`), never in the browser: `US-CHART-003` NFR requires one shared construction path for live and replay. The frontend receives `Bar` rows over REST/WS and renders them; the only client-side transform permitted is Heikin-Ashi (US-CHART-002 explicitly requires it client-side with no refetch).
- `spec_hash` (sha256 of canonical `BarSpec` JSON) is the cache key everywhere — QuestDB `bar_param`, WS topic `param`, builder-state blobs, and the frontend series cache all derive from the same spec.
- Renko/range bars have no fixed time width; the renderer spaces them by index (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 note and `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 renko edge case c). Time-based indicators over such series are disabled in the UI with an explanatory tooltip — that gating is E13's consumer-side work but the series must expose an `isTimeAligned: false` flag for it.
- LOD L2 candle decimation must be **min/max preserving** — a correctness requirement, not cosmetics.
- `confirm: false` on the last bar of any frame means "forming"; a client that treats it as closed reproduces the exact flicker bug Bybit's flag exists to prevent (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 note).

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85% on the `bar_builders` backend package and the series modules of `packages/chart-engine`.
- **Property** BI-1…BI-6 of `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.4 over ≥1M synthetic trades, plus random-cut-point snapshot/restore equivalence.
- **Golden file** recorded fixture day per builder, byte-compared.
- **Contract** generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines`, `/market/bars` and the `BarsBatch` schema.
- **Golden image** candle/bar/line/area/HA series at each LOD tier on SwiftShader (reusing E11-T08's harness).
- **E2E** Playwright + Electron: open chart, switch interval, switch bar mode, confirm forming-bar behaviour.
- **Perf** series-render benchmark wired into CI; backfill and rebuild throughput measured.

## Security notes
Market data is not secret, but this Epic adds a large user-controlled parameter surface. Threats (STRIDE, carried on E12-X-scope within E11's engine model plus this Epic's own review): **DoS** via an unbounded `from/to/limit` or an absurd `param` (`tick:1` over 30 days) — every endpoint enforces `BarLimit`, a per-request bar cap and a per-user concurrent-rebuild cap; **resource exhaustion** via subscribing to dozens of distinct `spec_hash`es — the `BarBuilderSet` cap (3–8 specs per symbol, §3.5) is enforced server-side with a clear error; **information disclosure** — `bars` topics require `marketdata:read` like every other market topic, RBAC-checked at subscribe. No PII, no secrets, no key material touched.

## Accessibility notes
Series rendering is canvas; accessibility is delivered through E11's DOM-mirror and the SCR-045 data table, which this Epic must **feed** with per-bar OHLCV, delta and the forming/closed flag. Specific obligations here: the bar-mode menu (SCR-042 / CMP-220) presents bar modes as a separate labelled group with an explanatory note because they change the meaning of the x-axis; chart-type options name the type in text, never icon-only (CMP-222); partial-history and no-data states are text, not colour; the bar countdown (CMP-226) is text with `aria-live="off"` by default. WCAG 2.2 AA, axe-core zero violations on SCR-030/041/042/047.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3: p95 frame ≤16.6 ms with 100k bars and all R1 overlays; ≥55 fps at 100k bars zoom-to-fit via LOD; ≤300 ms to first paint from cache for 5 000 bars (US-MKT-008); interval switch ≤200 ms from cache (US-CHART-005); chart-type switch ≤100 ms (US-CHART-002); rebuild of 1M prints ≤10 s and cancellable (US-CHART-003/004); ingest→bar-emit adds no measurable p95 to the ≤20 ms ingest→bus budget.

## Observability
Metrics: `bars_built_total{symbol,kind}`, `bars_late_trade_dropped_total`, `bar_build_latency_seconds`, `bar_rebuild_duration_seconds{kind}`, `bar_builder_specs_active`, `bar_backfill_pages_total`, `bar_backfill_rate_limited_total`, `bars_ws_frames_total`, `series_frame_ms` (engine). Structured logs on rebuild start/finish/cancel with `spec_hash`. A Grafana row "Bar builders" with build latency, active specs and late-trade drops; alert when `bars_late_trade_dropped_total` rate exceeds zero for 5 minutes.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2: every child Done or explicitly descoped; roadmap exit criterion 4 (byte-for-byte parity) demonstrated and recorded; coverage ≥85% backend/engine and ≥80% frontend; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3, `21-database-schema.md` §4.8, `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 reflect shipped behaviour; axe-core green plus one manual screen-reader pass on the chart surfaces introduced here; perf numbers recorded against the budgets above; QA epic-level regression pass recorded; demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review on staging (demo).

## Dependencies
- **E07** storage spike — QuestDB write path and Parquet cold tier decisions the `bars_*` tables depend on.
- **E08** Bybit adapter & ingestion — `TradeEvent` on the internal bus and the REST kline client.
- **E11** chart-engine core — scene graph, transforms, LOD infrastructure, data stores.
- **E17** WS protocol (via E11) — the `bars` topic rides the frozen transport.
- Consumed by **E13** indicators, **E18** footprint, **E26** replay.

## Branch
`feat/e12-bars-series`, with child branches `feat/e12-<ticket-slug>` merged into `main` via the merge queue (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §7); PRs ≤400 LOC diff preferred.

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §2 (trade events), §3 (bar builders, invariants BI-1…BI-6), §11 (replay bus)
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.8 `bars_*`, §4.9 footprint grid alignment, retention table
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines`, `/market/bars`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 topic catalogue, §14.3 `BarsBatch`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 data model, §3.6 LOD, §4 render layers, §15 milestones M1–M3
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 (E12 scope), §5.3 (exit criteria), §11 (dependency graph), §12 (descoping ladder), §13 (critical path)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §4 MKT, §5 CHART · `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030/041/042/047 · `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-219…CMP-226

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: UX research: how traders choose, parameterise and trust non-time bars
body:
## Context
E12 introduces a capability that no other epic in the programme introduces: bars whose x-axis is **not the clock**. `US-CHART-003` (volume bars, tick bars) is a Must, `US-CHART-004` (range, delta, Renko, P&F) is Should/Could, and `US-CHART-005` adds sub-minute and custom time intervals on top. `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-042 already states the surface must expose "Volume, Tick, Range, Renko and Point & Figure modes with inline parameter fields", and `CMP-220 IntervalPicker` already carries the a11y note that bar modes "are a separate labelled group with an explanatory note, since they change the meaning of the x-axis".

That note is a design problem, not a copy problem. A trader who does not realise the x-axis stopped being time will misread every drawing, every session boundary and every alert anchored to that chart. Two further trust problems are specific to this epic: (a) non-time bars are built from the **recorded trade tape**, so history is only as deep as the recorder (`US-CHART-003` scenario "Insufficient tick history", `US-CHART-005` "Sub-minute interval"), and (b) changing a parameter triggers a **rebuild from stored prints with a progress indicator** (`US-CHART-004` scenario "Parameter change"), which is a long, cancellable operation the user must understand rather than fear.

This study exists so that E12-D02..E12-D08 are grounded in how the Owner and managers actually reason about these modes, and so the vocabulary used for "partial history", "rebuilding", "aggregated/LOD" and "forming vs closed bar" is decided **once**, before six separate hi-fi tickets invent six variants of it. The participant pool is small and known (`10-personas.md`), so this is qualitative: structured interviews plus a stimulus comparison task.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Research plan and discussion guide covering `US-CHART-002`, `US-CHART-003`, `US-CHART-004`, `US-CHART-005`, `US-CHART-010`.
- 4–6 sessions (Owner, available account managers, and up to 2 external perp/order-flow traders if recruitable) covering: (a) which bar modes they use today and on which platform, and what parameter they reach for first; (b) how they currently discover that a chart is *not* time-based; (c) what they expect to happen to drawings, indicators and alerts when the bar mode or parameter changes; (d) their tolerance for a rebuild that takes seconds.
- Stimulus set: comparison boards of 3 candidate treatments each for — the **non-time x-axis banner/affordance** on `SCR-030`, the **partial-history marker** ("tick data begins here") on the price area, the **rebuild progress + cancel** affordance, and the **LOD/aggregation indicator** required by `US-CHART-001` scenario "Deep zoom out".
- A recommended **bar-mode vocabulary**: canonical user-facing names and one-line descriptions for time / tick / volume / range / delta / Renko / P&F, matching the `bar_type` enum in `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 topic `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`, plus the unit label for each `param` (trades, base-asset volume, ticks, signed volume, ticks-or-`atr:14`, `box:reversal`).
- Findings report at `docs/research/findings/E12-bar-modes.md` including recommended defaults per mode, the precedence rule when two states co-occur (e.g. *partial history* **and** *rebuilding*), and explicit "do not do this" anti-patterns.
- Corrections raised against `14-screens-catalogue.md` (SCR-042, SCR-047) and `15-component-catalogue.md` (CMP-220, CMP-222) wherever evidence contradicts the current wording, rather than silently diverging.
- Input handoff recorded as comments on E12-D02 (wireframes) and E12-D09 (design-system contribution).

## Out of scope
- Any pixel-level or hi-fi visual design — that is E12-D03..E12-D08.
- Footprint cell design, profiles and TPO (E18/E19) — this study covers the **price series and its bar construction only**.
- Drawing-tool re-anchoring interaction design (E14 owns the tools; this study only captures the *expectation*, and files the finding to E14).
- Indicator parameter UX (E13) and replay controls (E26).
- Quantitative usability benchmarking / SUS scoring — the pool is too small to be meaningful.
- Mobile/Android contexts (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).

```gherkin
Scenario: Study executed and reported
  Given the research plan and discussion guide are approved by the CDO
  When at least 4 sessions have been run and transcribed
  Then a findings report exists at docs/research/findings/E12-bar-modes.md
  And it names every bar mode with a user-facing label, a one-line description and the unit of its parameter

Scenario: Recommendations map to something the backend can emit
  Given the findings recommend a state such as "partial history" or "rebuilding"
  When an engineer opens an E12 story
  Then each recommended state maps to a real condition available from GET /api/v1/market/bars or the bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param} topic
  And any recommendation that no current API or topic can express is filed as an explicit gap with a linked follow-up ticket

Scenario: Evidence contradicts the screens catalogue
  Given participants consistently fail to notice that the x-axis is no longer time in the SCR-042 stimulus
  When the findings are reviewed with the CDO
  Then a correction to 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-042 is raised in the same sprint
  And the superseded wording is recorded in the decision log rather than deleted silently

Scenario: Colour-only or motion-only signalling is rejected (edge)
  Given a candidate treatment distinguishes a forming bar from a closed bar by hue or by a pulse alone
  When it is evaluated against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  Then it is recorded as rejected with the reason
  And a redundant non-colour, non-motion channel (text, glyph, outline weight) is recommended in its place

Scenario: Participants cannot be recruited (failure)
  Given fewer than 4 participants are available in the sprint
  When the study runs with Owner plus managers only
  Then the report states the reduced sample explicitly as a validity limitation
  And the CDO records in the ticket whether the reduced evidence is sufficient for sign-off of E12-D02
```

## Technical notes / design
- Anchor every stimulus in **real recorded Bybit data** — reuse the same recorded fixtures the E08/E12 integration tests use, so densities, tick sizes and print rates are realistic rather than invented. A synthetic tape makes range and Renko bars look far tidier than they are.
- Run the comparison task in a neutral prototyping tool with no CandleViewer branding, so participants react to the encoding rather than to the product.
- Include at least one stimulus at **extreme density** (100 k bars zoomed to fit, where LOD aggregation is active) and one at **extreme sparsity** (a 1 500-contract volume bar chart on a quiet symbol where bars are minutes apart) — these are the two ends E12's renderer must survive and where mode confusion is worst.
- Capture, per mode, the **first parameter a participant types**; those become the designed defaults in E12-D03 and the engineering defaults in the E12 stories.
- Record how participants read the `confirm: false` semantics described in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 ("A client MUST NOT treat it as closed") — the forming-bar treatment is the visual expression of that protocol rule.

## Test plan
- Not a code deliverable; validated by review rather than automated tests.
- Pilot the discussion guide with one internal participant before the first real session; revise and record the revision.
- Each stimulus board is checked against `05-accessibility-standard.md` for contrast and non-colour redundancy **before** it is shown, so the study never legitimises an inaccessible treatment.
- Findings are cross-checked against `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.
- Peer review of the report by a second designer and by the Architect for feasibility.

## Security notes
- Sessions use recorded fixtures only; no live account, no API keys and no order-entry surface is shown to any participant.
- External participants sign an NDA; recordings are stored in the private research drive and referenced by ID, never committed to the repo.
- The report must not contain account identifiers, balances, position sizes or key material; screenshots are scrubbed of anything account-scoped.
- No participant PII beyond a pseudonymous participant ID appears in `docs/research/findings/E12-bar-modes.md`.

## Accessibility notes
- At least one participant session must be run against the **keyboard-and-screen-reader path** for changing bar mode, since `CMP-220 IntervalPicker` requires bar modes to be an announced, separately labelled group.
- Every candidate treatment must be evaluated for a redundant non-colour channel; colour-only treatments are recorded as rejected with the reason.
- The report must state, per recommended state, how it is announced to a screen reader (text in the accessible name, a live-region message, or a row in the SCR-045 data table).
- Reduced-motion: any candidate that relies on animation to communicate "rebuilding" must have a static equivalent specified.

## Performance notes
- Stimuli must not promise interactions the engine cannot meet: `US-CHART-005` budgets a timeframe switch at ≤200 ms from cache and SCR-042 budgets ≤600 ms first paint uncached. Any treatment implying instant rebuild of a 1 M-print series is recorded as infeasible (the `US-CHART-003` NFR is ≤10 s for 1 M prints).
- Findings must state the **maximum acceptable silent wait** before a rebuild must show progress; that number becomes the threshold specified in E12-D08 and implemented by the E12 engineering stories.

## Observability
- The report lists the analytics events the designed flows imply, aligned with those already named in the catalogue: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed` (SCR-042), `chart.symbol_changed` (SCR-041), `chart.empty_state_shown` with `{reason}` (SCR-047).
- Recommends one new event if justified by the findings (e.g. `chart.bar_rebuild_cancelled`) with its property set, so E12's engineering stories can instrument it rather than retrofitting.

## Definition of Done

- Contradictions with `14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` raised as tickets, not left implicit.
- Handoff comments posted on E12-D02 and E12-D09.
- **CDO sign-off recorded on this ticket; Status = Done.** E12-D02 may not leave Ready until this ticket is Done.

## Dependencies
- No blocking dependencies; runs at the very start of the design-ahead window.
- Consumes recorded Bybit fixtures produced by E08 (ingestion skeleton) if available; if not yet available, a captured tape from the E06 chart-engine spike is an acceptable substitute and the substitution is recorded.
- Feeds E12-D02, E12-D03, E12-D08, E12-D09.

title: Wireframes: bar-mode selection, parameter entry and rebuild flow
body:
## Context
Before any hi-fi pixels are drawn, E12 needs an agreed **flow skeleton**: how a trader gets from a time chart to a 1 500-contract volume chart, what happens to the view while the series rebuilds, what happens to drawings and indicators, and how they get back. `US-CHART-005` demands that a timeframe switch "reuses cached bars and preserves the visible time window centre" with "no flash of empty chart"; `US-CHART-004` demands that a parameter change "rebuilds from stored prints with a progress indicator and drawings re-anchor by timestamp"; the E12 epic scope in `30-release-roadmap.md` §5 explicitly includes "symbol + timeframe switching without a full engine teardown". Those are flow requirements, and flows are cheapest to get wrong in wireframe.

This ticket produces low-fidelity wireframes and flow diagrams for the whole bar-mode surface — `SCR-042` (interval / bar-mode menu), `SCR-041` (quick-switcher), the relevant part of `SCR-031` (chart settings General tab, which already sketches Volume/Tick/Range/Renko fields), and the in-canvas states on `SCR-030` (forming bar, partial history, rebuilding, LOD aggregation) plus the terminal states `SCR-047` (empty/no data) and `SCR-048` (error).

The wireframes are the artefact the Architect reviews for feasibility against `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 (data model), §3.6 (LOD and decimation) and §9 (wire→GPU data flow), so that a flow the engine cannot serve is killed here rather than after it has been rendered at hi-fi.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Wireframe set covering: `SCR-042` menu (grouped time ladder + non-time bar modes with inline `param` fields and the "edit favourites" row defining the `1..9` hotkey ladder), `SCR-041` quick-switcher (symbol + interval in one overlay), `SCR-031` General tab bar-mode block, `SCR-030` in-canvas states, `SCR-047`, `SCR-048`.
- Flow diagrams (to be merged into `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` as mermaid) for: **F-BAR-1** switch time interval (cache hit → cache miss → progressive backfill); **F-BAR-2** switch to a non-time bar mode and enter its parameter; **F-BAR-3** change a parameter on an existing non-time series (rebuild, progress, cancel, revert); **F-BAR-4** switch chart type (candle → Heikin-Ashi → baseline) with the `US-CHART-002` "unsupported combination" branch where Heikin-Ashi is requested together with footprint; **F-BAR-5** insufficient recorded history (partial-history marker → SCR-047 when the whole window is unrecorded).
- A **state matrix** for the chart price area listing every E12 state (cache-loading, progressive-backfill, streaming, forming-bar, closed-bar, rebuilding, partial-history, LOD-aggregated, empty, error) against how it is signalled visually, in text, and to a screen reader, with the precedence order recommended by E12-D01.
- Annotated wireframes marking which existing components are reused (`CMP-041 Menu`, `CMP-048 Combobox`, `CMP-069 InfoPanel`, `CMP-213 FuzzyList`, `CMP-219 SymbolPicker`, `CMP-220 IntervalPicker`, `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle`, `CMP-226 BarCountdown`, `CMP-026 EmptyState`, `CMP-027 ErrorState`, `CMP-029 Skeleton-Chart`) and which behaviours are new and therefore need a design-system entry in E12-D09.
- Architect feasibility review comment recorded on this ticket, referencing `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3, §3.6 and §9.

## Out of scope
- Visual design, typography, colour and token application — E12-D03..E12-D08.
- Footprint, profile, CVD and indicator panes (E13, E18, E19, E23).
- Drawing re-anchoring mechanics beyond stating the requirement in F-BAR-3 (E14 owns the tools).
- Replay-specific bar behaviour (E26) and multi-chart propagation (SCR-049, owned by the layouts epic).
- Any Android or non-web surface.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E12 surface has a wireframe and a flow
  Given the wireframe set is submitted for review
  When it is checked against 14-screens-catalogue.md
  Then SCR-030 (E12 states), SCR-031 (General tab bar block), SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-047 and SCR-048 each have at least one wireframe
  And flows F-BAR-1 through F-BAR-5 each have a mermaid diagram ready to merge into 13-user-flows.md

Scenario: The state matrix is complete and ordered
  Given the state matrix is reviewed
  When two states can co-occur, for example partial history and rebuilding
  Then the matrix states which one wins and what the other degrades to
  And no state is signalled by colour alone in any row

Scenario: A flow the engine cannot serve is rejected (edge)
  Given a wireframe implies that changing the Renko brick size repaints instantly with no intermediate state
  When the Architect reviews it against 26-chart-engine-design.md and the US-CHART-003 NFR of 10 s per 1 M prints
  Then the flow is revised to include an explicit progress and cancel path
  And the rejected variant is recorded in the ticket rather than silently dropped

Scenario: Cancelling a rebuild is a first-class path (failure)
  Given F-BAR-3 is walked with a user who cancels a rebuild at 40 percent
  When the flow is inspected
  Then it specifies exactly what the chart shows afterwards, namely the previous series restored with its previous parameter, not an empty chart
  And the parameter field is restored to its previous value with an explanation

Scenario: Unsupported combination is designed, not error-handled by accident
  Given a user selects Heikin-Ashi while footprint cells are enabled
  When F-BAR-4 is inspected
  Then the flow shows an explanatory message naming why a real-price bar type is required and offering to switch back, per US-CHART-002
  And it does not silently disable footprint
```

## Technical notes / design
- Wireframes are **greyscale and token-free** on purpose; any decision that needs colour to be understood is a finding for E12-D01's vocabulary, not a wireframe decision.
- Model SCR-042 as a real menu with grouped items (time / tick / volume / range / delta / Renko / P&F) per its a11y note, with the `param` field **inside** the group, so mode and parameter are chosen in one gesture rather than two dialogs.
- The parameter field's unit label must come straight from the `/market/bars` `bar_type`/`param` table in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (trades, base-asset volume, ticks, signed volume, ticks or `atr:14`, `box:reversal`) so design and API never disagree about units.
- "No full engine teardown" implies the wireframe for a mode switch keeps the axes, drawings layer and toolbar mounted and swaps only the series; show that explicitly so engineering reads it as a requirement, not an aesthetic.
- The LOD/aggregation indicator required by `US-CHART-001` ("the aggregation level is indicated") is wireframed as persistent chrome, not a transient toast — it is a statement about what the user is looking at.
- Sub-minute intervals (1 s, 5 s, 15 s, 30 s) and custom intervals (e.g. `7m`) share one entry affordance; wireframe the validation message position for "Values below one tick / interval not allowed" style errors.

## Test plan
- Design walkthrough of each flow with the Owner and one QA/SDET, recorded in the ticket, checking that each branch has a designed destination (no dead ends).
- Cross-check every wireframed control against `15-component-catalogue.md`; any control with no CMP entry is listed as a new-component candidate for E12-D09.
- Cross-check every data element against `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 so nothing is drawn that no endpoint or topic can supply.
- Keyboard walkthrough on paper: every flow must be completable without a pointer, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Architect sign-off comment for engine feasibility.

## Security notes
- No secrets, keys or account identifiers appear in any wireframe; symbol and market data only.
- RBAC is reflected in the wireframes: the `Record this symbol` action on SCR-041/SCR-047 is owner-only, and the manager/viewer variant shows explanatory copy instead of a CTA, per the catalogue.
- No wireframe may imply that an order can be placed from the bar-mode surface; chart trading is armed separately and belongs to another epic.

## Accessibility notes
- Every flow is drawn with an explicit keyboard path, including opening SCR-042 (via the toolbar button and via the `1..9` interval hotkeys), moving between the bar-mode groups, and reaching the `param` field.
- The state matrix must record, per state, the screen-reader expression (accessible name text, polite live-region message, or a row in the SCR-045 data table alternative).
- Focus behaviour is specified for the rebuild flow: where focus goes when a rebuild starts, and that it is not stolen when the rebuild completes.
- Grouped menu semantics (`role="menu"` with groups) per CMP-220's contract are annotated on the wireframe.

## Performance notes
- Wireframes annotate the budgets they must respect: interval switch ≤200 ms from cache (`US-CHART-005`), first paint of an uncached interval ≤600 ms with progressive backfill (SCR-042), chart-type switch ≤100 ms client-side with no refetch (`US-CHART-002`), rebuild of 1 M prints ≤10 s and cancellable (`US-CHART-003`, `US-CHART-004`).
- The "no flash of empty chart" requirement is annotated as a designed behaviour: the previous frame remains visible until the first new data arrives.

## Observability
- Each flow annotates the analytics event it should emit: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed`, `chart.symbol_changed` with `{source}`, `chart.empty_state_shown` with `{reason}`, `chart.error_shown` with `{code, correlationId}`.
- F-BAR-3 annotates a rebuild start/complete/cancel event pair so rebuild duration is measurable against the 10 s budget in production.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Wireframe set and flow diagrams reviewed by the CDO, the Architect (feasibility) and a11y design lead; review comments resolved.
- Flow diagrams merged into `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`; the state matrix merged into the `SCR-030` entry of `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- New-component candidates listed and linked to E12-D09.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done.** E12-D03..E12-D08 may not leave Ready until this ticket is Done.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D01 (bar-mode vocabulary and state precedence).
- Informed by E06 (chart-engine spike & ADR) for what the renderer can actually do; informed by E11 (chart engine core) for the pane/axis chassis the wireframes assume stays mounted.
- Feeds E12-D03, E12-D04, E12-D05, E12-D06, E12-D07, E12-D08, E12-D09.

## Branch

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-042 interval & bar-mode menu with parameter entry
body:
## Context
`SCR-042` is the single control surface through which every bar type in the product is chosen. It carries the full time ladder (1 s, 5 s, 15 s, 30 s, 1 m, 3 m, 5 m, 15 m, 30 m, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 6 h, 12 h, 1 d, 1 w) **plus** Volume, Tick, Range, Renko and Point & Figure modes with inline parameter fields, **plus** the "edit favourites" row that defines the `1..9` hotkey ladder used from the chart. It is referenced by `US-CHART-002`, `US-CHART-004`, `US-CHART-005` and `US-FP-004`.

The catalogue already fixes the hard parts: bar modes must be a separately labelled group with a one-line description each (because they change the meaning of the x-axis), intervals unavailable for the symbol's recorded depth are greyed with "Needs recorded ticks", and the design sign-off checklist requires all bar modes drawn with their parameter inputs, favourites/pinned intervals, custom-interval validation messaging, and an explicit statement of which non-time modes require recorded tick history.

This ticket turns the E12-D02 wireframe into the signed-off hi-fi spec that the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories build against, at least two sprints ahead of them per the design-ahead rule in `00-planning-brief.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi Figma frames for `SCR-042` in both density modes (comfortable/compact per `16-design-system-brief.md`) and both themes: default (time ladder), bar-modes group expanded, each of the five non-time modes with its `param` field populated, favourites-editing mode, and the greyed "Needs recorded ticks" state.
- Per-mode specification table: user-facing label, one-line description, `param` field type, unit suffix, default value, min/max, and the validation message — units and semantics taken verbatim from the `/market/bars` `bar_type`/`param` table in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`time` interval string, `tick` trades/bar, `volume` base-asset volume/bar, `range` high-low in ticks, `delta` absolute signed volume, `renko` ticks or `atr:14`, `pnf` `box:reversal`).
- Custom-interval entry design (`US-CHART-005` scenario "Custom interval": entering `7m` aggregates from 1 m data and is added to the recent list) including the recent-intervals region and its overflow rule.
- Favourites editor design defining the `1..9` hotkey ladder, including how a slot is reassigned and how the assigned digit is displayed (`CMP-022 Kbd`).
- Validation and error specimens: value below one tick, Renko brick ≤ 0, range < 1 tick, volume below min lot, P&F reversal malformed — copy written for each, per `SCR-031`'s existing validation wording ("Values below one tick are not allowed.").
- Composition spec naming the reused components — `CMP-041 Menu`, `CMP-069 InfoPanel`, `CMP-220 IntervalPicker`, `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle`, `CMP-008 NumericStepperInput` — and any new variant handed to E12-D09.
- Redlines: spacing, type ramp, token names (no raw hex), focus rings, hit targets, and the popover anchoring/placement rules against the chart toolbar.

## Out of scope
- The quick-switcher overlay `SCR-041` (E12-D04) and the chart settings dialog `SCR-031` (E12-D05).
- The in-canvas rendering of the resulting series (E12-D06, E12-D07) and its failure states (E12-D08).
- Footprint bar-mode interactions beyond the shared `US-FP-004` reference (E18).
- Motion and transition specification (E12-D10).
- Implementation, Storybook stories and tokens code (engineering stories in Sprint 05–08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every bar mode is drawn with its parameter input
  Given the hi-fi frames are submitted for CDO review
  When they are checked against the SCR-042 design sign-off acceptance checklist
  Then time, tick, volume, range, Renko and Point & Figure are each drawn as a labelled group member with a one-line description
  And each non-time mode shows its param field with the correct unit suffix and default value

Scenario: Recorded-history dependency is visible before selection, not after
  Given a symbol whose recorder has only three days of prints
  When the bar-modes group is drawn for that symbol
  Then modes requiring tick history are greyed with the text "Needs recorded ticks"
  And the reason is available as text, not only as a reduced opacity

Scenario: Custom interval validation
  Given the custom-interval field is drawn
  When an invalid value such as 0m or 3x is entered
  Then the specimen shows an inline message naming the accepted format and the allowed range
  And the message is associated with the field for assistive technology, not rendered as a detached toast

Scenario: Renko ATR parameter is representable (edge)
  Given the Renko mode param accepts either a tick count or the string atr:14 per 22-api-openapi.yaml
  When the Renko row is drawn
  Then both entry forms are designed with a single control and a stated precedence, not two conflicting fields
  And the ATR form states its source interval

Scenario: Menu overflows at narrow chart widths (failure)
  Given a chart panel docked at its minimum width
  When SCR-042 is opened
  Then the frames show the menu scrolling or repositioning within the viewport with the selected item visible
  And no group is silently truncated, per the CMP-221 overflow rule
```

## Technical notes / design
- The menu must stay a **menu**, not a form disguised as one: mode selection commits on activation, while the `param` field commits on blur or Enter with the current value echoed in the menu-button accessible name ("Interval: volume 1 500").
- Group order follows the research recommendation from E12-D01 (expected: time first, then tick, volume, range, delta, Renko, P&F) and must match the group order used by `CMP-220 IntervalPicker` so the picker and the menu never disagree.
- The one-line descriptions are the product's only chance to explain a non-time x-axis; write them as consequences ("a new bar opens every 500 trades — the x-axis is no longer evenly spaced in time") rather than definitions.
- Favourites map to `1..9`; the spec must state what happens when fewer than nine favourites exist and when a favourite is a non-time mode with a parameter (the parameter travels with the slot).
- Anchor placement: the menu opens from the interval control in `CMP-221 ChartToolbar`; specify the flip/shift behaviour when the chart panel is near a screen edge or inside a floating Electron window (`SCR-027`).
- Use `CMP-069 InfoPanel` for the "which modes need recorded ticks" explanation rather than a tooltip, so the explanation is reachable by keyboard and persists while reading.

## Test plan
- Design review against every line of the `SCR-042` design sign-off acceptance checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md`; each box ticked with evidence.
- Token audit: every colour, space and type value resolves to a `16-design-system-brief.md` token; zero raw hex values in the delivered frames.
- Contrast audit of the greyed "Needs recorded ticks" state — disabled-looking items must still meet the contrast floor for text that conveys information.
- Copy review of all six descriptions and all five validation messages by the CDO and the Owner.
- A prototype click-through of F-BAR-2 and F-BAR-3 (from E12-D02) walked keyboard-only.
- Cross-check the per-mode spec table against `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` and the `barType` definition in `23-ws-protocol.md` §14; any mismatch is a blocking review comment.

## Security notes
- No account, key or balance data appears on this surface; it is market-data scoped only (`x-rbac: marketdata:read`).
- The "Record this symbol" affordance is **not** part of SCR-042; if the greyed state offers a route to recording, it must link to the owner-only surface and the spec must show the non-owner variant without the action.
- Parameter values are user input that reaches a backend query string; the design must bound them (min/max, max length 24 per the API's `param` schema) so the UI cannot originate an out-of-range request.

## Accessibility notes
- `role="menu"` with real group semantics; each non-time mode group is labelled and each item carries its description in the accessible name or via `aria-describedby`.
- The menu button's accessible name always states the current interval or mode plus parameter, per `CMP-220`'s contract, and is readable without opening the popover.
- Full keyboard operation: open, arrow between groups and items, type-ahead, reach and edit the `param` field, Esc restores the previous selection without changing the chart.
- Disabled items are still focusable and announce their reason ("Needs recorded ticks"), rather than being skipped silently.
- Hit targets and focus rings meet `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the `1..9` shortcuts are documented in `SCR-013` hotkey cheatsheet and shown with `CMP-022 Kbd`.

## Performance notes
- The spec states the budgets the built menu must honour: opening ≤80 ms from a cached instrument list (SCR-041's budget applies to the shared popover machinery), interval change reusing the cached series when present, otherwise ≤600 ms first paint with progressive backfill (SCR-042 Performance).
- The design must not require re-measuring or re-laying out the whole menu on each keystroke in the `param` field.

## Observability
- Emissions specified on the frames: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed` with `{from, to, param}` (analytics), plus the rebuild start event agreed in E12-D02 when a parameter change triggers a rebuild.
- No audit-log records are produced by this surface; the spec states that explicitly so engineering does not add one.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- All frames, the per-mode spec table and the redlines published in Figma and linked from the `SCR-042` entry of `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Every checklist item in the `SCR-042` design sign-off acceptance checklist ticked with evidence.
- a11y design lead review comment resolved; token audit clean.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, at least two sprints before the consuming frontend story starts (Sprint 05).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D02 (wireframes and flows).
- Depends on the design-system foundations from the E0x design-system epic for tokens, `CMP-041 Menu` and `CMP-008 NumericStepperInput`.
- Feeds E12-D04 (shared popover behaviour), E12-D09 (design-system contribution for CMP-220/CMP-222), E12-D12 (handoff) and the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories.

## Branch
`design/e12-scr042-bar-mode-menu` — Figma links, redline exports and the `14-screens-catalogue.md` update.

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-042 (and its design sign-off acceptance checklist), SCR-031, SCR-013, SCR-027
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` — US-CHART-002, US-CHART-004, US-CHART-005, US-FP-004
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-008, CMP-022, CMP-041, CMP-069, CMP-220, CMP-221, CMP-222
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6, §14
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/research/findings/E12-bar-modes.md`


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)

5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Branch & PR**

title: Hi-fi design: price series visual language (candle, bar, line, area, HA)
body:
## Context
This is the ticket that decides what CandleViewer's charts actually *look like*. `US-CHART-001` requires candlesticks that are "legible and smooth at any zoom"; `US-CHART-002` adds OHLC bars, line, area, Heikin-Ashi and a volume column sub-pane; `CMP-181 CandleSeries` additionally lists equi-volume and delta-volume; `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle` adds hollow candles and baseline. Every one of those is drawn by the WebGL renderer built in E12's engineering stories, which means the visual language must be expressed as **geometry rules and tokens**, not as a picture — the renderer cannot consult a Figma frame at runtime.

The constraints are unusually tight. `SCR-030` budgets ≥58 fps at 2560×1440 with 100 k bars; `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 defines LOD and decimation, which means at high bar counts a "candle" stops being a body-plus-wicks and becomes an aggregated mark — and `US-CHART-001` requires that the aggregation level be *indicated*. Body width, minimum wick width, the doji/zero-range case and the sub-pixel case are therefore product decisions with performance consequences, and they belong to design, made once, here.

This ticket also sets the **up/down encoding** rule. `05-accessibility-standard.md` forbids colour-only signalling, and green/red is exactly that; the spec must define the redundant channel (hollow vs filled body, or an outline-weight rule) that survives at every zoom level including LOD.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- A **series visual specification** document (markdown + Figma) covering, for each type in `CMP-181`/`CMP-222` — candle, hollow candle, OHLC bar, line, area, baseline, Heikin-Ashi, equi-volume, delta-volume: geometry rules (body width as a function of bar spacing, minimum width, wick/tick width, cap style), colour token mapping (`color.candle.up/down` per `CMP-180`/`CMP-181`), and the up/down redundant non-colour encoding.
- **Density ladder**: the rendering rules at bar spacings of ≥8 px, 4–8 px, 2–4 px, 1–2 px and <1 px (LOD-aggregated), including when bodies collapse to a single column, when wicks are dropped, and the exact appearance of an aggregated mark.
- The **LOD/aggregation indicator** design required by `US-CHART-001` ("the aggregation level is indicated") — persistent chart chrome stating what the user is looking at, with its text form.
- **Forming vs closed bar** treatment, expressing the `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 rule that the last bar may carry `confirm: false` and MUST NOT be treated as closed: a designed distinction that is not colour-only and not motion-only, plus its relationship to `CMP-226 BarCountdown`.
- **Gap rule**: a gap is drawn as a gap and never interpolated (`US-CHART-011` scenario "Misaligned history"); the visual treatment of a missing window inside an otherwise live series, and how it differs from the partial-history boundary designed in E12-D08.
- **Volume column sub-pane** design (`US-CHART-002`): linked sub-pane sharing the time axis and crosshair, its own scale treatment, and its up/down encoding consistent with the price series.
- **Non-time bar visual consequences**: how range, Renko, tick, volume and delta bars differ visually from time bars (uniform widths, no wall-clock spacing, brick geometry for Renko, column geometry for P&F) and what the time axis shows when spacing is not time-linear.
- Token contributions handed to E12-D09 for the design-system: any new `color.chart.*` / `color.candle.*` entries required.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cells (`CMP-109`, `CMP-182`) and profiles (E18/E19) — this covers the price series layer only.
- Indicator overlays (`CMP-194`, E13), drawings (`CMP-191`, E14), order/position overlays (`CMP-192`).
- Axis design (`CMP-188`, `CMP-189`) and crosshair/tooltip (`CMP-190`, `CMP-197`) — owned by the E11 chart-engine-core design; this ticket only states what the series contributes to them.
- The data-table alternative `SCR-045` (E12-D07).
- Motion (E12-D10) and the empty/error states (E12-D08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every supported chart type has an implementable geometry rule
  Given the series visual specification is submitted for review
  When an engineer reads it without access to Figma
  Then each of candle, hollow candle, OHLC bar, line, area, baseline, Heikin-Ashi, equi-volume and delta-volume has a stated geometry rule as a function of bar spacing and tokenised colours
  And no rule requires a value that is not a token or a computed quantity the renderer already has

Scenario: Up and down are distinguishable without colour
  Given the up/down encoding is reviewed against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  When the specification is rendered in greyscale
  Then direction remains readable at every step of the density ladder
  And the redundant channel is stated explicitly rather than left to the implementer

Scenario: Sub-pixel bars degrade to a designed mark (edge)
  Given 100 000 bars are zoomed to fit so bar spacing falls below one pixel
  When the density ladder is inspected
  Then it specifies an aggregated mark rather than overlapping candles
  And the aggregation indicator states the aggregation level in text

Scenario: A zero-range bar is still visible (edge)
  Given a bar whose open, high, low and close are identical
  When the geometry rules are applied
  Then the specification yields a visible mark of a stated minimum height
  And it is distinguishable from a rendering artefact

Scenario: A data gap is never interpolated (failure)
  Given a series is missing a window of bars
  When the gap rule is inspected
  Then the gap is drawn as a gap with a stated treatment
  And no line, area or baseline type bridges the missing range
```

## Technical notes / design
- Express every rule as **pixels derived from bar spacing**, e.g. "body width = clamp(round(spacing × 0.7), 1, 24) px; wick width = max(1, round(bodyWidth / 6)) px", so the renderer implements arithmetic rather than taste. Exact values are set in this ticket; the formula shape is fixed here.
- Align with `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 (LOD and decimation): the design must not require per-bar detail the decimation stage has already discarded. Confirm with the Architect which quantities survive decimation (typically open/high/low/close of the aggregate plus a count) and design the aggregated mark from exactly those.
- Heikin-Ashi is a client-side transform (`US-CHART-002`); its geometry is the candle geometry, but the spec must state that HA values are derived and therefore that crosshair readouts and drawings anchor to **real** time/price, matching the story's requirement that "drawings stay anchored to real time/price".
- Equi-volume and delta-volume vary **width** by volume/delta; state the width mapping, its clamp, and what happens when a single bar's volume dwarfs the window (cap plus an indicator rather than a bar that consumes the viewport).
- Renko bricks and P&F columns have no wall-clock spacing at all; specify the time-axis label strategy for those modes (labels at brick boundaries with their timestamps, spacing non-linear) so `CMP-189 TimeAxis` has a rule rather than an accident.
- The forming-bar treatment must survive on a 1 s interval where the "forming" state is nearly always true — it cannot be visually loud.
- Keep the token surface small: prefer reusing `color.candle.up/down`, `color.chart.grid`, `color.chart.background` over introducing new tokens; every proposed new token needs a justification in E12-D09.

## Test plan
- Render the specification against **real recorded fixtures** at each step of the density ladder and attach the images to the ticket; a rule that has not been seen against real data is not signed off.
- Greyscale and colour-vision-deficiency simulation (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) of every chart type at three densities.
- Contrast measurement of body/wick/background pairs in both themes against `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Architect review for renderability against `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.1, §3.6, §4 and the memory budgets in §7.
- Review with the Owner on the reference monitor at 2560×1440 — the target resolution named in `SCR-030` — not on a designer's laptop.
- Cross-check every type against `CMP-181` and `CMP-222` prop enums; a type in the design that no component prop can express is a blocking finding.

## Security notes
- No security-sensitive data is rendered by the series layer; the spec must not introduce any affordance that places or amends an order (chart trading is a separate, armed surface).
- The specification must not encode account-derived information (e.g. position side) into the series colouring, which would leak account state into a market-data view shared in screenshots.

## Accessibility notes
- Direction (up/down) must be conveyed by at least one non-colour channel at every density; the spec states it per type.
- `CMP-181`'s DOM-mirror contract applies: the focused bar surfaces OHLCV through the mirror node with arrow-key bar-to-bar movement and `Home`/`End` jumps. This ticket defines **what text** that mirror exposes per chart type (including what Heikin-Ashi exposes — the spec must state whether HA or real OHLC is announced, and why).
- The aggregation indicator is text, not an icon alone, and is included in the chart's rolling `aria-label` summary per `CMP-180`.
- Forming-bar state is expressed in the accessible name of the focused bar, not only visually.
- Reduced-motion users must lose no information: nothing in this spec may depend on animation.

## Performance notes
- The spec is bounded by `SCR-030`'s budget: ≥58 fps at 2560×1440 with 100 k bars, ≤450 MB per chart panel, and `US-CHART-001`'s ≥55 fps at 100 k bars with ≤512 MB GPU per pane.
- Any rule that would require per-bar text, per-bar alpha blending or an extra draw call per bar is flagged and justified, or replaced; the density ladder exists precisely to keep the draw-call count flat as bar count grows.
- The chosen geometry is handed to the E12 engineering stories together with a target: no rule may increase the vertex count per bar beyond the budget agreed with the Architect in review.

## Observability
- The aggregation level shown by the indicator is also a diagnostics value surfaced in `SCR-046` (chart engine diagnostics overlay: visible bars, cell count, fps); the spec names the field so the two never disagree.
- No analytics events originate from the series layer itself; stated explicitly so engineering does not instrument per-frame.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Series visual specification merged into the repo alongside the Figma links, and referenced from `CMP-181`/`CMP-222` in `15-component-catalogue.md` and from `SCR-030`.
- Density-ladder renders against real fixtures attached to the ticket.
- Architect renderability review and a11y design lead review both resolved.
- Token additions (if any) accepted by the design-system team via E12-D09.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, ≥2 sprints before the Sprint 05 rendering stories.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D01 (vocabulary, forming/closed and aggregation language).
- Depends on E06 (chart-engine spike) evidence and E11 (chart engine core) for the pane/scale chassis; the LOD stage in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 must be understood before the aggregated mark is designed.
- Feeds E12-D07, E12-D08, E12-D09, E12-D10, E12-D11, E12-D12 and all E12 rendering stories.

## Branch
`design/e12-series-visual-language`

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-041 symbol/interval quick-switcher & hotkey ladder
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-005` promises that "context and execution timeframes are one keystroke apart", and E12's epic scope in `30-release-roadmap.md` §5 includes "symbol + timeframe switching without a full engine teardown". `SCR-041` is the in-chart popover that delivers that: type-ahead symbol search with favourites, recents and an instrument metadata preview (tick size, lot size, max leverage, funding, 24 h volume), with interval shortcuts in the same overlay.

E12 changes this surface in two specific ways that need design: (1) the overlay must now also express **bar modes**, not just time intervals, because the chart it drives can be volume- or tick-based, and (2) the "not recorded" chip already specified in the catalogue becomes load-bearing — a symbol with no recorded tape cannot serve tick/volume/range/Renko bars at all, which is the `US-CHART-003` "Insufficient tick history" case observed at the moment of switching rather than after.

The catalogue's sign-off checklist for this screen requires: typeahead with fuzzy match, recent symbols, interval shortcuts in the same overlay, a not-recorded warning on symbols with no history, and a no-results state. This ticket delivers the hi-fi that satisfies it.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi Figma frames for `SCR-041`: idle/open, typing with fuzzy matches ranked, no-match state with the exact catalogue copy ("No USDT perpetual matches 'xyz' — v1 supports linear perpetuals only."), favourites and recents sections, instrument metadata preview, the not-recorded chip with its owner-only "Record this symbol" action, and the manager/viewer variant of that row without the action.
- Design of the **interval/bar-mode strip inside the overlay**: the `1..9` favourites ladder rendered with `CMP-022 Kbd`, consistent in order and labelling with `SCR-042` (E12-D03), including how a favourite that is a non-time mode displays its parameter.
- Switching behaviour spec: on symbol change the previous frame stays visible until first data ("no white flash", per SCR-041 Performance), the visible time-window centre is preserved on interval change per `US-CHART-005`, and the bar mode + parameter are carried across or reset — the rule stated explicitly, per mode.
- Cross-symbol bar-mode validity rule: what the overlay shows when the currently selected bar mode is unavailable for the newly chosen symbol (fall back to the nearest time interval with an explanatory message; the message drafted here).
- Composition spec naming `CMP-048 Combobox / AutoComplete`, `CMP-213 FuzzyList`, `CMP-219 SymbolPicker`, `CMP-220 IntervalPicker`, plus `CMP-022 Kbd`; new variants handed to E12-D09.
- Redlines: placement/anchoring from `CMP-221 ChartToolbar`, widths at comfortable and compact density, both themes, focus rings and hit targets.

## Out of scope
- Global symbol search `SCR-102` and the watchlist `SCR-100` (owned by the market-data/watchlist epic); this is the **in-chart** switcher only.
- Recording management screens (`SCR-140`, `SCR-141`) — the action links there but the destination is out of scope.
- The full bar-mode menu `SCR-042` (E12-D03) and the chart settings dialog `SCR-031` (E12-D05).
- Motion (E12-D10) and multi-chart symbol propagation (`SCR-049`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overlay satisfies its catalogue sign-off checklist
  Given the hi-fi frames are submitted for CDO review
  When they are checked against the SCR-041 design sign-off acceptance checklist
  Then typeahead with fuzzy match, recent symbols, interval shortcuts in the same overlay, the not-recorded warning and the no-results state are each drawn
  And the instrument metadata preview shows tick size, lot size, max leverage, funding and 24h volume

Scenario: Bar mode survives or resets explicitly on symbol change
  Given a chart is on a 1 500-contract volume bar mode
  When the user switches to a symbol with no recorded tape
  Then the frames show the overlay stating that the mode is unavailable for that symbol and naming the fallback time interval
  And the chart is never left showing bars built from data that does not exist

Scenario: No white flash on switch
  Given the switching behaviour spec is reviewed
  When a symbol change is walked through frame by frame
  Then the previous rendered frame remains visible until the first data of the new symbol arrives
  And any intermediate state is a labelled loading treatment over the retained frame, not a blank canvas

Scenario: Escape restores the previous value (edge)
  Given the overlay is open and a different symbol is highlighted but not committed
  When Escape is pressed
  Then the frames show the overlay closing with the original symbol intact and focus returned to the invoking control
  And no subscription change is implied

Scenario: No results for a non-linear-perpetual query (failure)
  Given the user types a spot or inverse symbol
  When the no-match state renders
  Then it uses the catalogue copy naming that v1 supports linear perpetuals only
  And it offers a route back rather than leaving an empty list
```

## Technical notes / design
- The overlay is a combobox (`aria-autocomplete="list"`) whose results are announced as a count; the interval strip inside it is a separate labelled group so arrow-key navigation does not cross from symbols into intervals by accident — specify the focus containment rule.
- Instrument metadata comes from `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}` and the list from `GET /api/v1/instruments?q=`; the recording chip comes from `GET /api/v1/recording/symbols` per `CMP-219`'s data contract. Do not design a field with no source.
- Ranking: favourites, then recents, then fuzzy matches; specify the tie-break and the maximum visible rows before scrolling, since the list is keyboard-traversed.
- The `1..9` ladder shown here is the **same** favourites set edited in `SCR-042`; there is one source of truth and the spec must say so, to prevent engineering building two lists.
- The not-recorded chip is the E12 trust hook: its copy must distinguish "live data will stream, history starts when you record" from "this mode cannot be built at all", matching the two cases drawn in `SCR-047` (E12-D08).

## Test plan
- Review against every line of the `SCR-041` design sign-off acceptance checklist.
- Keyboard-only click-through of flow F-BAR-1 (from E12-D02): open, type, select, change interval, Escape.
- Screen-reader script walkthrough with the a11y design lead: result counts, the recording state per option, the current value readable without opening the popover (per `CMP-219`).
- Token and contrast audit, both themes, both densities; the not-recorded chip verified as non-colour-only.
- Copy review of the no-match and mode-unavailable messages with the Owner.
- Consistency diff against the E12-D03 frames: group order, labels, parameter formatting and hotkey rendering must be identical.

## Security notes
- Market-data scope only (`marketdata:read`); no keys, balances or account identifiers on this surface.
- RBAC: the "Record this symbol" action is owner-only; the manager/viewer frame must show the explanatory sentence instead, and the spec must state that hiding the control is not sufficient on its own — the backend enforces it.
- Typed query text is sent to `GET /api/v1/instruments?q=`; the design bounds its length and states that results are rendered as text, never as markup.

## Accessibility notes
- Combobox semantics with `aria-autocomplete="list"`, results announced as a count, and the current symbol as the initial value with Escape restoring it (catalogue requirement).
- Each option announces symbol, base/quote and recording state, per `CMP-219`'s a11y contract.
- The interval/bar-mode group inside the overlay is separately labelled and its non-time entries carry their explanatory text, consistent with `CMP-220`.
- Focus returns to the invoking toolbar control on close; focus is never left on a detached node.
- Hotkeys `1..9` are documented in `SCR-013` and are not the only route to any interval.

## Performance notes
- Budget stated on the frames: overlay opens in ≤80 ms from the locally cached instrument list; symbol switch swaps subscriptions in a single WS frame and retains the previous frame until first data (SCR-041 Performance).
- Interval switch from cache ≤200 ms preserving the visible-window centre (`US-CHART-005` NFR).
- The design must not require a network round-trip to render the metadata preview for a symbol already in the cached list.

## Observability
- `chart.symbol_changed` with `{from, to, source: 'quick-switcher'}` (analytics), `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed` when the strip is used.
- The mode-unavailable fallback emits an event with the reason so how often users hit unrecorded symbols is measurable.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Frames, switching-behaviour spec and redlines published and linked from the `SCR-041` entry of `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Consistency diff against E12-D03 recorded as resolved.
- a11y design lead review comment resolved; token and contrast audits clean.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, ≥2 sprints before the consuming frontend story (Sprint 05+).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D02 (flows), E12-D03 (bar-mode labels, group order and parameter formatting that this overlay must mirror).
- Consumes `CMP-048`, `CMP-213`, `CMP-219`, `CMP-220` from the design-system epic.
- Feeds E12-D09, E12-D12 and the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories.

## Branch
`design/e12-scr041-quick-switcher`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-041 (and its sign-off checklist), SCR-013, SCR-047, SCR-049

- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` — `/instruments`, `/instruments/{symbol}`, `/recording/symbols`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §5 (sub/unsub), §6 (`bars.*`)

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-031 chart settings — bar mode, chart type & precision
body:
## Context
`SCR-031` is the tabbed chart settings modal (General · Scales · Appearance · Trading · Performance). Its wireframe in `14-screens-catalogue.md` already shows the E12-owned block on the **General** tab — chart type, bar mode with the interval/Volume/Tick/Range/Renko-brick fields, the bar-close countdown toggle, the 24/7 session note and precision — and its validation rules ("Renko brick > 0; range bars ≥ 1 tick; volume bars ≥ min lot; 'Values below one tick are not allowed.'").

SCR-042 (E12-D03) is the fast path used mid-analysis; SCR-031 is the deliberate path where a trader sets a chart up and where the *consequences* of a setting can be explained at length. The two must agree exactly on modes, units, defaults and validation, or the product will appear to have two different bar systems. The catalogue's sign-off checklist for this screen additionally requires a live preview against a real chart, reset-to-default per section and globally, and the "applies to this panel / all panels / as new default" scope control — all three interact with bar modes, because applying a volume bar mode to *all panels* may be impossible on symbols without recorded ticks.

This ticket delivers the hi-fi for the E12-owned portions of SCR-031 plus the chart-type surface required by `US-CHART-002` (candles, OHLC bars, line, area, Heikin-Ashi, hollow candles, baseline, equi-volume and delta-volume, per `CMP-181` and `CMP-222`).

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi Figma frames for the `SCR-031` **General** tab: chart type selector, bar mode selector with per-mode parameter fields, countdown toggle, session/day-boundary note, precision control; plus the shared modal chrome states (dirty, saving, reset confirmation).
- The **scope control** design ("applies to this panel / all panels / as new default") including the case where a chosen bar mode is invalid for some panels' symbols — the message and the partial-apply rule drafted here.
- **Live preview tile** design (`CMP-228 PreviewTile`) showing the selected chart type and bar mode against real data, including the textual description of what changed (required by the catalogue's a11y convention for preview tiles).
- Chart-type specification covering all `CMP-181` values (`candle`, `bar`, `line`, `equi-volume`, `delta-volume`) plus Heikin-Ashi, hollow candles, area and baseline from `CMP-222`/`US-CHART-002`: what each is, whether it is a client-side transform (Heikin-Ashi is, per `US-CHART-002` "applied client-side with no refetch") and which combinations are mutually exclusive.
- The **unsupported-combination** design required by `US-CHART-002`: requesting Heikin-Ashi together with footprint cells explains that footprint requires a real-price bar type and offers to switch back.
- Validation specimens for every field with copy: Renko brick > 0, range ≥ 1 tick, volume ≥ min lot, tick count ≥ 1, P&F `box:reversal` format, precision bounds.
- Reset-to-default design at section and global level, with confirmation (catalogue a11y note: "Reset requires confirmation").
- Composition spec: `CMP-006 RadioGroup`, `CMP-008 NumericStepperInput`, `CMP-031 ColorSwatch/ThemeChip`, `CMP-042 Tabs`, `CMP-043 Dialog`, `CMP-065 FormSection`, `CMP-069 InfoPanel`, `CMP-228 PreviewTile`; new variants handed to E12-D09.

## Out of scope
- The Scales, Appearance, Trading and Performance tabs, except where a bar-mode choice changes what they can offer (noted, not designed) — scales belong to the E11 chart-engine-core design work.
- Footprint settings `SCR-032` and profile settings `SCR-039` (E18/E19).
- The fast-path menu `SCR-042` (E12-D03) and the quick-switcher `SCR-041` (E12-D04).
- Chart templates (`US-CHART-012`, `SCR-035`) beyond noting that bar mode and parameter are template-persisted.
- Motion (E12-D10) and implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: General tab is complete and agrees with the fast path
  Given the hi-fi frames are submitted for CDO review
  When they are diffed against the E12-D03 SCR-042 frames
  Then the bar-mode set, their labels, units, defaults and validation messages are identical in both
  And any intentional difference is recorded with a reason in the ticket

Scenario: Live preview describes itself in text
  Given the preview tile is drawn for a Renko selection
  When it is reviewed for accessibility
  Then a textual description of the current selection accompanies the rendered sample
  And the preview is never the only way to understand what the setting does

Scenario: Applying a bar mode to all panels where some symbols lack ticks (edge)
  Given the scope control is set to "all panels"
  And one open panel shows a symbol with no recorded tape
  When the frames for that case are inspected
  Then the design states exactly which panels changed and which did not, naming the reason per panel
  And it does not silently skip panels or block the whole apply

Scenario: Heikin-Ashi with footprint is refused with an offer, not an error (failure)
  Given footprint cells are enabled on the panel
  When Heikin-Ashi is selected
  Then the frames show a message stating that footprint requires a real-price bar type and offering to switch back
  And the user is left in a valid state whichever option they take

Scenario: Reset is confirmed and scoped
  Given the user activates reset
  When the confirmation is drawn
  Then it names whether the reset applies to the section or the whole dialog and lists what will change
  And cancelling leaves every field untouched
```

## Technical notes / design
- Settings apply live where they are a uniform/shader change and are **labelled as requiring a refetch** where they are not (catalogue Performance note). A bar-mode or parameter change is a rebuild — the frames must mark those controls as rebuild-triggering so the user is never surprised by a progress bar.
- Heikin-Ashi is a client-side transform of the underlying time series (`US-CHART-002`); the spec must make clear it does **not** change `bar_type` on the wire — the `heikin_ashi` `bar_type` in `22-api-openapi.yaml` exists for server-side construction, and the design must state which path the dialog selects, to avoid engineering guessing.
- Precision defaults to the instrument's tick size (`GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`); the frames show the resolved value ("auto (tick 0.5)") as in the catalogue wireframe, with manual override bounded.
- Defaults come from `GET /api/v1/me/preferences` and persist into the panel config inside the workspace document; the "as new default" scope writes back to preferences — draw the distinction visibly, because it is the difference between changing one chart and changing every future chart.
- Day-boundary/session is referenced but owned by `US-CHART-009`; show the read-only note and link rather than duplicating the control.
- Every numeric field states its unit in the **label**, not in a placeholder (catalogue a11y requirement).

## Test plan
- Review against every line of the `SCR-031` design sign-off acceptance checklist.
- Field-by-field diff against E12-D03's per-mode spec table; mismatches are blocking.
- Cross-check chart-type list against `CMP-181`, `CMP-222` and `US-CHART-002`; any type in the design with no component support is filed to E12-D09.
- Keyboard-only walkthrough: tab order across `CMP-042 Tabs`, into each `CMP-065 FormSection`, to Reset/Cancel/Save, and through the confirmation dialog.
- Token, contrast and density audit in both themes.
- Copy review of all validation messages and the unsupported-combination message with the Owner and CDO.

## Security notes
- Chart settings are user-scoped preferences with no financial authority; the surface must not expose account, key or order data.
- Writing "as new default" mutates `me/preferences` — the design shows a clear, reversible confirmation so a misclick cannot silently reconfigure every future chart.
- Numeric inputs are bounded in the design so the client cannot originate out-of-range `param` values (API `param` maxLength 24); validation is presentational only and the spec states that the backend re-validates.

## Accessibility notes
- Tabs use `role="tablist"` semantics per the catalogue; panels are labelled by their tab.

- Reset requires confirmation and the confirmation states its scope in text.

- Focus is trapped within the modal, restored to the invoking control on close; Escape cancels without saving and the frames show the dirty-state guard.

- `chart.settings_changed` with `{section, key}` (analytics, no audit record — stated explicitly on the frames per the catalogue).
- `chart.bar_mode_changed` and the rebuild start/complete/cancel events when the change originates here, tagged with `{source: 'settings'}` so the fast path and the deliberate path are distinguishable.
