title: Hi-fi design: SCR-045 data-table alternative for every bar mode
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-014` and `SCR-045` establish that the chart's data-table view is the **normative accessible equivalent** of the canvas and "must reach feature parity for reading data" — an equal-status alternative, not a degraded fallback. E12 changes what that table has to represent: when the x-axis is trades, contracts, ticks or bricks rather than time, a table whose first column is "time" no longer describes the series.

This ticket designs the E12-owned portion of `SCR-045`: the column set per bar mode, how a non-time bar identifies itself (`open_time` and `close_time` are both meaningful for non-time bars per `22-api-openapi.yaml`, and the WS bars schema carries a `param`-derived field "Present for non-time bars"), how the forming bar and partial-history boundary appear as rows, and how the table stays in sync with the crosshair in both directions (`US-CHART-014` scenario "Sync").

Getting this right in E12 rather than retrofitting it is the difference between an accessible product and an accessibility ticket backlog; `05-accessibility-standard.md` treats this view as the compliance route for the entire charting surface.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi Figma frames for `SCR-045` in the E12 scope: default time-bar table, and one variant per non-time bar mode (tick, volume, range, delta, Renko, P&F) with the appropriate column set.
- **Column specification per bar mode**: which of open time, close time, duration, bar index, trades in bar, volume in bar, range in ticks, brick direction, OHLC, volume, delta and CVD are shown, in what order, with units in the header — mapped to the fields actually available from `GET /api/v1/market/bars` and the `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` topic.
- **Row states**: forming bar (the `confirm: false` case, which must be identifiable as not-final), closed bar, LOD-aggregated row when the canvas is aggregating (the table must state that a row represents N bars, not pretend to be per-bar), the partial-history boundary row, and the gap row.
- **Bidirectional crosshair sync** design: moving the crosshair moves the table's focused row and vice versa, including what happens when the crosshair is outside the loaded range.
- Column picker (`CMP-056`) and export design: `Ctrl+C` copies the selection as TSV and the export control is present in the header (`CMP-099 PrintExportBar`), per the catalogue interactions.
- Entry-point design: the view is reachable from the **chart panel header**, not hidden in settings (an explicit catalogue sign-off requirement), plus the `Alt+T` shortcut shown with `CMP-022 Kbd`.
- Empty/partial/error parity: what the table shows in each of the states E12-D08 designs for the canvas, so the two never disagree.
- Composition spec: `CMP-049 Table`, `CMP-053 Pagination`, `CMP-056 ColumnPicker`, `CMP-099 PrintExportBar`, `CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip`.

## Out of scope
- The expandable per-bar **footprint cell list** rows (`CMP-109`/`CMP-182`) — designed by E18; this ticket reserves the expansion affordance and states the contract.
- Indicator value columns (E13) beyond reserving the column slot.
- Alert creation, replay-from-here and note actions listed in the catalogue's row actions — owned by E40, E26 and E41 respectively; this ticket places them and defines nothing about their behaviour.
- The canvas rendering itself (E12-D06) and its failure states (E12-D08).
- Implementation and virtualisation engineering.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every bar mode has a defined column set
  Given the column specification is submitted for review
  When it is checked against the bar_type enum in 22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then time, tick, volume, range, delta, renko and pnf each have an ordered column set with units in the headers
  And every column maps to a field available from GET /api/v1/market/bars or the bars topic

Scenario: A non-time bar is identifiable without a time axis
  Given a tick-bar series at 500 trades per bar
  When a row is inspected
  Then it states the bar's open time, close time and the quantity that closed it
  And a reader can tell how long the bar took without consulting the canvas

Scenario: The forming bar is never mistaken for a closed one (edge)
  Given the last row represents a bar with confirm false
  When the row is rendered
  Then it is labelled as forming in text within the row, not only by styling
  And its accessible name states the same

Scenario: Aggregated rows are honest (edge)
  Given the canvas is LOD-aggregating 100 000 bars
  When the table is opened
  Then rows that represent multiple bars state how many, per the aggregation level shown on the canvas
  And the table never presents an aggregate as a single real bar

Scenario: Crosshair sync outside the loaded range (failure)
  Given the crosshair is moved to a time before the loaded window
  When the sync behaviour is inspected
  Then the table shows its first loaded row with a stated boundary indication rather than jumping to an arbitrary row
  And no sync loop is implied between the two surfaces
```

## Technical notes / design
- The table reads the **same in-memory series** as the canvas and issues no extra fetch (catalogue Performance note); the design must therefore never show a column the canvas's series does not carry.
- `open_time`/`close_time` both matter for non-time bars because they are "derived from its first/last trade" per the `/market/bars` description; the default column order for non-time modes leads with close time (the moment the bar became final) and shows duration as a derived column.
- The table must express the same `param` semantics as the rest of the epic: a tick-bar row's closing quantity is trades, a volume-bar row's is base-asset volume, a range-bar row's is ticks. Units live in the header, consistently with E12-D03's unit labels.
- Renko rows carry direction (up/down brick) as a **word**, not an arrow glyph alone; P&F rows carry column direction and box count.
- Sorting: the table is a time-ordered series, so arbitrary sorting is misleading. Specify whether sorting is offered at all and, if so, that reordering shows an explicit indicator that the rows are no longer in series order.
- Virtualisation is a design constraint as well as an engineering one: the design must not require sticky per-group headers or variable row heights that defeat windowing at 100 k rows.

## Test plan
- Review against every line of the `SCR-045` design sign-off acceptance checklist, especially the "equal status" and "reachable from the chart panel header" items.
- Screen-reader script walkthrough for each bar mode with the a11y design lead: grid navigation, row announcement, expansion, boundary rows.
- Keyboard-only walkthrough: `Alt+T` open, arrow navigation, `Enter` expand, `Ctrl+C` copy, export, close and focus restoration to the chart.
- Parity audit against E12-D06: every fact the canvas conveys visually is checked to have a textual home in the table; gaps are listed and either designed or explicitly deferred with a reason.
- Column-to-API audit against `22-api-openapi.yaml` and the `bars` schema in `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.3.
- Token, contrast and density audit at compact density, where the table is densest.

## Security notes
- The table exposes market data only; no account, position or key data is in scope for the E12 columns.
- Export/copy produces TSV of market data; the design states that exported content carries no account identifiers, so a shared export cannot leak account context.
- Row actions that reach other domains (create alert, replay from here) are placed but not enabled here; the design notes that each is RBAC-gated by its owning epic and must not appear to a `viewer` if that epic forbids it.

## Accessibility notes
- This is the normative accessible equivalent of `SCR-030`; every requirement in `05-accessibility-standard.md` for data tables applies, and the view is verified in every a11y test pass.
- Real table semantics with column headers associated to cells; the focused cell's row and column are announced.
- Forming, aggregated, gap and partial-history rows all state their condition in text within the row and in the row's accessible name.
- Bidirectional crosshair sync must not fight the screen reader: announcements are polite and throttled (`US-CHART-008` NFR caps announcements at ≤2/s).
- The entry point is a named control in the chart panel header plus the `Alt+T` shortcut documented in `SCR-013`; it is never the only route.
- Copy/export controls are real buttons with text names.

## Performance notes
- Budget from the catalogue: virtualised rendering of 100 k rows with ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame and no extra fetch; `US-CHART-014` requires the view to sustain ≥55 fps.
- The design avoids variable row heights and per-row measurement; expansion (reserved for footprint cells) is specified as a single expanded row at a time so windowing math stays simple.
- Crosshair-driven row focus must be coalesced rather than applied per mouse-move event; the design states the coalescing expectation so engineering implements it.

## Observability
- `chart.data_table_opened` and `chart.data_table_exported` (analytics), per the catalogue.
- A property recording the active `bar_type` on open, so adoption of the accessible view per bar mode is measurable.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Frames, per-mode column specification and redlines published and linked from the `SCR-045` entry of `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Parity audit against E12-D06 attached with every gap dispositioned.
- a11y design lead sign-off comment present (mandatory for this ticket, not advisory).
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, ≥2 sprints before the consuming frontend story (Sprint 05+).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D02 (flows and state matrix), E12-D06 (what the canvas conveys, which this view must match).
- Consumes `CMP-049`, `CMP-053`, `CMP-056`, `CMP-099` from the design-system epic.
- Reserves an extension point for E18 (footprint cell rows) and E13 (indicator columns).
- Feeds E12-D11 (a11y design review), E12-D12 (handoff) and the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories.

## Branch
`design/e12-scr045-data-table-bar-modes`

## References

title: Hi-fi design: rebuild, partial history, empty & error states (SCR-047/048)
body:
## Context
E12's most dangerous states are the ones where the chart is *not showing what the user assumes*. Three of them are unique to this epic:

1. **Partial history.** Non-time bars and sub-minute intervals are built from the recorded tape. `US-CHART-003` requires "an explicit partial-history marker" showing where tick data begins; `US-CHART-005` repeats it for sub-minute intervals. `22-api-openapi.yaml` is blunt about the backend contract: a window starting before `recording_started_at` returns `no_data_recorded` (422) "rather than silently substituting REST klines, because tick-accurate construction is impossible there".
2. **Rebuilding.** `US-CHART-004` requires that a brick/range size change "rebuilds from stored prints with a progress indicator" and its NFR requires the rebuild to be **cancellable**; `US-CHART-003` bounds it at ≤10 s per 1 M prints.
3. **Nothing to show.** `SCR-047` enumerates four causes (never recorded, interval too fine for available data, window entirely before recording start, exchange returned no bars) and `SCR-048` enumerates three failure classes (bootstrap failed, recompute failed, WebGL context lost with auto-retry ×3 then manual retry).

This ticket designs all of them as one coherent family, because they co-occur — a chart can be partially historic *and* rebuilding *and* then fail — and E12-D01 set the precedence order that decides what wins.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi Figma frames for `SCR-047` covering all four enumerated reasons, in both the owner variant (with the "Record this symbol" CTA to `SCR-140`) and the manager/viewer variant (explanatory copy, no CTA), including the "live data is streaming now" note where true.
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-048` covering the three failure classes with distinct copy: data-feed/bootstrap failure, footprint/bar recompute failure, and WebGL context loss ("Graphics context lost — restoring…", auto-retry ×3 then manual Retry with a link to `SCR-118` renderer settings), each with a copyable correlation id and the exponential-backoff next-attempt time (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, capped 30 s).
- **Partial-history marker** design on the `SCR-030` price area: the boundary where recorded ticks begin, its label, its behaviour when panned off-screen, and how it differs from a mid-series gap (designed in E12-D06).
- **Rebuild state** design: progress with a meaningful unit (prints processed or percent), elapsed/remaining expectation, an always-available **Cancel**, and the designed post-cancel outcome — the previous series and parameter restored, per E12-D02's F-BAR-3.
- **Precedence and co-occurrence matrix** realised visually: which indicator wins when partial-history, rebuilding, stale and LOD-aggregated are simultaneously true, and what the suppressed ones degrade to.
- The `no_data_recorded` (422) mapping: which API error maps to which `SCR-047` reason, written as a table so engineering does not invent the mapping.
- Composition spec: `CMP-001 Button`, `CMP-021 Link`, `CMP-026 EmptyState`, `CMP-027 ErrorState / InlineError`, `CMP-029 Skeleton-Chart placeholder`, `CMP-091 GlobalErrorBoundaryFallback`, `CMP-069 InfoPanel`.

## Out of scope
- Recorder configuration screens `SCR-140`/`SCR-141` (linked, not designed here).
- The stale/disconnected treatments for live data, which are the cross-cutting data-confidence vocabulary owned by E08's design work — this ticket **consumes** that vocabulary and must not redefine it.
- Footprint recompute progress specific to cell recomputation (E18) beyond sharing the rebuild pattern.
- The diagnostics overlay `SCR-046` (owned by the observability/settings design work).
- Motion specification (E12-D10).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every enumerated empty reason is drawn
  Given the SCR-047 frames are submitted for CDO review
  When they are checked against the screens catalogue
  Then never recorded, interval too fine, window entirely before recording start and exchange returned no bars are each drawn with distinct copy
  And the owner CTA variant and the manager or viewer explanatory variant both exist

Scenario: A rebuild can always be abandoned
  Given a Renko brick size change has started a rebuild over one million prints
  When the rebuild frames are inspected
  Then a Cancel control is present and reachable throughout
  And the designed post-cancel state restores the previous series and the previous parameter value with an explanation

Scenario: Partial history is stated as a boundary, not implied by absence
  Given the recorder holds three days of prints and the user requests thirty
  When the partial-history frames are inspected
  Then a labelled boundary marks where recorded ticks begin, with the timestamp as text
  And the chart does not simply start at that point with no explanation

Scenario: Two states co-occur (edge)
  Given a series is both partially historic and currently rebuilding
  When the precedence matrix is applied
  Then exactly one primary indicator is shown, per the order set in E12-D01
  And the suppressed state remains discoverable in text rather than disappearing

Scenario: WebGL context is lost and does not come back (failure)
  Given the graphics context is lost and three automatic retries have failed
  When the SCR-048 frames are inspected
  Then the design shows a manual Retry, a copyable correlation id and a link to the renderer settings in SCR-118
  And the rest of the workspace is shown as remaining usable
```

## Technical notes / design
- There is a hard product rule behind these screens: the product **never substitutes approximate data for missing tick data** on non-time bars. Every empty/partial state must read as a statement of fact, not an apology, and must never offer an "approximate it anyway" path for bar construction.
- Map errors explicitly: `no_data_recorded` (422) → the "window entirely before recording start" variant of `SCR-047`; an empty successful response → "exchange returned no bars"; transport/5xx → `SCR-048` data-feed failure; renderer context loss → `SCR-048` WebGL variant. Deliver this as a table.
- Progress must be honest about what it can know. If the backend can report prints processed, show a determinate bar; if it cannot, show an indeterminate state with elapsed time and never a fake percentage. Specify both and state which applies when.
- The partial-history boundary lives in the price area and must survive pan/zoom; when it scrolls off-screen, an edge indicator states that history begins off-view (the same pattern `US-CHART-013` uses for off-screen orders).
- `SCR-047` renders **without initialising the GL context for the data layer** (catalogue Performance note), so the empty state must be designed as DOM, not as a canvas drawing.
- Retry copy states the next attempt time; a spinner with no stated next attempt is explicitly forbidden by the catalogue's "no infinite spinner path" checklist item.
- Reuse the E08 data-confidence vocabulary verbatim for stale/reconnecting; if E12 needs a state that vocabulary lacks, raise it against E08's design rather than inventing a synonym here.

## Test plan
- Review against every line of the `SCR-047` and `SCR-048` design sign-off acceptance checklists.
- Walk flow F-BAR-5 and the cancel branch of F-BAR-3 (from E12-D02) end to end; verify no branch ends without a designed destination.
- Error-mapping table reviewed by the Architect and an ingestion engineer against `22-api-openapi.yaml` error responses; any unmapped error is a blocking finding.
- Copy review with the Owner for all seven state copies plus the retry and cancel messages.
- Screen-reader walkthrough of each state with the a11y design lead, including the announcement on transition from rebuilding to ready.
- Contrast and greyscale audit; verify no state is distinguishable by colour alone.

## Security notes
- Correlation ids are shown as selectable text for bug reports; the design states they must not contain account identifiers, symbols-as-secrets or session tokens.
- Error copy must not leak internal details (stack traces, hostnames, SQL, upstream URLs); the frames show user-facing language with the diagnostic detail behind the correlation id only.
- The owner-only "Record this symbol" CTA is RBAC-gated; the spec states that hiding it client-side is presentational and the backend enforces the permission.
- Backend failures are recorded in the incident log (`SCR-144`); the design must not surface that log's contents to non-owner roles.

## Accessibility notes
- `SCR-048` uses a `role="alert"` region with plain-language text, a focusable retry that is not colour-only, and a selectable correlation id (catalogue requirement).
- `SCR-047` is a heading plus paragraph plus action — never an icon alone; the recording-start timestamp is text.
- Rebuild progress is announced politely on start and on completion, and **not** continuously; the cancel control is keyboard-reachable at all times and focus is not stolen when the rebuild finishes.
- The partial-history boundary has a textual expression in the `SCR-045` data table (designed in E12-D07) and in the chart's rolling `aria-label` summary.
- Every state must be understandable with reduced motion enabled, so progress cannot be conveyed by animation alone.

## Performance notes
- `SCR-047` must not initialise the data-layer GL context, so an empty chart costs no GPU budget.
- Retry uses exponential backoff with the next attempt shown, and failures never spin the render loop (catalogue Performance note).
- Rebuild progress updates are coalesced (≤4 Hz) so the progress UI cannot itself compete with the rebuild for frame budget; the design states the cadence.
- The bounding budget for the rebuild itself is the `US-CHART-003` NFR of ≤10 s per 1 M prints; the design states what is shown if that budget is exceeded rather than assuming it never is.

## Observability
- `chart.empty_state_shown` with `{reason: 'not_recorded'|'no_data_in_range'|'symbol_delisted'}` and `chart.error_shown` with `{code, correlationId}` (analytics), per the catalogue; backend-side failures also land in the incident log (`SCR-144`).
- Rebuild start/complete/cancel events with duration and print count, so the 10 s budget is measurable in production rather than only in benchmarks.
- WebGL context-loss events counted, since recurrence is a browser/GPU-compatibility signal (risk R8) rather than a one-off.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Frames, precedence matrix and error-mapping table published and linked from the `SCR-047`, `SCR-048` and `SCR-030` entries of `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Architect and ingestion review of the error mapping resolved; a11y design lead review resolved.
- Confirmation recorded that the stale/reconnecting vocabulary is consumed from E08's design unchanged.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, ≥2 sprints before the consuming frontend story (Sprint 05+).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D01 (state precedence), E12-D02 (flows and state matrix), E12-D06 (canvas visual language the markers sit on).
- Consumes the data-confidence vocabulary from the E08 design work; consumes `CMP-026`, `CMP-027`, `CMP-029`, `CMP-091` from the design-system epic.
- Feeds E12-D07 (table parity), E12-D10 (motion for progress), E12-D11, E12-D12 and the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories.

title: Design-system: bar-mode & series components (CMP-181, 220, 222, 226)
body:
## Context
E12 touches four catalogued components that other epics will keep using long after R1: `CMP-181 CandleSeries` (the price series primitive, whose `chartType` and `barMode` prop enums are exactly E12's subject), `CMP-220 IntervalPicker` (time ladder plus bar modes), `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle` (candles, bars, line, area, Heikin-Ashi, hollow candles, baseline plus the footprint toggle) and `CMP-226 BarCountdown` (which is meaningless on non-time bars and therefore needs a designed behaviour rather than an accident).

`15-component-catalogue.md` §7A's own rationale is that trading-specific and chart-engine components get the same first-class treatment as generic atoms, "per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §11.3" — so E12's contributions must land **in the design system**, with Storybook states, a11y contracts and tokens, not as one-off decisions inside a chart screen. Without this ticket, E18 (footprint), E19 (profiles), E23 (CVD) and E26 (replay) each re-derive bar-mode labelling and forming-bar semantics from scratch.

This ticket consolidates everything E12-D03..E12-D08 decided into design-system entries and hands them to the design-system team, at least two sprints before the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories consume them.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Updated component entries in `15-component-catalogue.md` for:
  - `CMP-181 CandleSeries` — the full `chartType`/`barMode` enum agreed in E12-D06, the geometry-rule reference, the density ladder, the forming-bar and aggregated-mark states, and the DOM-mirror text contract per bar mode.
  - `CMP-220 IntervalPicker` — the grouped time/tick/volume/range/delta/Renko/P&F structure, the inline `param` field with per-mode unit, the "Needs recorded ticks" disabled-but-focusable state, favourites and the `1..9` ladder.
  - `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle` — every type from E12-D05's chart-type specification, plus the mutually-exclusive combination rule with the footprint toggle.
  - `CMP-226 BarCountdown` — the designed behaviour on non-time bars (it has no meaningful countdown; the spec defines what replaces it, e.g. progress toward the bar's closing quantity, or hidden with the reason available in text).
- New variants/entries where E12-D03..E12-D08 introduced something the catalogue lacks: the **LOD/aggregation indicator**, the **partial-history boundary marker**, and the **rebuild progress + cancel** pattern — each proposed as a catalogue entry (tier, purpose, props, a11y, tokens, Storybook states, tests) rather than a screen-local detail.
- **Token contributions**: any additions to `color.candle.*`, `color.chart.*` or status tokens required by E12-D06/E12-D08, each with a justification, a contrast measurement in both themes, and a rejected-alternatives note; submitted to the design-system team for acceptance into `16-design-system-brief.md`.
- **Storybook state list** per touched component, so the frontend stories build the exact states the design system will visual-test (e.g. `CMP-181`: Candle, HollowCandle, Bar, Line, Area, Baseline, HeikinAshi, EquiVolume, DeltaVolume, RenkoMode, FormingBar, LodAggregated, WithGap, PartialHistoryBoundary).
- A **consistency contract**: a single table asserting that the bar-mode label, description, unit and default value are identical across `CMP-220`, `SCR-042`, `SCR-041`, `SCR-031` and `SCR-045`, to be enforced by the catalogue-level test pattern already used for `CMP-227 EstimatedBadge`.

## Out of scope
- Footprint components (`CMP-109`, `CMP-182`), profile panes (`CMP-183`, `CMP-184`), CVD (`CMP-185`) — other epics own their catalogue entries.
- Axes (`CMP-188`, `CMP-189`), crosshair (`CMP-190`) and tooltip (`CMP-197`) except for the single note each needs about non-time spacing, which is contributed here as an amendment rather than a redesign.
- Implementing the components in code (frontend stories) and writing the Storybook stories themselves.
- Motion tokens (E12-D10) and the a11y review pass (E12-D11).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E12 design decision has a catalogue home
  Given the contribution is submitted to the design-system team
  When it is reviewed against the E12-D03 to E12-D08 outputs
  Then each decision appears either as an updated entry for CMP-181, CMP-220, CMP-222 or CMP-226, or as a proposed new catalogue entry
  And no E12 decision remains documented only inside a screen frame

Scenario: The consistency contract holds
  Given the consistency table is reviewed
  When the bar-mode labels, descriptions, units and defaults are compared across CMP-220, SCR-031, SCR-041, SCR-042 and SCR-045
  Then all five agree exactly
  And any divergence is resolved before sign-off rather than recorded as known

Scenario: A new token is justified or refused (edge)
  Given a proposed new colour token duplicates an existing one within the contrast tolerance
  When the design-system team reviews it
  Then the token is refused and the existing token is used
  And the refusal and its reason are recorded in the ticket

Scenario: Countdown on a non-time bar is defined (edge)
  Given a chart is in volume-bar mode
  When CMP-226 BarCountdown behaviour is inspected
  Then the entry defines exactly what the component shows or that it is not rendered, with the reason available as text elsewhere
  And it never shows a countdown that cannot be computed

Scenario: The design system refuses a component (failure)
  Given the rebuild progress pattern is judged to be a screen-local composition rather than a component
  When the design-system team rejects the proposed entry
  Then the pattern is instead documented as a named pattern with the same a11y and token rigour
  And the E12 screens referencing it are updated to point at the pattern
```

## Technical notes / design
- Props in the catalogue must stay implementable against the real data: `CMP-181`'s `barMode` enum must match the `bar_type` enum in `22-api-openapi.yaml` and the `barType` definition in `23-ws-protocol.md` §14, or one of the three has to change — surface that as a blocking review item rather than letting the catalogue drift.
- Prefer **amending existing entries over creating new ones**; the catalogue is already at 238 entries and its own rationale warns against both silent overloading and gratuitous expansion. Every proposed new entry must state why it is not a variant.
- The consistency contract is enforceable: follow the `CMP-227 EstimatedBadge` precedent of a catalogue-level test, so a future epic that adds a bar mode in one place and not the others fails CI rather than shipping an inconsistency.
- Token proposals must include measured contrast in both themes and the greyscale/CVD check from E12-D06; a token that only works in dark mode is not accepted.
- Where E12 needs a note on a component it does not own (`CMP-189 TimeAxis` under non-linear spacing), deliver it as a one-paragraph amendment with the owning team's acknowledgement recorded, not as an edit made unilaterally.

## Test plan

- Enum diff: `CMP-181.barMode` vs `/market/bars` `bar_type` vs `23-ws-protocol.md` `barType` — three-way, must be identical.
- Consistency table verified by manually walking `SCR-031`, `SCR-041`, `SCR-042`, `SCR-045` frames.
- Contrast measurements attached for every proposed token, both themes, plus CVD simulation.
- A11y contract review with the a11y design lead for each touched entry (the catalogue requires an a11y line per component).
- Confirm each entry lists Storybook states and test types, matching the catalogue's established format.

## Security notes
- No component in this contribution handles secrets, keys or order authority; the entries must state that explicitly where a reader might assume otherwise (e.g. `CMP-181` renders market data only and must not encode account state).
- The "Needs recorded ticks" state exposes whether a symbol is recorded; that is owner-scoped operational information, so the entry states that the state is rendered from `GET /api/v1/recording/symbols` which is itself RBAC-gated, and that no additional recording metadata is leaked to `viewer`.

## Accessibility notes
- Each touched entry must carry a complete a11y contract: `CMP-220`'s grouped menu semantics and disabled-but-announced items; `CMP-222`'s requirement that each option names the chart type in text (icons alone insufficient) and that footprint is a separate `aria-pressed` toggle; `CMP-226`'s `aria-live="off"` default so the countdown does not flood a screen reader; `CMP-181`'s windowed DOM mirror with `Home`/`End` and arrow-key bar navigation.
- New entries must specify their accessible name, keyboard operation and screen-reader announcement before they can be accepted.
- The aggregation indicator and partial-history marker must both be text-bearing; neither may be accepted as icon-only.

## Performance notes
- Entries carry the performance expectations already attached to them: `CMP-181` is tested at 100 k+ bars against a ≥58 fps budget; the aggregation indicator and partial-history marker are chrome and must cost nothing per frame (updated on range change, not per tick).
- The rebuild-progress pattern states its ≤4 Hz update cadence so that a future consumer does not implement it as a per-frame update.

## Observability
- No component emits analytics directly; events are emitted by the screens that compose them. The contribution states this rule so instrumentation stays at screen level and is not duplicated per component.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- `15-component-catalogue.md` updated for `CMP-181`, `CMP-220`, `CMP-222`, `CMP-226` and any accepted new entries; `16-design-system-brief.md` updated with accepted tokens.
- Three-way enum diff recorded as clean (or the resulting change tickets raised against the API/WS docs).
- Consistency contract table merged and a catalogue-level test proposed to QA for implementation.
- Design-system team acceptance recorded, a11y design lead review resolved.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, ≥2 sprints before the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories consume the components.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D03, E12-D04, E12-D05, E12-D06 (the decisions being consolidated).
- Depends on the design-system epic for the token pipeline and Storybook conventions.
- Feeds E12-D10, E12-D11, E12-D12 and every E12 frontend story; unblocks E18/E19/E23 from re-deriving bar-mode semantics.

title: Motion spec: bar-mode transitions, forming bar, rebuild progress, LOD change
body:
## Context
Motion on a trading chart is not decoration — it is either information or it is frame budget spent for nothing. E12 introduces four moments where something changes under the user and where the absence of a designed transition causes a real misread: switching interval or bar mode (the whole series is replaced), a bar closing (the forming bar becomes final and a new one opens), a rebuild running and completing, and an LOD threshold being crossed as the user zooms (the marks change meaning).

The constraints are explicit. `US-CHART-006` requires pan/zoom inertia that "respects reduced-motion settings". `US-CHART-005` requires "no flash of empty chart" on switch. `SCR-030` budgets ≥58 fps with 100 k bars and footprint on, so any transition competes directly with the render loop. `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.2 defines the render loop that every animation must live inside, and §5 the visual/theming rules.

This ticket produces a short, strict motion specification for those four moments, expressed in tokens from `16-design-system-brief.md`, with a reduced-motion equivalent for each.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Motion specification covering: **(a)** interval/bar-mode switch (crossfade vs instant swap, with the previous frame retained until first data per `SCR-041`/`US-CHART-005`); **(b)** bar close — the forming bar becoming confirmed and a new bar opening, on intervals as short as 1 s; **(c)** rebuild progress start/complete and the cancel/revert transition designed in E12-D08; **(d)** LOD threshold crossing during zoom, so the change in mark meaning is legible rather than a pop.
- Per moment: duration, easing, the property animated, the token names used, and the **reduced-motion equivalent** (which must preserve all information, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`).
- A **budget statement** per moment: the maximum per-frame cost the transition may add, and the rule that transitions are dropped (not queued) when the frame budget is already exceeded.
- Pan/zoom inertia parameters for `US-CHART-006` insofar as they interact with LOD transitions, coordinated with the E11 chart-engine-core design rather than redefined here.
- Prototype clips (or recorded screen captures against real fixtures) of each moment at 1 s, 1 m and volume-bar modes, attached to the ticket as the evidence for sign-off.
- Motion tokens proposed to the design-system team via E12-D09 if any duration/easing is not already tokenised.

## Out of scope
- Motion for footprint cells, profiles, DOM and heatmap (E18/E19/E20-series epics).
- Modal/popover open-close motion, which is design-system-owned and merely referenced here.
- Drawing-tool manipulation feedback (E14) and order-line drag feedback.
- Replay playback motion (E26).
- Implementation and any shader work.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Each moment has a spec and a reduced-motion equivalent
  Given the motion specification is submitted for review
  When it is checked against the four moments in scope
  Then each has a duration, easing, animated property and token names
  And each has a reduced-motion equivalent that conveys the same information without animation

Scenario: No transition conveys information on its own
  Given the reduced-motion variants are applied
  When a reviewer with animation disabled walks each moment
  Then bar close, rebuild completion and LOD change remain detectable through text or static visual state
  And nothing is discoverable only by having seen the animation

Scenario: Transitions are dropped under load (edge)
  Given the chart is already at its frame budget with 100 000 bars loaded
  When a bar-mode switch occurs
  Then the specification requires the transition to be skipped rather than queued or degraded to a stutter
  And the end state is identical whether or not the transition played

Scenario: One-second bars do not animate continuously (edge)
  Given a one-second interval where a bar closes every second
  When the bar-close motion is applied
  Then the specification either suppresses the transition below a stated interval threshold or bounds it so it cannot overlap the next close
  And the threshold is stated numerically

Scenario: A proposed transition exceeds its budget (failure)
  Given a crossfade of the full series is measured to cost more than its stated per-frame budget
  When it is reviewed with the Architect
  Then it is replaced with an instant swap that retains the previous frame until first data
  And the rejected variant and its measurement are recorded in the ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Default to **less**: on a chart that updates every frame, the strongest motion design is usually no motion. Every proposed transition must justify itself as information the static design cannot carry.
- Animations live inside the render loop described in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.2; they are driven by the loop's clock, never by CSS transitions on canvas content, and must be interruptible mid-flight when the user pans, zooms or switches again.
- The "no flash of empty chart" requirement is satisfied by **retaining the last rendered frame**, which is a state rule rather than an animation; the spec must say so explicitly so engineering does not implement a fade from blank.
- LOD crossings should be designed to be as invisible as possible in geometry and as explicit as possible in the indicator: the marks may change silently, but the aggregation indicator text changes and that change is the signal.
- Coordinate durations with the interaction budgets: a transition may not push an interval switch past the ≤200 ms cached budget (`US-CHART-005`) or a chart-type switch past ≤100 ms (`US-CHART-002`). If the budget leaves no room, the answer is no transition.
- Reduced motion is read from the OS/user preference and from the accessibility settings surface (`SCR-117`); the spec states that both are honoured and which wins.

## Test plan
- Record each moment against real recorded fixtures at 1 s, 1 m and a volume-bar mode; attach clips to the ticket.
- Measure the per-frame cost of each prototype transition with the Architect, on the reference machine at 2560×1440 with 100 k bars — a transition that has not been measured is not signed off.
- Reduced-motion pass: walk every moment with animation disabled and confirm no information loss.
- Vestibular-safety review against `05-accessibility-standard.md` — no large-area parallax, no rapid flashing, nothing exceeding the flash thresholds.
- Review with the Owner on the reference monitor; subjective "does this help or distract" recorded per moment with a keep/drop decision.

## Security notes
- Motion carries no data and no authority; the spec states that no transition may be used to indicate order or position state, which would place account information in a market-data view.
- No transition may delay or obscure a safety-relevant message (an error, a stale-data indicator, or a rebuild failure); those appear immediately regardless of motion settings.

## Accessibility notes
- Every transition has a reduced-motion equivalent that preserves information; this is a hard gate, not a best-effort item.
- No flashing that could trigger photosensitive responses; measured against the standard's thresholds.
- Transitions must not move focus, and must not cause a screen-reader announcement per animation frame.
- Bar-close motion must not be the only indication that a bar closed — the accessible name of the focused bar and the `SCR-045` table row carry it in text (E12-D06, E12-D07).
- Interval/mode switches must announce the new mode once, politely, rather than announcing during the transition.

## Performance notes
- Hard budget: the chart must hold ≥58 fps at 2560×1440 with 100 k bars (`SCR-030`); transitions are the first thing sacrificed when that is at risk, and the spec states the drop rule rather than leaving it to runtime luck.
- Each transition carries a stated maximum added per-frame cost, measured, not estimated.
- Rebuild progress animates at ≤4 Hz per E12-D08, not per frame.

## Observability
- No analytics are emitted by motion. The spec notes that dropped-transition counts, if instrumented at all, belong in the engine diagnostics overlay (`SCR-046`: dropped frames) rather than in product analytics.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Motion specification published, linked from `16-design-system-brief.md` (motion section) and from the `SCR-030` entry; any new motion tokens routed through E12-D09.
- Measured per-frame costs attached for every retained transition; rejected variants recorded with their measurements.
- Reduced-motion equivalents reviewed and approved by the a11y design lead.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, ≥2 sprints before the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D06 (series visual language and the LOD ladder), E12-D08 (rebuild and state transitions).
- Coordinates with the E11 chart-engine-core design for pan/zoom inertia; consumes motion tokens from the design-system epic.
- Feeds E12-D11, E12-D12 and the E12 frontend stories.

## Branch
`design/e12-motion-spec`

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` — US-CHART-001, US-CHART-002, US-CHART-005, US-CHART-006
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-030, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-046, SCR-117

title: Accessibility design review & screen-reader script for the bar/series band
body:
## Context
A WebGL canvas is, to assistive technology, an empty box. Everything E12 renders is therefore accessible only through deliberate constructions: the DOM mirror described in `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1–§6.2 and implemented by `CMP-180 ChartRoot`/`CMP-181 CandleSeries`, the rolling `aria-label` summary, the keyboard-driven crosshair, and the `SCR-045` data-table alternative that `US-CHART-014` declares to be an *equal-status* view.

Seven E12 design tickets have each made local a11y decisions. This ticket is the pass that checks them **as a set**, before any of them is built: it verifies that the vocabulary is consistent, that no state is announced twice or not at all, that the keyboard path across the whole band is unbroken, and it produces the **screen-reader script** — the normative, scenario-by-scenario expectation of what a user hears — that QA will later test against in E12's QA tickets and that engineering will implement against.

Without this ticket, a11y is verified per screen after the fact; with it, the band has one specification and one test oracle.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- A **design-level a11y review** of E12-D03..E12-D08 producing a findings list with severities, each finding either fixed in the originating ticket before its sign-off or explicitly accepted with a reason recorded.
- The **screen-reader script**: for each scenario below, the expected announcement sequence, verbatim, with the mechanism (accessible name, `aria-describedby`, polite live region, or table cell) —
  - focusing the chart and hearing the rolling summary (`CMP-180`);
  - arrowing bar to bar and hearing OHLCV, including on Heikin-Ashi (where the script must state whether HA or real OHLC is read) and on each non-time mode;
  - `Home`/`End` jumps to range start/end;
  - opening `SCR-042` and moving across bar-mode groups, hearing each mode's one-line description and each disabled item's "Needs recorded ticks" reason;
  - entering a parameter and hearing its unit and validation error;
  - switching mode and hearing the single, polite confirmation;
  - a bar closing (forming → confirmed) without flooding;
  - a rebuild starting, progressing (not announced continuously), completing or being cancelled;
  - crossing an LOD threshold and hearing the new aggregation level;
  - reaching the partial-history boundary and the gap;
  - `Alt+T` into `SCR-045`, navigating rows, and returning focus to the chart;
  - `SCR-047` empty and `SCR-048` error, including the correlation id being selectable.
- A **keyboard map** for the band: every operation reachable without a pointer, with its key, its scope (global / chart / menu), and confirmation that nothing is hover-only (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 forbids hover-only functionality).
- An **announcement budget**: which events are announced, at what rate, and the throttling rule (`US-CHART-008` caps live-region announcements at ≤2/s; `CMP-226 BarCountdown` defaults to `aria-live="off"`).
- Contrast and non-colour-encoding audit results for every state introduced by E12, in both themes and under CVD simulation.
- The script handed to QA as the basis for the manual screen-reader pass required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, and to engineering as the implementation target via E12-D12.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell announcements (E18), profile/TPO panes (E19), indicator values (E13) — the script reserves their slots and states the contract, no more.
- Automated axe-core rule configuration and CI wiring (engineering/QA tickets).
- Remediation of components owned by other epics (findings are filed to them).
- Testing the built product — that is E12-D13's design QA pass and the E12 QA tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The whole band is operable by keyboard
  Given the keyboard map is complete
  When every E12 operation is listed
  Then each has a keyboard route with a stated key and scope
  And no operation exists that is reachable only by hovering or only by pointer

Scenario: The script is specific enough to test against
  Given a QA engineer reads the screen-reader script without access to the designs
  When they run a scenario
  Then they can determine pass or fail from the script alone, because the expected announcement is written verbatim
  And the mechanism producing each announcement is named

Scenario: Announcements are bounded (edge)
  Given a one-second interval where a bar closes every second and the crosshair is moving
  When the announcement budget is applied
  Then the combined announcement rate stays at or below two per second
  And the script states which announcement is dropped when they collide

Scenario: Heikin-Ashi ambiguity is resolved (edge)
  Given Heikin-Ashi is a derived transform of the real series
  When the bar-navigation script is inspected
  Then it states unambiguously whether the announced OHLC values are the Heikin-Ashi values or the real values, and how the other is reachable
  And the same rule is reflected in the SCR-045 table columns

Scenario: A finding cannot be fixed before sign-off (failure)
  Given a review finding requires a change that the design cannot absorb in this sprint
  When it is triaged
  Then it is recorded as an accepted risk with a named owner and a follow-up ticket
  And it is not silently closed, nor does it block sign-off without the CDO recording the decision
```

## Technical notes / design
- The DOM mirror is **windowed to the visible range** (`CMP-181`, standard §6.2); the script must therefore state what happens at the window edges — arrowing past the last mirrored bar must extend the window or announce the boundary, not fall silent.
- Two surfaces can announce the same fact (the canvas mirror and the `SCR-045` table). The script must assign ownership per fact so the user never hears it twice when both are open.
- Disabled menu items remain focusable and announce their reason; this is a deliberate deviation from the common "skip disabled items" pattern and must be written down so an implementer does not "fix" it.
- The rolling `aria-label` on `CMP-180` is throttled; specify its update trigger (range change, symbol change, mode change) rather than per render tick, which would flood.
- Where a state has no natural announcement moment (partial history is a property of the range, not an event), specify that it is part of the summary rather than a live-region message.
- Verify that every hotkey in the band is listed in `SCR-013` (hotkey cheatsheet) and editable in `SCR-113` (hotkey editor), so the keyboard map is discoverable by users, not only by this document.

## Test plan
- Walk each scenario against the E12-D03..E12-D08 frames with the a11y design lead and at least one screen-reader-proficient reviewer, using the reader(s) named in `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Contrast measurement of every new state pair in both themes; CVD simulation for all three common deficiency types.
- Keyboard-only traversal of the full band with no pointer attached, confirming focus is never lost or trapped.
- Cross-check the announcement budget arithmetic against the worst case (1 s bars + moving crosshair + a rebuild in progress).
- Confirm every hotkey appears in `SCR-013`; file any missing entry.
- Review findings triage with the CDO; each finding closed as fixed, deferred-with-owner or accepted-with-reason.

## Security notes
- The script must not cause account-scoped information to be announced on a market-data surface; verify that no announcement includes position, order or balance data (those belong to `US-CHART-013`'s overlay work, announced by its own surface).
- Correlation ids announced on `SCR-048` must be read as opaque identifiers; confirm they carry no session token or account identifier.
- The "Needs recorded ticks" announcement reveals recording state; confirm it is consistent with the RBAC rules for `GET /api/v1/recording/symbols` and is not announced to roles that cannot see it.

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket **is** the accessibility deliverable for the band; it is governed by `05-accessibility-standard.md` end to end, targeting WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Non-negotiables verified here: no colour-only encoding of direction or state; no hover-only functionality; visible focus on every interactive element; announcements polite and throttled; the `SCR-045` table treated as equal status, not fallback.
- The script explicitly covers reduced-motion users, confirming they lose no information (cross-checked against E12-D10).
- Findings of severity "blocks a user from reading the chart at all" are P0 and block the originating ticket's sign-off.

## Performance notes
- The a11y constructions have a frame cost: the DOM mirror is windowed rather than full-series precisely so it does not scale with 100 k bars, and the rolling `aria-label` is throttled. The review must confirm no design decision here would force per-bar DOM for the whole series, which would breach the `SCR-030` budget.
- The `SCR-045` table reads the same in-memory series and issues no extra fetch; confirm the script does not imply otherwise.

## Observability
- No analytics are emitted by the a11y layer. The review notes which existing events (`chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.bar_mode_changed`) are sufficient to observe accessible-path usage, so adoption of the accessible view can be measured without adding assistive-technology detection, which the standard forbids.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Screen-reader script, keyboard map and announcement budget published in the repo and linked from `SCR-030`, `SCR-045` and `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- All findings triaged; P0 findings fixed in their originating design tickets before those tickets reach Done.
- Contrast/CVD audit results attached.
- Script handed to QA (referenced from the E12 QA tickets) and to engineering via E12-D12.
- **CDO and a11y design lead sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, before the Sprint 05 frontend stories begin.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D03, E12-D04, E12-D05, E12-D06, E12-D07, E12-D08 (all must have drafts to review; each may only reach Done after its findings are addressed).
- Cross-checks E12-D10 (reduced motion).
- Feeds E12-D12 (handoff), E12-D13 (design QA), the E12 QA tickets and every E12 frontend story.

`design/e12-a11y-review-bar-series`

title: Engineering handoff pack for the bar-builder & series-rendering band
body:
## Context
E12's frontend stories run in Sprint 05–08 and are worth 63 points across two areas (`area/chart-engine`, `area/ingestion`, modules M7 and M8). The design-ahead rule in `00-planning-brief.md` requires their designs to be Done ≥2 sprints earlier; `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 additionally requires each Story to link a Done design artefact and to have its states enumerated before it can enter Ready.

This ticket produces the single artefact that makes those stories *Ready*: a handoff pack that collects every decision from E12-D01..E12-D11 into an implementable form — redlines, token names, the per-mode specification table, the geometry rules, the state matrix with precedence, the screen-reader script, the keyboard map, the motion spec, the error-mapping table, and the analytics event list — plus a walkthrough session with the frontend engineers who will build it.

The explicit goal is the planning brief's standard: "a developer must not need to ask for more details".

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- A **handoff pack** (a document in the repo plus the linked Figma frames) indexed by consuming surface — `SCR-030` (series states), `SCR-031` General tab, `SCR-041`, `SCR-042`, `SCR-045`, `SCR-047`, `SCR-048` — and by component — `CMP-181`, `CMP-220`, `CMP-222`, `CMP-226` plus any entries accepted in E12-D09.
- **Per-mode implementation table** consolidating: `bar_type` value, user-facing label, description copy, `param` type/unit/default/min/max, validation message, whether recorded ticks are required, and the API/WS field each is bound to (`GET /api/v1/market/bars`, `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`).
- **Geometry and density rules** from E12-D06 in numeric, implementable form (formulas, clamps, token names), with the LOD ladder and the aggregated-mark definition.
- **State matrix with precedence** from E12-D02/E12-D08, plus the **error-mapping table** (`no_data_recorded` 422 → `SCR-047` variant; empty success → "no bars"; transport failure → `SCR-048`; context loss → `SCR-048` WebGL variant).
- **A11y pack** from E12-D11: screen-reader script, keyboard map, announcement budget, DOM-mirror text contract per bar mode.
- **Motion pack** from E12-D10 with durations, easings, reduced-motion equivalents and the drop-under-load rule.
- **Token and Storybook manifest**: every token used, every Storybook state the frontend must produce, so visual regression coverage matches the design intent.
- **Analytics manifest**: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed`, `chart.symbol_changed`, `chart.settings_changed`, `chart.empty_state_shown`, `chart.error_shown`, `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`, plus the rebuild start/complete/cancel events — each with its property set and its trigger point.
- A recorded **walkthrough session** with the E12 frontend engineers, QA/SDET and the Architect; questions raised are answered in the pack itself rather than in chat, and the pack is updated before sign-off.
- An **open-questions register** listing anything deliberately left to engineering judgement, so ambiguity is explicit rather than discovered mid-sprint.

## Out of scope
- Writing the engineering stories themselves (the E12 engineering chunk owns those).
- Backend bar-builder algorithm specification (module M8) — that is architecture/engineering, referenced here only where it constrains what the UI can show.
- Footprint, profile, indicator and drawing handoffs (E18, E19, E13, E14).
- Implementation, Storybook code and visual-regression baselines.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The pack makes the frontend stories Ready
  Given an E12 frontend story is being refined for Sprint 05
  When its Definition of Ready is checked
  Then the linked design artefact is this pack and it is Status Done
  And the story's states, tokens, a11y expectations and analytics events are all resolvable from the pack without asking a designer

Scenario: Every consuming surface is indexed
  Given the pack is reviewed
  When it is checked against the screens this epic touches
  Then SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-047 and SCR-048 each have an entry with frames, states, tokens and acceptance notes
  And each touched component entry links to its updated 15-component-catalogue.md record

Scenario: Walkthrough questions are absorbed, not answered in chat (edge)
  Given an engineer asks during the walkthrough what happens when a rebuild is cancelled while the symbol is also being switched
  When the question is triaged
  Then either the pack is updated with the answer or the case is added to the open-questions register with an owner
  And the answer is not left only in the meeting notes

Scenario: A design decision has no API or WS field to bind to (failure)
  Given the pack specifies a column or state with no source in 22-api-openapi.yaml or 23-ws-protocol.md
  When the binding audit is run
  Then the gap is filed as a blocking change ticket against the API or WS contract
  And the affected design element is marked as pending that change rather than handed over as buildable

Scenario: Late design change after handoff
  Given a design element changes after this pack is signed off
  When the change is made
  Then the pack is versioned and the affected engineering stories are notified on their tickets
  And the change is reflected in 14-screens-catalogue.md and 15-component-catalogue.md in the same sprint
```

## Technical notes / design
- Organise the pack **by what an engineer opens a ticket to do**, not by design artefact type: surface first, then component, then the cross-cutting packs (a11y, motion, analytics). A pack organised by Figma page is a pack nobody reads.
- Every visual value is a token name; the pack contains no raw hex, px-without-rule, or "match the mock" instructions.
- The binding audit is the highest-value part: every field the design shows is traced to `GET /api/v1/market/bars`, `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`, `GET /api/v1/recording/symbols`, `GET /api/v1/me/preferences` or the `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` topic. Anything untraceable is a contract change, filed before Sprint 05 starts, not discovered during it.
- Carry the `confirm: false` rule forward verbatim from `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 — the forming-bar visual, the table row label and the accessible name all descend from that one protocol fact, and the pack should present them together so their coupling is obvious.
- Include the **negative space**: what the design deliberately does not do (no approximation of missing tick data, no countdown on non-time bars, no sorting that silently breaks series order, no colour-only direction encoding). Engineers implement the absence of features badly when nobody wrote the absence down.
- Version the pack (`v1`, `v1.1`, …) and state the change log at the top; the design-ahead rule means the pack will outlive several sprints of memory.

## Test plan
- Dry-run the pack with one frontend engineer who was **not** in the design reviews: they attempt to spec a build for `SCR-042` using only the pack, and every question they must ask is a defect in the pack.
- Binding audit against `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md`, item by item, with the Architect.
- Cross-check the Storybook manifest against the states listed in `15-component-catalogue.md` for each touched component; mismatches resolved.
- Verify every DoR item in `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 that depends on design can be satisfied from the pack for at least three sample E12 stories.
- QA/SDET review: confirm the screen-reader script and state matrix are usable as test oracles.

## Security notes
- The pack states the RBAC expectations for every surface it covers: `marketdata:read` for the bar surfaces, owner-only for the "Record this symbol" action, and the rule that client-side hiding is presentational while the backend enforces.
- It states that user-entered `param` values are bounded client-side for usability but re-validated server-side (API `param` maxLength 24), so no engineer treats the UI bound as the security control.
- It states that error copy and correlation ids carry no internal detail, secrets or account identifiers.
- No credentials, keys, account ids or live account screenshots appear anywhere in the pack or its Figma frames.

## Accessibility notes
- The a11y pack from E12-D11 is included in full and is presented as a **build requirement**, not an appendix: screen-reader script, keyboard map, announcement budget and the DOM-mirror text contract per bar mode.
- Each surface entry lists its axe-core expectations and the manual screen-reader scenarios QA will run, so a11y work is scoped into the story estimate rather than discovered at review.
- The pack restates the non-negotiables: equal-status data table, no hover-only functionality, no colour-only encoding, visible focus, throttled announcements.

## Performance notes
- Budgets are restated per surface so they land in the story estimates: ≥58 fps at 2560×1440 with 100 k bars and ≤450 MB per chart panel (`SCR-030`); ≥55 fps / ≤512 MB GPU per pane (`US-CHART-001`); interval switch ≤200 ms cached, ≤600 ms uncached; chart-type switch ≤100 ms client-side; rebuild ≤10 s per 1 M prints, cancellable; data table ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame at 100 k rows.
- The pack names which benchmark in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 each budget is verified by, so the engineering stories reference an existing gate rather than inventing one.

## Observability
- The analytics manifest is part of the handoff, with each event's name, properties and trigger point, so instrumentation ships with the feature rather than after it.
- The pack notes which engine diagnostics values (`SCR-046`: fps, frame time p50/p95, visible bars, dropped frames) must agree with design-visible values such as the aggregation level, so the two cannot diverge.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Pack published in the repo, versioned, and linked from every touched `14-screens-catalogue.md` entry and from the E12 epic ticket.
- Walkthrough session held with frontend, QA/SDET and the Architect; all questions absorbed into the pack or into the open-questions register with owners.
- Binding audit complete; any contract gaps filed as tickets against `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` before Sprint 05.
- Dry-run with an uninvolved engineer completed and resulting defects fixed.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done** before Sprint 05 planning, satisfying the design-ahead rule for all E12 frontend stories.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D09 (design-system contribution), E12-D10 (motion), E12-D11 (a11y pack) — which in turn depend on E12-D01..E12-D08.
- Consumed by every E12 frontend story in Sprint 05–08 and by E12-D13 (design QA), which tests the built result against this pack.

`design/e12-handoff-pack`

title: Spike: Renko brick sizing, ATR bricks and cancellable series rebuilds
body:
## Context
Two open questions sit in front of the Renko and range builders and both would be expensive to answer wrong after the code is written.

**(1) ATR bricks.** `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` documents `renko` `param` as "brick size in ticks, **or `atr:14` for ATR bricks**", and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 repeats it. But `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1 `BarSpec` has only `range_ticks` — there is no ATR field and no statement of *which* series the ATR is measured over, or whether the brick size is recomputed per brick (making the series non-deterministic under `restore()`) or frozen per session. The contract and the internal model disagree, and this Epic must resolve the disagreement before E12-S04 is written, not during it.

**(2) Rebuild cancellation.** `US-CHART-004` NFR says "rebuild is cancellable" and `US-CHART-003` says "rebuilds of 1M prints complete in ≤10 s". Whether that is achievable on the QuestDB read path, and what the cancellation mechanism is (asyncio task cancellation over a streaming cursor vs a chunked pull loop with a cancellation token), determines the shape of E12-S12's rebuild API.

`30-release-roadmap.md` §12 puts Renko and range bars on rung 2 of the descoping ladder, so a cheap, early answer here also tells the Owner what is actually at risk if the rung is pulled.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Timebox: 3 days.** One engineer.
- Answer Q1: define ATR-brick semantics or reject them for R1. Deliverables: a written recommendation covering (a) the source series for ATR (which `BarSpec` the ATR is computed over — it cannot be the renko series itself without circularity), (b) recompute cadence, (c) the effect on invariant BI-4 (replay determinism) and BI-5 (`restore(snapshot())` equivalence), (d) the `BarSpec` field(s) needed.
- Answer Q2: measure rebuild throughput. Read 1M `TradeEvent` rows for one symbol-day from QuestDB through the E08 storage adapter and drive each of the six builders end to end; record wall-clock, peak RSS and rows/s. Prototype and measure at least two cancellation strategies.
- Produce **ADR-0014 "Renko brick sizing and series rebuild semantics"** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` recording both decisions (including "defer ATR bricks to R2" if that is the answer).
- File follow-up tickets against E12-S04 and E12-S12 carrying the findings.

## Out of scope
- Production-shippable builder code. Prototype code is throwaway unless the ADR says otherwise.
- P&F box/reversal semantics — `pnf` is not built in R1 at all.
- UI for choosing brick size (E12-S12 owns SCR-042).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: ATR-brick decision is recorded
  Given the spike has run to its timebox
  Then ADR-0014 states either the exact BarSpec fields and recompute rule for ATR bricks
  Or states "atr:* deferred to R2" with the enum value reserved and a 422 error path specified
  And in either case BI-4 and BI-5 are shown to still hold

Scenario: Rebuild throughput is measured, not estimated
  Given a 1M-trade symbol-day fixture
  When each builder rebuilds the full day
  Then measured wall-clock, rows/s and peak RSS are recorded per builder in the ADR
  And the result is compared against the 10 s budget with a pass/fail statement

Scenario: The budget is missed
  Given a builder needs more than 10 s for 1M prints
  Then the spike records the dominant cost (read path, per-trade Python overhead, or emit path)
  And files a follow-up Task with a concrete optimisation proposal rather than silently relaxing the NFR

Scenario: Cancellation actually cancels
  Given a rebuild is in flight
  When cancellation is requested
  Then the prototype stops reading within 250 ms, releases the cursor, and leaves no partial rows in bars_*
```

## Technical notes / design
- Circularity trap: ATR over the renko series itself is self-referential (brick size depends on bricks that depend on brick size). The only coherent options are ATR over a fixed time series (e.g. 1m bars, N periods) or ATR frozen at series-construction time from a lookback window. State which, explicitly.
- Determinism is the hard constraint: whatever is chosen must survive `restore(snapshot())` at a random cut point (BI-5) and must reproduce byte-identically under replay (BI-4). A brick size that drifts with live ATR fails both unless the drift itself is deterministic from the trade sequence.
- Cancellation over a streaming QuestDB cursor: measure whether `asyncio.CancelledError` propagates promptly through the driver, or whether a chunked pull loop with an explicit token is needed. The answer becomes E12-S12's contract.

## Test plan
Spike code is not production; no coverage gate applies. Measurements must be reproducible: the benchmark script, the fixture identifier and the hardware profile are committed alongside the ADR so a later engineer can re-run them.

## Security notes
No production surface. The one security-relevant finding to capture: if ATR bricks are accepted, `param` parsing gains a second grammar (`atr:14`) — note the input-validation requirement (strict regex, bounded period) so E12-T05 implements it as a whitelist, not a parser.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. If the ADR defers ATR bricks, it must state the user-facing message the UI shows for an unsupported `param` so E12-S12 has copy to render as text (not a silent fallback).

## Performance notes
This spike *is* the performance measurement for the rebuild path. Numbers feed the CI budget that E12-T07 later enforces.

## Observability
Recommend the metric names the rebuild path should expose (`bar_rebuild_duration_seconds{kind}`, `bar_rebuild_cancelled_total`) so E12-S12 ships them from day one.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2: questions answered with recorded evidence (numbers, not opinions); ADR-0014 merged; follow-up tickets filed against E12-S04 and E12-S12 with findings linked; spike branch `spike/e12-renko-rebuild` left unmerged and marked throwaway; findings presented at Sprint Review; `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk (e.g. rebuild budget unreachable) surfaced.

## Dependencies
- **E08** — the ingestion/storage adapter that supplies the trade fixture and the read path being measured.

title: Build deterministic time bars from the trade tape with clock-driven closes
body:
## Context
Time bars are the default series every chart opens on and the reference every other builder is checked against. They are also the only builder with a second input besides trades: a **clock**. `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 is explicit that "a bar closes on `on_clock` even if no trade arrives, so `on_bar_close` rules fire on schedule in a dead market" — a requirement that comes from the rule engine (E35), not from charting, and that a trades-only implementation silently fails.

This Story implements the `time` kind of the `BarBuilder` protocol, serving **US-MKT-008** (the bars that backfill produces), **US-CHART-001** (the candles that render) and the substrate for **US-CHART-005** (timeframe switching) and **US-CHART-009** (session anchoring, whose `session_anchor_utc_min` this builder consumes).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `TimeBarBuilder` implementing `on_trade`, `on_clock`, `snapshot`, `restore` per `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.2.
- Boundary arithmetic: `floor((ts_event - anchor) / interval_ms) * interval_ms + anchor`, with `align_to_epoch` and `session_anchor_utc_min` from `BarSpec` (US-CHART-009's UTC-00:00 / funding-time / custom anchor all resolve to a minutes-past-midnight offset here).
- Empty-interval handling: no bar emitted by default; `gap_before=True` on the next real bar; `BarSeries.densify()` (from E12-T01) supplies synthetic flat bars to consumers that need a continuous index, and those are never persisted.
- Clock-driven close via `on_clock`, emitting a `close` `BarUpdate` on schedule in a dead market.
- Late-arriving trade handling: a trade whose `ts_event` falls in an already-closed bar is applied to that bar and re-emits `close` with `amended=True`; beyond 60 s the trade is dropped and counted in `bars_late_trade_dropped_total`.
- Full field population: `buy_volume`/`sell_volume` from the taker side, `delta`, running-path `min_delta`/`max_delta`, `trade_count`, `turnover`, `vwap`, `closed`, `partial`, `gap_before`.
- The standard interval ladder of US-CHART-005 (1 s … 1 D) plus arbitrary custom intervals (e.g. 7m), all expressed as `interval_ms`.

## Out of scope
- Non-time builders (E12-S02/S03/S04).
- Multi-spec fan-out and state persistence cadence (E12-T03).
- The kline REST backfill that seeds pre-recording history (E12-S05).
- Rendering (E12-S06) and the timeframe-switch UX (E12-S11).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bars close on the boundary
  Given a 1m time spec anchored to UTC 00:00
  And trades at 10:00:59.900 and 10:01:00.100
  Then the first trade belongs to the 10:00 bar and the second opens the 10:01 bar
  And the 10:00 bar is emitted with closed=true exactly once

Scenario: A dead market still closes bars
  Given a 1m spec and no trades for 5 minutes
  When on_clock advances past each boundary
  Then 0 bars are persisted (empty intervals emit nothing)
  And the bar that was open at the start of the silence is closed on its own boundary, not on the next trade

Scenario: Late trade amends a closed bar
  Given the 10:00 bar closed 20 seconds ago
  When a trade with ts_event inside 10:00 arrives
  Then that bar's OHLCV and delta are recomputed and re-emitted with amended=true
  And the total-volume invariant BI-1 still holds

Scenario: Very late trade is dropped, not silently merged
  Given the 10:00 bar closed 90 seconds ago
  When a trade with ts_event inside 10:00 arrives
  Then it is not applied to any bar
  And bars_late_trade_dropped_total is incremented with the symbol label

Scenario: Session anchor shifts the grid
  Given a 1h spec with session_anchor_utc_min = 480
  Then bar boundaries fall at 08:00, 09:00 … UTC rather than on the epoch grid
  And switching the anchor produces a different spec_hash and therefore a separate series
```

## Technical notes / design
- `min_delta`/`max_delta` track the running intra-bar delta **path**, updated on every trade — not `min(delta_start, delta_end)`. They are the input to exhaustion/absorption reads in R2, so an endpoint-only implementation is a silent correctness bug that no OHLCV comparison would catch.
- No allocation in the common path: the builder mutates an internal mutable draft and materialises a frozen `Bar` only on emit (`24-internal-schemas.md` §3.5).
- The amendment path must be idempotent against the QuestDB dedup upsert of E12-T02 — re-emitting a bar overwrites it.
- Clock source is the offset-corrected exchange clock (US-MKT-009), not the local wall clock.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85%: boundary arithmetic across DST-free UTC (crypto has no sessions, but anchors do shift the grid), each field's accumulation, amendment and drop thresholds.
- **Property**: BI-1 (volume conservation), BI-2 (`delta == buy - sell`), BI-3 (`min_delta <= delta <= max_delta`, both attained on the path), BI-6 (`vwap == turnover / volume` to 8 dp, or `open` when volume is 0) over ≥1M synthetic trades.
- **Golden file**: the recorded BTCUSDT fixture day at 1m/5m/1h compared against the reference implementation, byte-for-byte on OHLCV (roadmap exit criterion 4).
- **Integration**: builder driven by the real bus from E08 against a recorded fixture; cross-checked against Bybit `/v5/market/kline` for the same window with a documented tolerance for the known edge (exchange klines include bars we deliberately omit for empty intervals).

## Security notes
`interval_ms` is user-controlled via `param`. Bound it: minimum 1 s (the documented floor of US-CHART-005), maximum 1 D, and reject non-integer or zero values before a builder is instantiated — an interval of 0 or 1 µs is a CPU-exhaustion vector that would emit bars per trade forever. No secrets, no PII.

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI. Two obligations flow downstream: the `gap_before` flag must be exposed so the renderer can draw a real gap (never interpolate) and the data-table alternative (SCR-045) can state it in text; and `partial=True` must be exposed so "history starts at <ts>" is a text statement rather than a visual cue.

## Performance notes
Per-trade cost must be O(1) with no allocation; the builder sits on the ingest hot path whose budget is ingest→bus ≤20 ms p95 at 5 000 prints/s (US-MKT-006). Benchmark: 1M trades through a single 1m spec in well under the 10 s rebuild budget, measured as part of E12-T04's harness.

## Observability
`bars_built_total{symbol,kind="time"}`, `bars_amended_total`, `bars_late_trade_dropped_total`, `bar_build_latency_seconds{kind="time"}`. Log at INFO on first bar per new spec, at WARN on a dropped late trade with the lateness in ms.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2: every Gherkin scenario backed by an automated test; coverage ≥85%; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 matches shipped behaviour; perf benchmark recorded; QA sign-off on the black-box plan; demoed (a chart rendering these bars, or a recorded terminal run if E12-S06 has not landed); feature-flag state recorded (`bars.time` is default-on, it is the baseline series); PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T01** — the domain model and `spec_hash`.
- **E08** — `TradeEvent` on the bus, the taker-side field, and the exchange clock offset (US-MKT-009).

## Branch
`feat/e12-time-bars`

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1–§3.5 (model, protocol, time-bar edge cases, invariants, multi-spec)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-001, US-CHART-005, US-CHART-009, US-MKT-006, US-MKT-008, US-MKT-009
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.8 `bars_time`
