title: Implement BarBuilderSet fan-out with snapshot/restore state persistence
body:
## Context
A single symbol typically carries 3–8 active bar specs at once — 1m, 5m and 1h time bars plus a footprint tick or volume series. `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.5 fixes how that works: "`BarBuilderSet` fans one `TradeEvent` to all builders for that symbol in a single pass; **builders never subscribe to the bus individually**. Cost is O(specs) per trade with no allocation in the common path."

The second half of this Task is restart survival. §3.2: "`snapshot()`/`restore()` exist so a restart or a replay seek resumes mid-bar without replaying the whole day. `BuilderState` is a msgpack blob persisted every 60 s per `(symbol, spec_hash)`." Without it, every backend restart either loses the forming bar or pays a full-day rebuild for every active spec on every symbol — which at the recorder's symbol count is minutes of cold start.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `BarBuilderSet`: one bus subscription per symbol, fanning each `TradeEvent` to every registered builder in a single pass; register/unregister of specs at runtime without dropping trades.
- Lifecycle: a spec is registered when a chart, a footprint view, an indicator, a rule or the recorder needs it, and reference-counted so the last consumer's departure unregisters it after a grace period (mirroring the 30-second grace of US-MKT-005).
- A hard cap on concurrent specs per symbol and per user, with a clear error when exceeded (the resource-exhaustion mitigation named in the Epic's security notes).
- `BuilderState` msgpack serialisation for all six builders, persisted every 60 s per `(symbol, spec_hash)`, with atomic write and a corruption-safe read (a bad blob is discarded and the spec cold-starts rather than crashing).
- Restart path: on boot, restore each active spec from its blob, then replay only the trades newer than the blob's watermark before going live.
- Emit routing: `BarUpdate`s flow to the QuestDB write path (E12-T02) and to the WS publisher (E12-T06) from one place, so live and replay share the emit path exactly.

## Out of scope
- The WS topic and framing itself (E12-T06) and the REST endpoints (E12-T05).
- Replay-specific seek semantics — E26 reuses `restore()` as-is; no replay code here.
- The recorder's symbol-list management (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One pass, many specs
  Given 8 registered specs for BTCUSDT
  When a TradeEvent arrives
  Then the bus is read once and all 8 builders are advanced
  And no builder holds its own bus subscription

Scenario: Restart resumes mid-bar
  Given a 1h time bar is 40 minutes formed and a state blob was written 30 seconds ago
  When the process restarts
  Then the builder restores from the blob, replays only the trades after the blob watermark
  And the resulting bar is identical to the one an uninterrupted run would have produced (invariant BI-5)

Scenario: Corrupt state is survivable
  Given a truncated or unparseable state blob
  When restore is attempted
  Then the blob is discarded, a warning is logged with the spec_hash
  And the spec cold-starts by rebuilding from the tape rather than crashing the process

Scenario: Spec cap is enforced
  Given the per-symbol spec cap is reached
  When another distinct spec is registered
  Then registration is refused with an error naming the cap and the currently active specs
  And existing series are unaffected

Scenario: Last consumer releases the spec
  Given the only chart using vol:1000 on ETHUSDT closes
  Then the spec is unregistered after the grace period
  And its final state blob is written before teardown
```

## Technical notes / design
- "No allocation in the common path" is a measurable requirement, not a slogan: the fan-out loop must not build a list per trade. Verify with an allocation-count assertion in the benchmark.
- The state blob watermark is a `TsUs` of the last applied trade, so the post-restore replay window is exact. Persisting every 60 s bounds the replay to 60 s of tape per spec.
- Atomic write: write-temp-then-rename, so a crash mid-write never leaves a half blob (which the corruption path above then has to handle anyway — belt and braces).
- Reference counting must be robust to a client that disconnects without unsubscribing; the grace period plus a liveness sweep handles it.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85%: registration/unregistration, reference counting, cap enforcement, msgpack round-trip per builder kind, corrupt-blob handling.
- **Property**: BI-5 — `restore(snapshot())` at random cut points across all six builders yields the same final series as an uninterrupted run, including mid-split (volume) and mid-reversal (renko) states.
- **Integration**: kill and restart the process mid-day against a recorded fixture; assert the resulting series equals the uninterrupted run byte-for-byte.
- **Perf**: fan-out benchmark at 8 specs × 5 000 prints/s with an allocation assertion.

## Security notes
This is where the resource-exhaustion mitigation actually lives. An attacker (or an over-enthusiastic client) subscribing to hundreds of distinct `spec_hash`es multiplies CPU, memory and QuestDB SYMBOL cardinality without bound. Enforce: per-symbol spec cap, per-user total spec cap, and a global cap; refuse with a clear error rather than degrading silently. State blobs are written to a server-controlled path derived from `(symbol, spec_hash)` where both components are already whitelist-validated (E12-T01) — no client string is ever concatenated into a filesystem path, which closes the path-traversal vector that `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 flags for E16's archive paths.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The cap-exceeded error message is rendered by SCR-042 and must be a human-readable sentence stating the cap and what to close, not a code.

## Performance notes
Budget: fan-out adds O(specs) with no allocation, keeping ingest→bus within the ≤20 ms p95 of US-MKT-006 at 5 000 prints/s. Cold start after restart must be bounded by the 60 s state cadence rather than by the day length — measured as "time from boot to first live bar emit" and recorded.

## Observability
`bar_builder_specs_active{symbol}`, `bar_builder_fanout_latency_seconds`, `bar_state_snapshots_written_total`, `bar_state_restore_failures_total`, `bar_builder_cold_starts_total`, `bar_builder_spec_cap_rejections_total`. Cold-start duration exported as a histogram.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2: acceptance criteria verified by tests including the restart integration test; coverage ≥85%; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.2/§3.5 matches shipped behaviour; perf benchmark with allocation assertion recorded; security review comment on the cap and path handling; demo of the restart-resume behaviour (observable effect); PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S01**, **E12-S02** — at least two builder kinds must exist before fan-out is meaningful; S03/S04 plug in without changing this code.
- **E12-T02** — the write path the emit routing targets.

## Branch
`feat/e12-builder-set`

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.2 (protocol, `BuilderState`), §3.5 (multi-spec efficiency), §3.4 BI-5
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-MKT-005 (30 s unsubscribe grace), US-MKT-006 (throughput NFR)

title: Build the bar determinism harness: BI-1..BI-6 properties and golden fixtures
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criterion 4 is the single hardest gate in R1: **"All five bar types produce identical results to a reference implementation on a recorded fixture day, byte-for-byte on OHLCV."** `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.4 turns that into six named invariants (BI-1…BI-6) each with a prescribed test layer, and §16 assigns "Property tests for BI-1…BI-6 over ≥1M synthetic trades plus a recorded-day golden file" as the bar-builder test obligation.

This Task builds the machine that proves it, and wires it into CI so a regression fails the build rather than surfacing in R2 as an inexplicable footprint discrepancy. It is deliberately a single shared harness rather than six ad-hoc test files, because the invariants are cross-builder and the fixture must be identical for all of them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Synthetic trade generator**: seeded, reproducible, producing ≥1M `TradeEvent`s with configurable volatility, print-size distribution, taker-side skew and adversarial patterns (huge prints spanning N thresholds, exact-threshold hits, rapid reversals, long silences, late arrivals, duplicate `tradeId`s).
- **Property suite** implementing BI-1…BI-6 exactly as §3.4 prescribes, run against all six builders:
  - BI-1 volume conservation (with volume-bar splitting and renko single-allocation);
  - BI-2 `delta == buy_volume - sell_volume`;
  - BI-3 `min_delta <= delta <= max_delta`, both attained on the intrabar path;
  - BI-4 replay determinism including `spec_hash`;
  - BI-5 `restore(snapshot())` equivalence at random cut points;
  - BI-6 `vwap == turnover / volume` to 8 dp, or `open` when volume is 0.
- **Golden fixture**: a version-controlled recorded Bybit symbol-day (the fixed fixture `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 requires for integration), stored with its provenance, plus generated golden bar files per builder kind and parameter.
- **Reference implementation**: an independent, deliberately naive, non-optimised implementation of each builder used only as the comparison oracle — written from the spec text, not from the production code, so it is a genuine cross-check rather than a tautology.
- **Byte-for-byte comparator** producing a readable diff (bar index, field, expected, actual) rather than an assertion dump.
- **CI wiring**: the suite runs as a required check; golden-file updates require an explicit, reviewed regeneration commit with a stated reason (a silent `--update-goldens` in CI is forbidden).
- Rebuild-throughput benchmark (1M prints per builder) reported alongside, carrying forward E12-K01's baselines.

## Out of scope
- Engine-side render golden images (E11-T08 owns that harness; E12-S09 uses it).
- Footprint/profile invariants (E18/E19 add their own, reusing this generator).
- The recorder producing the fixture (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All six builders satisfy every invariant
  Given 1 000 000 generated trades and the standard spec matrix
  When the property suite runs
  Then BI-1 through BI-6 hold for every builder and every spec
  And a violation reports the invariant name, the builder, the spec and the first offending bar

Scenario: Golden comparison is byte-for-byte on OHLCV
  Given the recorded fixture day
  When each builder replays it and is compared against the reference implementation
  Then OHLCV matches exactly for every bar
  And any mismatch prints bar index, field name, expected and actual

Scenario: A deliberate regression fails CI
  Given an intentional off-by-one introduced into the time-bar boundary
  When the harness runs in CI
  Then the build fails and names the invariant or golden file that broke

Scenario: Golden regeneration is deliberate
  Given a builder change that legitimately alters output
  When goldens are regenerated
  Then the commit contains the regenerated files, a stated reason, and a build_version bump
  And CI rejects a run that would regenerate goldens implicitly
```

## Technical notes / design
- The reference implementation must be written by a different engineer than the production builders, or at minimum written from the spec document alone. A reference derived from the production code proves nothing.
- Seeded generation makes failures reproducible: every failing property run prints the seed, and the seed is the whole repro.
- The fixture day is committed (or pinned by content hash in object storage with a checked-in manifest) so the comparison is stable across machines and years.
- `build_version` (E12-T02) is the coupling point: a golden regeneration and a `build_version` bump must happen in the same commit, because the bump is what triggers rebuilds of already-persisted bars.

## Test plan
This Task *is* test infrastructure; its own correctness is verified by **mutation testing**: a set of deliberately seeded defects (off-by-one boundary, endpoint-only `min_delta`, missing volume split, phantom range bars, renko double-allocation) must each be caught by the harness. A defect the harness misses is a gap in the harness, and closing it is part of this Task's Done.

## Security notes
The fixture contains only public market data — no keys, no PII, no account identifiers. Confirm this explicitly before committing it (a recorded session captured through the app could otherwise carry authentication frames). The generator must not be usable as a load-generation tool against the live exchange; it is offline-only by construction.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — test infrastructure, no UI. The comparator's diff output should be plain text readable in a terminal and in CI logs without colour dependence.

## Performance notes
The full 1M-trade × 6-builder suite must complete within the CI budget (target ≤10 minutes) or it will be disabled by attrition; if it cannot, split into a fast PR-gate subset (100k trades) and a full nightly run, with the nightly failure treated as a build break. Rebuild throughput per builder is recorded here and becomes the baseline the 10 s / 1M-print NFR is enforced against.

## Observability
Publish per-run metrics to the CI dashboard: invariant pass/fail per builder, rebuild throughput per builder, harness wall-clock. A throughput regression >10% against the recorded baseline is a build warning and >25% a failure, mirroring the engine benchmark policy of `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3.

## Definition of Done
Per §4.2: all six invariants implemented and green; golden fixtures committed with provenance; reference implementation reviewed as independent; mutation-testing set demonstrably caught; CI required check wired; coverage met; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.4/§16 reflect the shipped harness; demo of a deliberate regression failing the build; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T03** — fan-out and snapshot/restore must exist for BI-5 to be testable.
- **E12-S03**, **E12-S04** — all six builders must exist before the suite can cover them.
- **E12-K01** — rebuild baselines.

## Branch
`feat/e12-determinism-harness`

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.4 invariants BI-1…BI-6, §16 test obligations
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criterion 4, §5.4 quality gates (integration: recorded fixture)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (property testing, golden files, CI gates)
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.8 `build_version`

title: Implement GET /market/klines and GET /market/bars with source metadata
body:
## Context
Two REST endpoints are the bootstrap path for every chart: `GET /market/klines` for time candles and `GET /market/bars` as "the single entry point for every non-time bar construction". Both are fully specified in `22-api-openapi.yaml`, down to the `bar_type`/`param` table, the `x-rbac: { permissions: [marketdata:read] }` gate, the `meta.sources` / `meta.recording_started_at` honesty fields and the exact error semantics — `/market/bars` returns **422 `no_data_recorded`** for a window starting before recording began "rather than silently substituting REST klines, because tick-accurate construction is impossible there".

This Task implements the spec rather than inventing it. The interface is already merged, so per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10 the work here is implementation plus contract tests that prove the implementation and the document are the same thing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /market/klines`: `symbol`, `interval`, `from`, `to`, `limit`, `price_type` (trade|mark|index|premium_index), `include_open`, `include_delta`; source priority tape → kline backfill → Parquet; `confirm` flag on the in-progress candle only when `include_open=true`.
- `GET /market/bars`: `symbol`, `bar_type`, `param`, `from`, `to`, `limit`, `include_open`, `include_delta` (default true); the full `bar_type` enum with `param` parsed per the documented table; 422 `no_data_recorded` for pre-recording windows; `pnf` and (per ADR-0014) possibly `atr:*` returning a 422 that names the reason and the supported alternatives.
- Shared response assembly producing `KlineResponse` with `meta.next_cursor`, `has_more`, `count`, `sources`, `recording_started_at`, `generated_at`.
- Cursor-based pagination honouring `BarLimit`, oldest→newest ordering.
- RBAC: `marketdata:read`, scope none, enforced by the shared dependency from E09.
- Null-not-zero discipline for delta fields on kline-sourced windows.
- Generated contract tests asserting responses validate against the committed OpenAPI schemas, including every documented error.

## Out of scope
- `GET /market/footprint` — E18.
- The WS `bars` topic — E12-T06.
- Client-side consumption — E12-S06/S11.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bars endpoint serves every supported bar type
  Given recorded tape for BTCUSDT
  When /market/bars is called for each of time, tick, volume, range, delta and renko with a valid param
  Then each returns bars ordered oldest to newest with meta.sources naming the tiers touched
  And the response validates against the KlineResponse schema

Scenario: Pre-recording window is refused for non-time bars
  Given recording_started_at is 2026-10-27
  When /market/bars is called for tick:500 with from=2026-10-12
  Then the response is 422 with code no_data_recorded
  And no kline-derived bars are returned

Scenario: Klines degrade honestly
  Given the same pre-recording window on /market/klines with include_delta=true
  Then bars are returned from the kline tier
  And their delta, min_delta, max_delta and cvd are null rather than zero
  And meta.recording_started_at states where tick-accurate data begins

Scenario: Invalid param is rejected before it reaches a builder
  When /market/bars is called with bar_type=tick and param="../../etc"
  Then the response is 400 validation_failed naming the param
  And no builder is instantiated and no QuestDB SYMBOL value is created

Scenario: Unauthorised access is refused
  Given a caller without marketdata:read
  When either endpoint is called
  Then the response is 403 and no market data is disclosed

Scenario: Oversized window is bounded, not served
  When a request would exceed the documented bar limit
  Then the response paginates with meta.has_more and meta.next_cursor
  And never returns an unbounded result set
```

## Technical notes / design
- `param` parsing is a strict whitelist per `bar_type` (bounded integer, or the documented colon grammar), enforcing `maxLength: 24` and rejecting dots, reusing the E12-T01 mapping rather than re-implementing it.
- Reads go through E12-T02's query helpers and E12-T03's spec registry; an endpoint must never construct a builder directly, or the spec cap is bypassed.
- `meta.sources` is assembled from what the read path actually touched, not predicted — a chart that says `questdb` while silently falling back to REST is exactly the dishonesty the spec is written to prevent.
- `generated_at` uses the offset-corrected exchange clock (US-MKT-009), not local wall time.

## Test plan
- **Contract** (generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml`): every documented response and error code, for both endpoints.
- **Unit** ≥85%: param parsing matrix, cursor arithmetic, `meta` assembly, null-vs-zero delta logic.
- **Integration** against a seeded QuestDB + recorded fixtures: each bar type, cache hit, cold-tier read-through, pre-recording refusal.
- **Security**: RBAC matrix (Owner/Manager/Viewer), param fuzzing, oversized-window rejection.

## Security notes
Labelled `security`. Threats: **injection** — `symbol` and `param` reach a query and a SYMBOL column, so parameterised queries and whitelist validation only, never interpolation; **DoS** — unbounded `from/to/limit` or a pathological `param` (`tick:1` over months) triggers unbounded work, so bar caps, window caps, per-user concurrency limits and the E12-T03 spec cap all apply at this boundary; **broken access control** — `marketdata:read` enforced through the shared RBAC dependency, never a hand-rolled check; **information disclosure** — error bodies name the field at fault but never leak internal paths, SQL or `spec_hash` internals. Data classification: public market data, no PII, no secrets, no key material. STRIDE notes feed the Epic-level model.

## Accessibility notes
No UI, but the error `message` fields are rendered verbatim by SCR-042 and SCR-047: they must be human-readable sentences that state what happened and what to do ("Tick bars need recorded trade data; recording for BTCUSDT begins 1 Dec 2026"), never bare codes.

## Performance notes
5 000-bar cache-hit response within the 300 ms first-paint budget of US-MKT-008, measured server-side at p95 and leaving headroom for transport and render. Responses are streamed or chunked for large windows so the server does not materialise the whole set in memory.

## Observability
`http_request_duration_seconds{route="/market/bars"}`, `bars_endpoint_rows_returned`, `bars_endpoint_422_no_data_recorded_total`, `bars_endpoint_param_rejected_total`, `bars_endpoint_source_tier_total{tier}`. Structured logs carry `symbol`, `bar_type`, `param`, `spec_hash` and the tiers touched.

## Definition of Done
Per §4.2: contract tests green against the committed OpenAPI; coverage ≥85%; `22-api-openapi.yaml` amended if the implementation revealed a spec gap; SAST/SCA clean; Security engineer review comment present (this Task is `security`-labelled); QA sign-off; PR merged via the merge queue.

- **E12-T03** — the spec registry and cap the endpoints must go through.
- **E09** — the RBAC dependency and `marketdata:read` permission.

title: Playwright E2E for bar modes, series types and timeframe switching
body:
## Context
Groups 1, 2, 5 and 6 of the E12 black-box plan are user-journey shaped: open a chart, switch type, switch bar mode, switch symbol, change days-to-load, and never see a lie about history. Those journeys cross the WebGL canvas, which is hostile to conventional DOM assertions — a screenshot of a canvas tells you little and is flaky across GPUs (risk **R8**).

The answer, already established by E11's engine work, is that the engine exposes a **deterministic test surface**: the DOM-mirror a11y layer (`SCR-045` data-table alternative) and a diagnostics/state probe (`SCR-046`). This suite drives the real app through Playwright (web and Electron per `03-testing-strategy.md`) and asserts against those surfaces plus normal chrome (`CMP-220 IntervalPicker`, `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle`, `CMP-199 ChartLegend`), not against pixels.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/specs/e12-bars/` Playwright specs implementing the automated cases from `E12-Q01`:
  - `candles.spec.ts` — open `SCR-041` quick-switcher, load BTCUSDT 1 m, assert first/last bar values via the data-table alternative match `GET /market/klines`; forming bar updates without a reload (US-CHART-001).
  - `series-types.spec.ts` — switch candle → OHLC bar → line → area → Heikin-Ashi → baseline; assert no network refetch occurs (request interception) and drawings/anchors stay at the same timestamps (US-CHART-002); assert the volume sub-pane mounts as a linked pane sharing the time axis.
  - `bar-modes.spec.ts` — select tick and volume modes from `SCR-042`, assert the parameter control, the resulting bar count from the data table, and the partial-history marker when the fixture's recording starts mid-window (US-CHART-003).
  - `range-renko.spec.ts` — switch to range/delta/renko, assert the rebuild progress affordance appears and is cancellable, and that an unsupported combination (Heikin-Ashi + footprint) surfaces the documented guard message rather than rendering (US-CHART-004, US-CHART-002 scenario 3).
  - `switching.spec.ts` — hotkey timeframe switch preserves the visible-window centre, no flash of empty chart (assert the skeleton `CMP-029` or prior frame persists), symbol switch without engine teardown (assert the GL context id from `SCR-046` is unchanged) (US-CHART-005).
  - `history-states.spec.ts` — days-to-load control, empty state `SCR-047` naming the first available timestamp, error state `SCR-048` on a stubbed 503, and the `no_data_recorded` 422 path (US-CHART-010, US-MKT-008).
- Deterministic backend: specs run against a **fixture-backed staging profile** that serves the `E12-Q01` tapes, with a frozen clock so bar-close countdowns and the forming bar are reproducible.
- A shared `chartProbe` page-object wrapping the data-table alternative, diagnostics overlay and legend readout, so specs never poke at canvas internals directly.
- Both runners wired: Chromium (web) and the Electron shell, with the Electron run marked required before the R1 exit review.
- Flake controls: no fixed sleeps (only web-first assertions on probe state), per-spec trace-on-failure, and a quarantine list that fails the build if anything sits in it for more than one sprint.

## Out of scope
- Builder-level value correctness (`E12-Q02` owns it); E2E asserts the *plumbing*, spot-checking a handful of values only.
- Frame-rate and memory budgets (`E12-Q05`).
- Keyboard/screen-reader conformance depth (`E12-Q07`) — this suite uses the a11y layer as a probe but does not audit it.
- Drawing tools (E14), indicators (E13), layouts (E15).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Series type switch does not refetch
  Given BTCUSDT 5m is loaded with 5000 bars
  When the user switches from candles to Heikin-Ashi via CMP-222
  Then no request to /market/klines or /market/bars is issued
  And the data-table alternative reports the same bar count with transformed OHLC values

Scenario: Symbol switch reuses the engine
  Given a chart on BTCUSDT with a known GL context id from SCR-046
  When the user switches to ETHUSDT from SCR-041
  Then the GL context id is unchanged
  And the chart never renders an empty grid between the two symbols

Scenario: Failure case - backend error surfaces the error state
  Given /market/klines is stubbed to return 503
  When a chart is opened
  Then SCR-048 is shown with a retry affordance and the failure reason
  And the app does not show an empty chart implying there is no data

Scenario: Edge case - window predates recording for a tick bar mode
  Given ETHUSDT tick:1000 is requested for a window before recording_started_at
  When the chart loads
  Then the partial-history marker is rendered at the recording start
  And the empty region is labelled rather than drawn as flat price

Scenario: Edge case - rebuild is cancellable
  Given a renko brick-size change triggers a rebuild over 1M prints
  When the user cancels mid-rebuild
  Then the previous series remains displayed and no partial series is committed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Use Playwright request interception to assert absence-of-network for client-side transforms — a stronger assertion than visual equality and immune to GPU differences.
- The frozen clock is injected at the app boundary (a test-only clock provider), never by patching `Date` in page context, so the backend and frontend agree on bar boundaries.
- Electron run reuses the same specs via the Playwright Electron launcher; any spec that cannot run in Electron must state why in a comment, per `03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Probe state is read from a stable `data-testid` JSON island emitted by the diagnostics overlay, versioned so a probe-shape change is a deliberate PR, not silent breakage of the suite.

## Test plan
- The suite *is* the test artefact; its own correctness is demonstrated by seeded-failure runs: stub a wrong bar count, a missing partial-history marker, and a teardown-on-symbol-switch, and confirm each fails.
- Run three consecutive green CI passes before marking done, to establish a flake baseline.
- Trace and video retained for failures only, to keep artefact size sane.

## Security notes
- Specs run against staging with a seeded non-privileged test user holding only `marketdata:read`; no live credentials, no live environment, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8's demo/staging rule.
- Fixture responses must not contain account identifiers; the stub server is asserted to serve market data only.
- Any test-only probe (diagnostics JSON island, clock provider) must be compiled out of production builds — add an assertion in this suite that the probe is absent when the app is built in production mode, so a debug surface cannot ship by accident (cross-link `E12-X02`).

## Accessibility notes
- Because the suite drives the DOM-mirror layer, it doubles as a regression guard that the a11y alternative stays wired: if `SCR-045` regresses, these specs fail loudly rather than a11y silently rotting.
- Every interaction in the specs is performed by keyboard where the UI claims keyboard support (interval hotkeys, quick-switcher), so the claimed keyboard paths are exercised on every run.

## Performance notes
- The suite asserts *perceived* behaviour only (no flash of empty chart, skeleton shown, interactive before full history), with generous web-first timeouts; hard budgets are `E12-Q05`'s.
- Total suite wall time target ≤12 minutes on CI in parallel shards.

## Observability
- Each spec tags its run with the build sha and fixture set; results feed the QA run log rolled up in `E12-Q08`.
- On failure, the spec attaches the diagnostics probe JSON and the last 200 lines of backend logs for the fixture server, so triage does not require local reproduction.

## Definition of Done
- All six specs merged and green on Chromium and Electron; three consecutive green runs recorded.
- Seeded-failure evidence attached for at least three scenarios.
- Quarantine list empty at merge time.
- Frontend coverage contribution recorded (E2E does not count toward the ≥80% unit threshold but its journey coverage is mapped to `E12-Q01` case ids).
- Suite documented in the QA plan with how to run locally against fixtures.
- Demo: a live run of `switching.spec.ts` at sprint review.

## Dependencies
- `E12-S01`, `E12-S02`, `E12-S03`, `E12-S05` (the journeys must exist), `E12-Q01` (case ids), E11's diagnostics overlay and DOM-mirror layer.

## Branch
`chore/e12-q03-e2e-bars`

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (E2E layer, Playwright web + Electron)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-001..005, US-CHART-010, US-MKT-008
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-046, SCR-047, SCR-048
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-180, CMP-181, CMP-199, CMP-220, CMP-221, CMP-222, CMP-029
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines`, `/market/bars`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-029, CMP-180, CMP-181, CMP-199, CMP-220, CMP-221, CMP-222, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-046, SCR-047
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**

**Branch & PR**

title: Contract tests for /market/klines, /market/bars and the bars WS topic
body:
## Context
R1's exit criteria freeze the WS protocol: "`23-ws-protocol.md` matches the implementation, contract tests pass, and a deliberate breaking change fails CI". E12 owns two REST endpoints (`GET /market/klines`, `GET /market/bars`) and the `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` topic whose payload is normatively specified in `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.3 `BarsBatch`. E13, E18, E23 and E26 will all build on those shapes; if the implementation drifts from the document, every downstream consumer inherits an undocumented contract (risk **R6 Feed rot**).

This ticket adds schema-driven contract tests that treat the committed documents as the source of truth and the server as the thing under test — in both directions: responses must validate against the schema, and the schema must have no field the server never emits.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **REST contract tests** generated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: every documented response code for `/market/klines` and `/market/bars` (200, 400, 422, 503) exercised against the fixture-backed server, with responses validated against the referenced schemas (`KlineResponse`, `BarType`, `KlineInterval`, `meta.sources`, `meta.recording_started_at`, `meta.next_cursor`/`has_more`).
- Parameter-matrix coverage: every `bar_type` value in the documented table (`time`, `tick`, `volume`, `range`, `delta`, `renko`, `pnf`, `heikin_ashi`) with a valid `param`, plus `include_open`, `include_delta`, `price_type`, `limit` and cursor paging.
- **Documented-error conformance**: a window before `recording_started_at` on a non-time bar type returns `422 no_data_recorded` with the documented error body; an unknown `bar_type` or malformed `param` returns `400`; a store outage returns `503` — asserted by error *code string*, not just status.
- **WS contract tests** for `bars.*`: subscribe, receive snapshot then deltas, validate each frame against `cv://ws/v1/bars.schema.json`; assert `confirm:false` on exactly the forming bar; assert `close_t_ms` present for non-time types and absent-or-consistent for time; assert `coalesced`/`coalesced_count` semantics under a forced slow consumer; assert per-topic sequence numbers increase and a forced gap triggers the documented resync.
- **Schema-drift guard**: a CI job that fails when the server emits a field absent from the schema (`additionalProperties:false` enforced) *and* when a schema field is never observed across the full contract run (dead-contract detection), with an allowlist requiring a comment.
- **Breaking-change canary**: a deliberately breaking mutation (rename `confirm` → `closed`) proven to fail CI, as required by the R1 exit criterion — recorded as evidence.
- Binary framing check: for the binary encoding of `bars.*`, decode frames with the reference decoder and assert field-for-field equality with the JSON fallback encoding of the same update.

## Out of scope
- Transport-level framing, auth handshake, backpressure policy in general — owned by E17; this ticket tests only the `bars` topic's conformance to the frozen envelope.
- Bar value correctness (`E12-Q02`).
- Load and coalescing *performance* (`E12-Q05`); here only the documented coalescing *semantics* are asserted.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every documented response validates
  Given the fixture-backed server
  When the contract suite exercises /market/klines and /market/bars across the full parameter matrix
  Then every response validates against its OpenAPI schema
  And every documented status code is observed at least once

Scenario: WS frames conform to BarsBatch
  Given a subscription to bars.BTCUSDT.time.1
  When a snapshot and 50 deltas are received
  Then every frame validates against cv://ws/v1/bars.schema.json
  And exactly one bar per frame set carries confirm:false

Scenario: Failure case - a breaking change fails CI
  Given the server is patched to emit "closed" instead of "confirm"
  When the contract suite runs
  Then the suite fails naming the offending field and topic
  And the failure message points at 23-ws-protocol.md section 14.3

Scenario: Edge case - pre-recording window on a non-time bar type
  Given a /market/bars request with bar_type=tick and from before recording_started_at
  Then the response is 422 with error code no_data_recorded
  And no REST kline substitution appears in meta.sources

Scenario: Edge case - binary and JSON encodings agree
  Given the same bars update encoded in binary and in the JSON fallback
  When both are decoded
  Then all fields are equal including decimal precision
```

## Technical notes / design
- Generate cases from the spec files at test-collection time rather than hand-transcribing them; a new documented `bar_type` should produce a new test automatically and fail until implemented.
- Decimals are strings end-to-end (`common.schema.json#/$defs/decimal`); the validator must reject a numeric-typed price even if its value is right, because float serialisation is exactly how precision bugs enter.
- Reuse the E17 WS conformance harness rather than building a second client; this ticket contributes the `bars` topic rows to the conformance matrix in `23-ws-protocol.md` §16.
- Run against the fixture server so results are deterministic and the suite can be a required PR check.

## Test plan
- Contract layer per `03-testing-strategy.md`; required check on PRs touching the market-data API surface or the WS bars publisher.
- Negative self-test: three seeded mutations (drop `meta.recording_started_at`, emit a numeric price, omit `close_t_ms` on renko) must each fail.
- Nightly run against the staging server (real store, recorded symbols) to catch drift the fixture server hides.

## Security notes
- Assert `x-rbac: marketdata:read` is actually enforced: an unauthenticated request and a session lacking the permission both receive the documented auth/permission error, never data. This is a contract-level check; deeper RBAC abuse cases live in `E12-X02`.
- Assert input-validation boundaries documented in the spec: `param` maxLength 24 is enforced server-side; `limit` above the documented maximum is rejected rather than honoured (resource-exhaustion guard, `SR-042`-class control).
- Assert `category=linear` is never absent on the upstream Bybit calls made during backfill (SR-054); the fixture server records upstream call shapes for this assertion.

## Accessibility notes
- N/A (protocol-level, no UI). The suite's failure output is plain text with explicit field paths so it is usable by screen-reader users triaging CI.

## Performance notes
- Suite wall time ≤4 minutes so it can gate PRs.
- One coalescing-semantics case uses an artificially slow consumer; it asserts *correctness of the final state*, with throughput measured in `E12-Q05`.

## Observability
- The suite emits a conformance report artefact (endpoint/topic × documented case × pass/fail) that is diffed against the previous run, so newly-skipped coverage is visible.
- Report feeds the R1 protocol-freeze evidence pack referenced by the release checklist.

## Definition of Done
- REST and WS contract suites merged, green, wired as required checks and into nightly.
- Breaking-change canary demonstrated and its evidence attached to this ticket (R1 exit-criterion evidence).
- `23-ws-protocol.md` §16 conformance matrix updated with the `bars.*` rows.
- Dead-contract detection produces an empty allowlist, or each entry carries a justification comment.
- Any spec/implementation divergence found is resolved by changing whichever is wrong — with the decision recorded on the ticket, not silently adjusting the test.
- Demo: show the canary failing CI at sprint review.

## Dependencies
- `E12-T05` (REST endpoints), `E12-T06` (bars WS topic), E17 (WS envelope, binary framing, conformance harness), `E12-Q01`.

## Branch
`chore/e12-q04-bars-contract-tests`

## References

- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §3.1 envelope, §3.4 binary, §7 snapshot+delta, §8 coalescing, §14.3 `BarsBatch`, §16 conformance matrix

title: Performance and load scripts for bar building, backfill and series rendering
body:
## Context
E12 sits on the hot path of two hard R1 exit gates. Budget **#1** (≤16.6 ms p95 frame with 100 k bars loaded) is meaningless unless the series renderer and its LOD/decimation path (`E12-S09`) hold at 100 k bars; budget **#5** (sustain full Bybit cadence with zero dropped messages) is meaningless unless the bar-builder fan-out keeps up while five builders run per symbol. US-CHART-003's NFR adds a concrete throughput claim — "rebuilds of 1 M prints complete in ≤10 s" — and US-MKT-008 adds "≤300 ms to first paint from cache for 5 000 bars".

None of those numbers currently have a script that produces them repeatably. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` requires measurement method, reference hardware and a regression threshold per budget, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes a recorded benchmark mandatory for `perf`-labelled work — which is default-on for `area/chart-engine`. This ticket delivers the scripts and the baselines.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Builder throughput harness** (`bench/bars/throughput.py`): replays a tape of configurable size through the full `BarBuilderSet` (all five families active simultaneously, as a real recorded symbol would run) and reports prints/s, p50/p95/p99 per-print latency, peak RSS and GC pressure. Baseline runs at 100 k / 1 M / 5 M prints.
- **Rebuild benchmark**: end-to-end parameter-change rebuild (`renko:30 → renko:45`, `vol:50 → vol:200`) over 1 M prints, measuring wall time, cancellability latency (time from cancel to released resources) and whether the previous series stayed served throughout — asserting the US-CHART-003 ≤10 s NFR and the `E12-S12` rebuild-strategy decision.
- **Backfill load script** (k6): paged `GET /market/klines` over a 30-day window with concurrent chart opens, measuring p95 REST latency against budget #13 (<150 ms read), page count, and behaviour under a simulated upstream `10018` rate-limit — the backoff must not stall other requests.
- **WS bars fan-out load** (k6/Locust): N clients subscribing to `bars.*` across M symbols, measuring backend fan-out add-on latency against budget #6 (≤20 ms p95), coalescing rate, and slow-consumer behaviour per `SR-073` (bounded queue, conflation, disconnect-on-overflow — never backpressure into ingestion).
- **Engine series benchmark** (extends E11's harness): frame time p95 for each series type (candle, OHLC bar, line, area, Heikin-Ashi, baseline) plus the volume sub-pane, at 10 k / 100 k bars, with and without LOD, on the reference hardware and in Electron — feeding budget #1 and #2 and quantifying what decimation actually buys.
- **Memory soak**: 2 h run with continuous live bars plus periodic symbol/timeframe switching (`E12-S05`), asserting frontend budget #7 (≤1.5 GB) and backend budget #8 (≤300 MB/symbol) and, critically, **no monotonic growth across switches** — the classic leak that a teardown-free engine invites.
- Baseline numbers committed to `bench/bars/BASELINES.md` with hardware, build sha and date; a CI perf job comparing against them and failing on >10 % regression per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §8.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of bars (`E12-Q02`) and of the UI (`E12-Q03`).
- Chaos/failure injection (`E12-Q06`).
- Optimising anything: this ticket measures and gates. Fixes are filed as separate tickets against `E12-S12`/`E12-S09` or E46.
- Footprint/heatmap rendering budgets (#14) — E18/E22 own those, though the harness is shared.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Documented budgets are measured and recorded
  Given the benchmark suite runs on reference hardware
  When all scripts complete
  Then BASELINES.md records p95 frame time per series type at 100k bars, builder throughput at 1M prints, backfill p95 latency and fan-out add-on latency
  And each number names the budget id it maps to in 06-performance-and-load-standard.md

Scenario: Rebuild NFR is enforced
  Given a 1M-print tape and a renko brick-size change
  When the rebuild benchmark runs
  Then the rebuild completes in <= 10 seconds
  And the previously built series remained queryable for the whole rebuild

Scenario: Failure case - a regression fails the perf gate
  Given a change that disables min/max-preserving decimation
  When the CI perf job runs
  Then p95 frame time at 100k bars regresses beyond 10 percent of baseline
  And the job fails naming the series type and the measured delta

Scenario: Edge case - slow WS consumer does not harm ingestion
  Given one subscriber that reads at a tenth of the publish rate
  When the fan-out load script runs
  Then that client's queue conflates and then disconnects on overflow
  And ingestion message-loss counters stay at zero and other clients' latency is unaffected

Scenario: Edge case - repeated symbol switching does not leak
  Given a 2 hour soak alternating between 8 symbols and 4 timeframes
  Then resident memory at the end is within 10 percent of the value after the first full cycle
  And no GL context is created after the first
```

## Technical notes / design
- Reference hardware is the machine defined in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1; runs on other hardware are recorded but never used as gate baselines.
- Frame-time measurement uses the engine's own instrumentation (`requestAnimationFrame` deltas plus GPU timer queries where available), not wall-clock around a render call, so we measure what the user sees.
- The builder harness must run the builders through the production fan-out path, with the same decimal types; a benchmark on a float fast-path would be a lie.
- Warm-up and steady-state windows are explicit: discard the first 5 s, measure the next 60 s, report the distribution not the mean — a p95 gate is only honest with a stated sample size.
- Run each configuration three times and take the median run to damp thermal/scheduler noise; record variance so a flaky gate can be recognised as flaky.

## Test plan
- Self-verification: seeded regressions (disabled decimation, a synchronous rebuild that blocks serving, an unbounded client queue) must each trip the corresponding gate — evidence attached.
- The scripts themselves get unit tests for their reporting math (percentile computation, regression comparison).
- Nightly scheduled run on the reference machine; PR-time run only for the cheap frame-time subset to keep PRs fast.

## Security notes
- Load scripts are pointed at staging only, never live, and carry a guard that refuses to run against a host resolving outside the tailnet staging range — an accidental load test against the live trading stack is a self-inflicted denial of service.
- The slow-consumer scenario doubles as a resource-exhaustion abuse check; its results are handed to `E12-X02` as evidence for the DoS threat rather than being re-derived there.
- Benchmark artefacts must not embed session cookies or tokens; the report scrubber is asserted in a unit test.

## Accessibility notes
- The engine benchmark includes one configuration with `prefers-reduced-motion` emulated, confirming the reduced-motion path (no kinetic scroll) does not itself regress frame time or, worse, get benchmarked as the default and hide a regression in the animated path.
- Benchmark reports are plain markdown/CSV with no colour-only encoding.

## Performance notes
- This ticket *is* the performance work; the budgets it gates are #1, #2, #5, #6, #7, #8, #13 from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.
- Regression threshold is 10 % on p95 for frame time and throughput; latency budgets are absolute, not relative.

## Observability
- Results are pushed to the perf dashboard time-series (build sha as a label) so trends are visible across the R1 train rather than only pass/fail at a point in time.
- Backend runs export `bars_build_duration_seconds`, `bars_rebuild_duration_seconds`, `ws_client_queue_depth`, `ws_client_disconnect_overflow_total` for correlation with the harness's external measurements.

## Definition of Done
- All five scripts merged and runnable with a single command each, documented in `bench/bars/README.md`.
- `BASELINES.md` populated on reference hardware with build sha and date.
- CI perf job wired with the 10 % gate; seeded-regression evidence attached.
- Any budget currently missed is filed as an explicit ticket with the measured gap — not quietly rebaselined.
- Results summarised into the R1 exit-criteria evidence pack.
- Demo: dashboard walkthrough at sprint review showing series-type frame-time comparison.

## Dependencies
- `E12-S05` (backfill), `E12-S09` (LOD/decimation), `E12-Q02` (fixtures), E11 benchmark harness, E17 WS fan-out.

## Branch
`chore/e12-q05-bars-perf`

## References
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #1, #2, #5, #6, #7, #8, #13; §3.1 reference hardware; §8 regression policy
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-001 NFR, US-CHART-003 NFR, US-CHART-005 NFR, US-MKT-008 NFR
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-073
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (LOD tiers)
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criteria 1–2

title: Add line, area, baseline, hollow-candle and Heikin-Ashi series types
body:
## Context
**US-CHART-002 (Should)**: "I want OHLC bars, line, area, Heikin-Ashi and a volume column pane, so that I can read price the way the situation demands." Two of its three scenarios are behavioural rather than visual, and both matter more than the drawing itself:

1. **"the transform is applied client-side with no refetch and drawings stay anchored to real time/price"** — Heikin-Ashi is a *derived view* of the same bars, so switching to it must not touch the network and must not move a single drawing.
2. **"When I request Heikin-Ashi together with footprint cells, then I am told footprint requires a real-price bar type and offered to switch back"** — an incompatible combination must be refused with an explanation and a way out, not silently rendered wrong.

CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle already specifies the control: SegmentedControl semantics, "each option names the chart type in text (icons alone are insufficient)", and footprint as a separate `aria-pressed` toggle because it composes with any base type.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `LineSeries`, `AreaSeries`, `BaselineSeries` and `HollowCandleSeries` as `SeriesPlugin` implementations, using the `line` and `bar` programs of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §4 with instanced thick-line segments.
- Heikin-Ashi as a **client-side transform** over the bound time series: `haClose = (o+h+l+c)/4`, `haOpen = (prevHaOpen + prevHaClose)/2`, `haHigh/haLow` from the extremes, computed incrementally on the worker thread and rendered by the existing candle series — no refetch, no new subscription, no new spec.
- Baseline series with a configurable reference level and distinct above/below fills from theme tokens.
- Chart-type switching within ≤100 ms (US-CHART-002 NFR), preserving the visible time window, the price-scale mode and every drawing's anchor.
- Incompatibility handling: requesting Heikin-Ashi with footprint cells enabled produces an explicit explanatory message offering to switch back, rendered through the design system's inline-message pattern rather than a toast that disappears.
- CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle wired to the engine, with every option named in text.

## Out of scope
- Volume column pane — E12-S08.
- Footprint cells themselves — E18 (this Story only implements the refusal when the two are combined).
- Compare/overlay symbol (US-CHART-011) — E15/E11 scope.
- Server-side Heikin-Ashi bar construction — HA is deliberately not a `BarSpec.kind`; it is a view transform.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Heikin-Ashi switches without a refetch
  Given a BTCUSDT 5m candle chart with three drawings
  When I switch to Heikin-Ashi
  Then no network request is made
  And the transform is applied within 100 ms
  And every drawing remains anchored to its original time and price

Scenario: Heikin-Ashi maths is correct and incremental
  Given a known bar sequence with a known HA reference output
  Then the computed HA series matches the reference exactly
  And appending one new bar updates only the last HA bar rather than recomputing the series

Scenario: Incompatible combination is explained, not rendered wrong
  Given footprint cells are enabled
  When I select Heikin-Ashi
  Then I am told footprint requires a real-price bar type
  And I am offered to switch back, with that offer reachable by keyboard
  And the chart continues to render the previous valid combination meanwhile

Scenario: Every type is named in text
  Given the chart-type toggle
  Then each option's accessible name states the chart type in words
  And the footprint toggle is a separate control with aria-pressed, not an option in the same group

Scenario: Baseline series honours its reference
  Given a baseline series with the reference set to the session open
  Then values above and below render with distinct fills from theme tokens
  And the distinction is not conveyed by colour alone
```

## Technical notes / design
- HA is computed on the worker thread against the columnar store, writing into a derived typed-array view rather than a copied series, so memory does not double at 100k bars.
- The HA recurrence depends on the previous HA bar, so a windowed view must seed from a deterministic warm-up point (a fixed number of bars before the visible window) and document it — otherwise scrolling changes the values, which is a classic and very visible HA bug.
- Line/area/baseline share the `line` program; area and baseline add a fill quad strip. Keep each series at its documented draw-call budget so the ≤18-call pane target survives.
- Drawings must not move: they anchor to real time/price, and the HA transform changes only the rendered geometry, never the anchor space.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: HA recurrence against a reference dataset, warm-up seeding, incremental append, baseline reference handling, line/area geometry.
- **Golden image** (SwiftShader): each series type in both themes, plus baseline above/below.
- **E2E** (Playwright + Electron): switch through every chart type with drawings present; assert no network request on the HA switch, assert drawings unmoved, assert the incompatibility message appears and is keyboard-dismissible.
- **Perf**: chart-type switch timed against the 100 ms budget at 100k bars.
- **a11y**: axe-core on SCR-042 and the toggle; manual screen-reader pass confirming type names and the footprint toggle's separate semantics.

## Security notes
No new data path, no new inputs from the network — this Story consumes bars already validated at the store boundary by E12-S06. The only new surface is the chart-type preference persisted per pane (E15/E12-S12 own persistence); it is an enum, validated against the known set on load so a tampered stored workspace cannot select an arbitrary renderer.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-222's contract is binding: SegmentedControl semantics, every option named in text (icons alone insufficient), footprint as a separate `aria-pressed` toggle. The incompatibility message must be an inline, persistent, keyboard-reachable message with an actionable control — not a transient toast, which a screen-reader user may never perceive. Baseline above/below and HA up/down must be distinguishable without colour (fill pattern or outline), per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. The data-table alternative must state which chart type is active, and for HA must make clear the values shown are derived, not traded prices.

## Performance notes
Chart-type switch ≤100 ms (US-CHART-002 NFR) including the HA transform at 100k bars. No additional GPU memory beyond the derived HA view. Frame budget #1 unchanged — these series must not push a pane over 16.6 ms p95.

## Observability
`series_type_switch_duration_ms` histogram labelled by target type; `series_incompatible_combination_total{combination}` so a frequently attempted illegal combination becomes a product signal rather than a repeated user annoyance.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario backed by an automated test; frontend coverage ≥80%; golden images committed; switch-time benchmark recorded; axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass on the type toggle; design-QA pass against the CMP-222 spec; QA sign-off; demoed; feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S06** — the candle series and the `SeriesPlugin` binding that HA renders through.
- **E05 / E11-T04** — theme tokens and LUT ingestion for baseline/area fills.

## Branch
`feat/e12-series-types`

title: Render the volume column sub-pane linked to the price pane
body:
## Context
US-CHART-002's second scenario: "When I enable the volume column pane, then it renders as a linked sub-pane sharing the time axis and crosshair." It is the smallest possible exercise of E11's multi-pane stacking (E11-S09) with a real data series in it — which makes it valuable out of proportion to its size, because it proves the pane-linking contract works before E13's indicator panes and E23's CVD panes depend on it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A volume column series rendered in a linked sub-pane below the price pane, sharing the time axis, the visible range, the crosshair and the pan/zoom state via E11's pane-sync mechanism.
- Per-bar colouring from the bar's direction (up/down close) or from delta when `include_delta` data is present, always from theme tokens.
- Independent autoscale for the sub-pane's own value axis, with the shared time axis rendered once (the sub-pane does not duplicate time labels).
- Toggle on/off from the chart toolbar, with the pane's presence and height persisted per chart (persistence lands via E12-S12's chart settings).
- Correct behaviour on non-time-aligned series: volume columns follow the same index spacing as the bricks/range bars above them.
- Empty/partial handling: bars with null volume (kline-sourced pre-recording windows do carry volume, but tick-derived fields may be null) render honestly rather than as zero.

## Out of scope
- Volume moving average and OBV — **E13** indicators.
- Volume profile (horizontal) — **E19**.
- The Deep-Stats strip — **E20**.
- Pane stacking and sync machinery itself — **E11-S09**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Linked sub-pane shares the time axis
  Given the volume pane is enabled
  When I pan or zoom the price pane
  Then the volume pane follows exactly, with no drift at any zoom level
  And the time axis is drawn once, beneath the lowest pane

Scenario: Crosshair is shared
  When the crosshair moves over the price pane
  Then the volume pane shows the corresponding vertical position
  And the readout includes the volume for that bar

Scenario: Columns follow index spacing on renko
  Given a renko series
  Then volume columns align one-to-one with bricks by index
  And a brick with volume_allocated=false renders a zero-height column rather than a gap or an interpolated value

Scenario: Toggling does not disturb the price pane
  When I enable or disable the volume pane
  Then the price pane's visible range and price scale are unchanged
  And the layout reflows without a visible flash of empty chart

Scenario: Null volume is not shown as zero
  Given a bar whose volume is unavailable
  Then the column is omitted and the state is stated in the readout as unavailable
  And it is not drawn as a zero-height column implying no trading
```

## Technical notes / design
- The sub-pane uses the `bar` program with instanced quads — one draw call. It must not add a second time-axis renderer; the shared axis belongs to the pane stack (E11-S06).
- Autoscale for volume is independent of price autoscale but must respect the same lock/unlock affordances so the interaction model is consistent (E11-S05).
- Renko's `volume_allocated=false` bricks are the interesting case: zero-height is correct and intentional, and the tooltip/readout should say the volume is attributed to a neighbouring brick so the user is not confused by the visual.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: column geometry, direction/delta colour selection, null-volume handling, index-spacing alignment.
- **Golden image**: volume pane with time bars and with renko bars, both themes.
- **E2E**: toggle the pane, pan/zoom, assert sync; crosshair readout includes volume.
- **a11y**: axe-core; the data-table alternative includes a volume column and states unavailability in text.

## Security notes
No new inputs beyond the bars already validated at the store boundary. Defensive check: a negative or non-finite volume is rejected rather than producing an inverted or infinite column geometry.

## Accessibility notes
The volume pane must appear in the DOM mirror and the SCR-045 data table as a column, not only as pixels; the crosshair readout announces volume alongside OHLC within the ≤2/s live-region throttle of US-CHART-008. Up/down colouring must not be the only signal — the readout states the value in text. The pane toggle has a text name ("Volume pane") and its pressed state is programmatically exposed.

## Performance notes
One additional draw call and one instance buffer; must not push the pane stack over the ≤40 draw calls documented for a 3-pane chart, nor the p95 frame budget of 16.6 ms. Pane toggle reflow must not trigger a full data re-upload.

## Observability
Draw-call and frame-time attribution for `series.volume` in `FrameStats`, visible in the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: scenarios automated; coverage ≥80%; golden images committed; axe-core green; data-table integration verified; design-QA pass; QA sign-off; demoed; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S07** — the series-type work and toolbar wiring.
- **E11-S09** — multi-pane stacking and sync; this Story is its first real consumer.

## Branch
`feat/e12-volume-pane`

## References

title: Decimate series by LOD tier with hysteresis and min/max spike preservation
body:
## Context
US-CHART-001's second scenario is the one that decides whether the custom engine was worth building: "Given 100 000 bars are in the series, when I zoom to fit, then rendering stays at or above 55 fps using level-of-detail aggregation, **and the aggregation level is indicated**."

`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 defines the candle ladder — L0 full OHLC bodies+wicks at `barSpacing ≥ 3 px`, L1 bodies only at `≥ 1.5 px`, L2 a min/max column strip (one column per pixel) below that — and states the rule that makes this a correctness ticket rather than an optimisation: **"Decimation for candles at L2 uses a min/max preserving reduction (per pixel column emit min-low, max-high, first-open, last-close) so spikes never disappear — a correctness requirement, not a cosmetic one."** A decimation that averages or samples will hide the exact wick a trader zoomed out to find.

§3.6 also requires **±15% hysteresis** on the thresholds so slow zooming does not flicker between levels.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The three-tier candle LOD ladder with the documented `barSpacing` thresholds and ±15% dead-band hysteresis.
- Min/max-preserving reduction at L2: per pixel column emit min-low, max-high, first-open, last-close — never an average, never a sample.
- Incremental/cached aggregation: LOD buckets computed off the main thread against the columnar store and reused across frames; a pan of one column must not recompute the whole window.
- Aggregation-level indication in the UI (US-CHART-001's explicit requirement) — a text affordance stating the current level and that bars are aggregated, surfaced in the chart chrome and in the accessible readout, not merely in the diagnostics overlay.
- Correct interaction with non-time-aligned series (index-spaced renko/range decimate by index).
- Correct interaction with the forming bar: the last bar is never merged into an aggregate in a way that hides its live movement (E12-S10 depends on this).
- Benchmark scenarios added to E11-T06's harness at 5k / 50k / 100k bars across all three tiers, wired as a CI gate.

## Out of scope
- Footprint, heatmap, profile and bubble LOD ladders — E18/E19/E21/E22 (each has its own row in §3.6).
- Memory governor and eviction — E11-S15.
- The diagnostics overlay itself — E11-T07.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Spikes survive decimation
  Given a series containing a single-bar wick far outside its neighbours
  When the view is zoomed until that region occupies one pixel column
  Then the rendered column still reaches the extreme high and low
  And a property test over random series confirms the rendered extremes equal the true extremes for every pixel column

Scenario: Frame budget at 100k bars
  Given 100 000 bars zoomed to fit
  Then the p95 frame time stays within 16.6 ms and the frame rate at or above 55 fps on the reference GPU
  And the benchmark result is recorded by the CI gate

Scenario: Hysteresis prevents flicker
  Given barSpacing is hovering at the L0/L1 threshold
  When the user zooms slowly back and forth across it
  Then the level changes only after the plus or minus 15 percent dead band is exceeded
  And no per-frame level oscillation occurs

Scenario: The aggregation level is indicated
  Given the view is at L2
  Then the chart states in text that bars are aggregated and at what level
  And that statement is available to assistive technology, not only as a visual badge

Scenario: The forming bar is never hidden by aggregation
  Given the last bar is still forming
  When the view is at L2
  Then the forming bar's live movement remains visible rather than being frozen into an aggregate bucket

Scenario: Index-spaced series decimate by index
  Given a renko series at L2
  Then aggregation buckets are formed by brick index
  And no time-based bucketing is applied to a series with isTimeAligned=false
```

## Technical notes / design
- L2 buckets are keyed by device-pixel column, so they must be recomputed when the DPI or the pane width changes — but not on every pan. Cache by (first index, bars-per-column) and slide the window.
- Aggregation runs on the worker thread against the typed-array store (E11-T02/T03), writing into a reusable output buffer with no per-frame allocation.
- Hysteresis state lives with the pane, not globally, so two panes at different zooms behave independently.
- The min/max reduction is the single most test-worthy function in the engine: it deserves a dedicated property test (rendered extremes == true extremes for all columns) rather than only golden images, because a golden image of a decimated chart is very hard to read by eye.

## Test plan
- **Property** (primary gate): for random series and random zoom levels, the rendered per-column extremes equal the true extremes of the underlying bars — the anti-spike-loss invariant.
- **Unit** ≥80%: threshold selection with hysteresis, bucket keying, cache invalidation on DPI/width change, index-vs-time bucketing.
- **Golden image** per tier on SwiftShader, plus a dedicated spike fixture.
- **Perf**: 5k / 50k / 100k bars × 3 tiers in the E11-T06 harness, gated in CI with a >10% regression failing the build.
- **E2E**: zoom from L0 to L2 and back; assert the aggregation indication appears and that no flicker occurs across the threshold.

## Security notes
No new external input. The one robustness concern is a pathological bar count or a degenerate pane width (zero or negative after a resize) producing a division by zero or an unbounded bucket loop — clamp both and cover with tests, since a hung render loop is a client-side DoS at the worst possible moment for a trader.

## Accessibility notes
"The aggregation level is indicated" is an accessibility requirement as much as a product one: when bars are aggregated, the data-table alternative (SCR-045) and the crosshair readout must state that the values shown are aggregated and over how many bars, so a screen-reader user is not given decimated values as though they were per-bar truth. The indication is text, never a colour or an icon alone. Live-region announcements remain within the ≤2/s throttle of US-CHART-008.

## Performance notes
This Story *is* the mechanism by which budget #1 (p95 ≤16.6 ms) and US-CHART-001's ≥55 fps at 100k bars are met. GPU memory stays under the 512 MB per-pane cap because L2 uploads one instance per pixel column rather than per bar. Aggregation cost must be amortised: a full-window recompute is permitted on zoom, not on pan.

## Observability
`FrameStats` gains `lodTier` and `aggregatedBarsPerColumn`, surfaced in the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay and in the CI benchmark output. `series_lod_transitions_total{from,to}` to detect flicker regressions in the field.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: the anti-spike-loss property test green; every scenario automated; coverage ≥80%; golden images committed; CI perf gate wired and baselines recorded; axe-core green and the aggregation indication verified with a screen reader; design-QA pass on the indication affordance; QA sign-off; demoed (zoom to 100k bars); PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S06** — the candle series being decimated.
- **E11** — columnar stores, worker protocol, benchmark harness (E11-T06), golden-image harness (E11-T08), DPI handling (E11-S10).

## Branch
`feat/e12-series-lod`

## References

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-001 (scenario 2), US-CHART-008

title: Show the forming bar distinctly from closed bars with a live countdown
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 gives this Story its reason to exist in one sentence: **"Unconfirmed bars. The last bar in any `bars`/`footprint` frame may have `confirm: false`. A client MUST NOT treat it as closed — this is the flicker bug Bybit's own `confirm` flag exists to prevent."** The same discipline appears in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`include_open` + `confirm`) and in `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1 (`Bar.closed`).

The trading consequence is concrete: a rule that fires `on_bar_close`, an indicator that computes on close, or a trader reading a completed pattern must all agree on *when* a bar is closed. A UI that renders a forming bar identically to a closed one invites a trader to act on a pattern that has not happened yet.

US-CHART-001 also requires that "the forming bar updates on every trade **without a full redraw**", and US-CHART-008 requires the bar-close countdown (CMP-226) that "turns amber in the final 10 seconds".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Consumption of the `bars` WS topic (E12-T06): snapshot application, delta application by sequence, and resync on a gap — with the forming bar patched in place rather than appended.
- Visual distinction of the forming bar per the design spec (E11-D02 chassis + this Epic's design tickets): a distinct treatment that is **not colour-only**.
- Patch-only updates: a forming-bar tick mutates one instance in the store and redraws, never re-uploading or re-decimating the series.
- Bar-close countdown via CMP-226 for time-aligned series: text, 1 Hz, `aria-live="off"` by default, amber warn state that adds a word rather than only a colour; hidden (not zeroed) for non-time-aligned series where no close time can be predicted.
- Transition on close: when `confirm` flips to true, the bar settles into the closed treatment and the next bar opens, with no flicker and no duplicated bar.
- Amended-bar handling: a re-emitted closed bar (late trade, `amended=true` from E12-S01) updates in place and is announced as a correction rather than silently changing under the user.
- Stale-feed handling: if the topic stops delivering, the forming bar is marked stale rather than continuing to display as live (mirroring US-MKT-003's "grey out with a stale marker rather than showing frozen values as if live").

## Out of scope
- The WS topic implementation — E12-T06.
- Crosshair readout layout — E11-S07 (this Story supplies the forming/closed fact it displays).
- `on_bar_close` rule semantics — E35.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Forming bar is visibly and programmatically distinct
  Given the last bar has confirm=false
  Then it renders with the forming treatment
  And that distinction is not conveyed by colour alone
  And the accessible readout for that bar states that it is still forming

Scenario: Updates patch, not rebuild
  Given 20 trades update the forming bar in one second
  Then only the last instance in the store is mutated
  And no full series re-upload or re-decimation occurs
  And the frame budget is unaffected

Scenario: Close transition is clean
  Given the forming bar's interval boundary passes
  When the close frame arrives with confirm=true
  Then that bar settles into the closed treatment exactly once
  And a new forming bar opens
  And no duplicate bar appears at the same open time

Scenario: Countdown behaves
  Given a 5m time series
  Then the countdown shows seconds remaining as text, updating at 1 Hz
  And in the final 10 seconds it adds a warning word in addition to any colour change
  Given a renko series
  Then no countdown is displayed, because no close time can be predicted

Scenario: Amendment is surfaced, not silent
  Given a closed bar is re-emitted with amended=true after a late trade
  Then the bar updates in place
  And the change is surfaced to the user rather than mutating silently

Scenario: Stale feed is not shown as live
  Given the bars topic stops delivering for longer than the staleness threshold
  Then the forming bar is marked stale in text
  And it is not presented as a live value
```

## Technical notes / design
- The forming bar must be excluded from LOD aggregation buckets that would freeze it (E12-S09's corresponding scenario) — the two Stories share this contract and it is tested from both sides.
- Countdown time comes from the offset-corrected exchange clock (US-MKT-009), not the browser clock; a browser clock skew would show a countdown that disagrees with the actual bar close.
- Resync after a sequence gap must not duplicate the forming bar: applying a fresh snapshot replaces the tail rather than appending to it.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: snapshot/delta application, forming-bar patching, close transition, amended handling, staleness detection, countdown formatting and warn threshold.
- **Integration**: against a scripted WS fixture replaying a real bar-close sequence including a gap and a resync.
- **E2E** (Playwright + Electron): watch a live-ish 1m bar close on a fixture feed; assert exactly one closed bar and one new forming bar.
- **Perf**: forming-bar update path measured to confirm no re-upload and no frame-budget impact at 100k bars.
- **a11y**: axe-core; manual screen-reader pass confirming the forming/closed distinction and that the countdown does not flood announcements.

## Security notes
The client must not trust frame ordering blindly: apply deltas strictly by sequence, reject out-of-order or duplicate sequences, and resync rather than merging speculatively — a malformed or replayed frame must not be able to fabricate a bar state. Beyond that, no credentials or secrets are handled in this path.

## Accessibility notes
This is a case where a wrong visual is a trading hazard, so the forming/closed distinction must be available in three ways: the visual treatment (not colour-only), the accessible readout for the focused bar ("forming" / "closed"), and the SCR-045 data table's per-row state. CMP-226's contract is binding: text rather than a bare progress ring, 1 Hz updates, `aria-live="off"` by default so it never floods a screen reader, and the warn state adds a word, not just a colour. Amendment notifications must be polite, not assertive.

## Performance notes
A forming-bar update is a single instance patch plus a redraw; it must not trigger re-decimation, re-upload or a scene rebuild. US-CHART-001's "updates on every trade without a full redraw" is the acceptance condition, verified by an instrumented counter in the benchmark rather than by eye.

## Observability
`bars_forming_updates_applied_total`, `bars_ws_resyncs_total` (client side), `bars_stale_seconds` gauge, `bars_amendments_surfaced_total`. Frame attribution confirms the patch path does not re-upload.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario automated; coverage ≥80%; axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass on the forming/closed state and the countdown; design-QA pass on the forming treatment; perf assertion that no re-upload occurs; QA sign-off; demoed (watch a bar close); feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T06** — the `bars` WS topic supplying snapshots, deltas and the `confirm` flag.
- **E12-S06** — the candle series being patched.
- **E11-S07** — the crosshair/readout and countdown placement in the chassis.

## Branch
`feat/e12-forming-bar`

## References
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 (unconfirmed bars), §7 snapshot+delta
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines` `include_open`/`confirm`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1 (`closed`), §3.3 (amended late trades)
