title: Switch symbol and timeframe without tearing down the engine
body:
## Context
**US-CHART-005 (Must)**: "I want to switch intervals from 1 s to 1 D including custom intervals, so that context and execution timeframes are one keystroke apart", with NFRs of **≤200 ms from cache** and **"no flash of empty chart"**. Symbol switching (US-MKT-002: "the focused chart pane switches symbol and the search closes") has the same requirement.

The roadmap scopes this explicitly for E12: "symbol + timeframe switching **without a full engine teardown**". That constraint is what makes 200 ms possible — recreating a WebGL context, re-uploading the theme LUT and rebuilding the scene graph costs far more than the budget, and a teardown/rebuild is also how the "flash of empty chart" happens.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Re-binding the existing engine instance and pane stack to a new series: unsubscribe the old `bars` topic, subscribe the new one, swap the columnar store contents, keep the GL context, programs, LUTs, scene graph and pane layout intact.
- Cache-first switching: an already-cached (symbol, spec) window paints from the local store immediately, with only the tail fetched.
- Visible-window preservation: on an interval change, the **centre** of the visible time window is preserved (US-CHART-005 scenario 1); on a symbol change, the time window is preserved and the price scale re-autoscales to the new symbol's range.
- Drawings and indicators re-anchored by timestamp, not by bar index, so they land correctly on a different interval.
- The interval ladder of US-CHART-005: standard intervals 1 s … 1 D via hotkeys, sub-minute intervals built from recorded prints (with the partial-history marker when recording is shallower than the view), and custom intervals (e.g. 7m) aggregated from 1m data and added to a recent list.
- SCR-041 quick-switcher and CMP-219 SymbolPicker / CMP-220 IntervalPicker wired to the engine, keyboard-first.
- Delisted-symbol handling per US-MKT-001: the chart shows a delisted banner rather than an empty chart.
- Loading state: the previous series stays visible with a loading affordance until the new one is ready — never an empty pane.

## Out of scope
- Bar-mode switching and parameter-change rebuilds — E12-S12.
- Symbol search itself (US-MKT-002's fuzzy matching and ranking) — E08/E10 scope; this Story consumes the selection event.
- Watchlist (US-MKT-003) and layouts/sync groups (E15).
- Chart templates (US-CHART-012) — E15.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Interval switch from cache is fast and centred
  Given a BTCUSDT 1m chart with 5m bars already cached
  When I press the 5m hotkey
  Then the chart switches within 200 ms
  And the centre of the visible time window is preserved
  And no WebGL context is created or lost

Scenario: No flash of empty chart
  Given a switch that requires a network fetch
  Then the previous series remains visible with a loading affordance
  And at no point is an empty pane or an axes-only grid displayed

Scenario: Drawings re-anchor by time
  Given a trend line drawn on the 1m chart
  When I switch to 5m
  Then the line connects the same timestamps and prices
  And it is not shifted by the change in bar index

Scenario: Symbol switch keeps the engine
  Given a BTCUSDT chart with indicators and drawings
  When I switch to ETHUSDT from the quick-switcher
  Then the same engine instance re-binds
  And the price scale re-autoscales to the new symbol
  And BTCUSDT's bars topic is unsubscribed after the grace period

Scenario: Sub-minute interval with shallow recording
  Given the recorder holds less history than the requested 5 s view
  When I select 5 s
  Then bars are built from the available prints
  And a partial-history marker names where recorded data begins

Scenario: Custom interval
  When I enter 7m
  Then bars are aggregated from 1m data
  And 7m is added to my recent-intervals list

Scenario: Delisted symbol
  Given the selected symbol is no longer trading
  Then the chart renders the available history with a delisted banner
  And order entry for it is disabled
```

## Technical notes / design
- Re-binding must be atomic from the user's perspective: build the new store contents, then swap in one frame. A partial swap is what produces a flash or a frame of mixed data.
- Unsubscribe uses the 30-second grace of US-MKT-005 so a rapid A→B→A switch does not thrash subscriptions.
- Drawings anchor in (time, price) space already (E14's model); this Story must simply avoid re-anchoring them to index — but it must be tested explicitly because index-anchoring is the easy accidental implementation.
- Custom intervals aggregate client-side from 1m only when the requested interval is an exact multiple; otherwise a distinct server-side spec is registered. State which path was taken in the diagnostics.
- The LOD cache (E12-S09) is keyed per series and must be invalidated on re-bind without discarding the GL resources it lives in.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: window-centre preservation maths, cache-hit decision, custom-interval aggregation eligibility, recent-intervals list behaviour.
- **E2E** (Playwright + Electron): the full switch matrix — cached/uncached × interval/symbol — asserting timing, no context loss (instrument `webglcontextlost`), no empty-pane frame, and drawing anchors unchanged.
- **Perf**: switch timed at p95 against the 200 ms budget with 100k bars loaded; a counter asserts zero GL context recreations.
- **a11y**: axe-core on SCR-041/SCR-042; keyboard-only switch path verified; focus returns to the chart after the switcher closes.

## Security notes
The symbol arriving from the switcher is validated against the instrument catalogue before any subscription or request is made — an arbitrary symbol string must never reach a topic name or a query (the same whitelist discipline as E12-T05/T06, enforced client-side too so a malformed request is not even sent). Unsubscribing reliably on switch also matters for resource fairness: a client that leaks subscriptions across switches is a slow-motion DoS against its own backend budget.

## Accessibility notes
Switching is a keyboard-first flow: CMP-219 and CMP-220 follow the combobox/menu-button patterns with the current value readable without opening the popover, and CMP-220 presents bar modes as a separate labelled group. After a switch, focus must return to the chart canvas (not be lost to the body), and the new symbol/interval must be announced once politely — not on every subsequent data update. The partial-history and delisted states are text. The loading affordance must not be a colour-only or motion-only signal, and must respect reduced-motion.

## Performance notes
≤200 ms switch from cache (US-CHART-005 NFR) at 100k bars; zero WebGL context recreations; no re-upload of theme LUTs, shaders or glyph atlas; GPU memory must not grow across repeated switches (a leak here is the classic re-bind bug — assert stable memory over a 100-switch loop).

## Observability
`chart_switch_duration_ms{kind="symbol"|"interval",cache="hit"|"miss"}`, `chart_switch_context_recreations_total` (must stay zero), `ws_subscription_churn_total`, GPU memory gauge sampled across switches.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario automated; coverage ≥80%; switch-time and memory-stability benchmarks recorded; axe-core green plus a keyboard-only and screen-reader pass on the switcher; design-QA pass against SCR-041/SCR-042; QA sign-off; demoed; feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S09** — the LOD cache that must be invalidated and rebuilt on re-bind.
- **E12-S10** — live subscription lifecycle for the `bars` topic.
- **E08 / US-MKT-001** — the instrument catalogue for validation and delisted status.

title: Publish the bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param} WS topic with snapshot and deltas
body:
## Context
Charts update live over the multiplexed client WebSocket frozen by **E17**. `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 defines the topic precisely: `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`, options `include_delta` and `history` (≤1 000), snapshot = the last `history` bars, throttle 250 ms, **binary kind 4**, payload `BarsBatch` (§14.3). Two notes in that section are load-bearing: `param` follows the REST convention exactly (dots illegal, colons for compound values), and **"the last bar in any `bars` frame may have `confirm: false`. A client MUST NOT treat it as closed — this is the flicker bug Bybit's own `confirm` flag exists to prevent."**

This Task adds the topic to the already-frozen transport; it changes no framing, no sequencing and no backpressure policy. That is the entire point of E17 shipping first.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Topic registration for `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` with option validation (`include_delta`, `history` ≤1 000) and `param` parsing reusing E12-T01's mapping.
- Snapshot on subscribe: the last `history` bars from the E12-T05 read path, followed by deltas with per-topic sequence numbers per §7.
- Delta publication driven by `BarUpdate`s from E12-T03's emit routing — one source for live and replay.
- `BarsBatch` binary encoding (kind 4) per §14.3, with the JSON fallback path.
- 250 ms coalescing: within a window, repeated updates to the same forming bar collapse to the latest; a `close` update is never coalesced away (a closed bar must always be delivered).
- `confirm: false` on the forming bar, `true` on closed bars, matching the REST semantics exactly.
- Gap-driven resync: a sequence break triggers a fresh snapshot per §7, without inventing bar-specific resync semantics.
- Subscribe-time authorisation (`marketdata:read`) and the spec-cap check from E12-T03.
- Conformance tests generated from `23-ws-protocol.md` §16's matrix for this topic.

## Out of scope
- Transport, framing, heartbeats, backpressure, auth handshake — **E17**.
- `footprint.*` topic — E18.
- Client-side subscription management and rendering — E12-S10/S11.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Snapshot then deltas
  Given a client subscribes to bars.BTCUSDT.time.5 with history=500
  Then a snapshot of the last 500 bars is delivered first
  And subsequent frames are deltas carrying monotonically increasing sequence numbers

Scenario: Forming bar is flagged
  Given the current 5m bar is still forming
  Then it is delivered with confirm=false in every frame
  And when its boundary passes it is delivered exactly once with confirm=true

Scenario: Coalescing never drops a close
  Given 40 trades update the forming bar within one 250 ms window
  Then one coalesced update is sent carrying the latest state
  Given a bar closes and a new one opens within the same window
  Then the close update is still delivered, not collapsed into the open

Scenario: Sequence gap triggers resync
  Given a client detects a non-contiguous sequence number
  When it requests resync per the protocol
  Then a fresh snapshot is delivered and the sequence restarts per section 7
  And no bars are silently missing from the client's series

Scenario: Illegal param is refused at subscribe
  When a client subscribes to bars.BTCUSDT.tick.500.extra
  Then the subscription is refused with the documented protocol error
  And no builder is registered

Scenario: Unauthorised subscribe is refused
  Given a connection whose principal lacks marketdata:read
  When it subscribes to any bars topic
  Then the subscription is refused and no data frames are sent
```

## Technical notes / design
- Dots are illegal in `param` because the topic namespace is dot-delimited; `atr:14` and `10:3` use colons for exactly this reason (§6.1). Validation must reject the dot case explicitly, since a permissive parser here is a namespace-injection bug.
- `bars` and `footprint` for the same `(symbol, bar_type, param)` are **separate subscriptions with independent sequences**, guaranteed consistent (same builder) but not frame-synchronised; the client keys them by bar open time. Nothing here may assume otherwise.
- Publication is fan-out from one `BarBuilderSet` — N subscribers to the same spec share one builder, which is what keeps real-time cost (risk R3) bounded.

## Test plan
- **Contract/conformance**: generated from `23-ws-protocol.md` §16 for this topic; a deliberate breaking change to the payload must fail CI (roadmap exit criterion 7).
- **Unit** ≥85%: option validation, coalescing logic including the never-drop-a-close rule, sequence assignment, binary encode/decode round-trip.
- **Integration**: subscribe/unsubscribe lifecycle, snapshot correctness against the REST endpoint for the same window, resync after an injected gap.
- **Load** (k6, per §5.4): 5 concurrent WS clients × 10 symbols sustained 1 h with bars topics subscribed; fan-out add-on ≤20 ms p95.

## Security notes
Labelled `security`. Threats: **topic-namespace injection** via `param` (closed by the dot/whitelist rule above); **resource exhaustion** via many distinct specs per connection (closed by the E12-T03 spec cap, checked at subscribe, plus a per-connection topic cap from E17); **broken access control** (subscribe-time `marketdata:read`, re-checked on token refresh/revocation per §9, so a revoked session stops receiving frames rather than continuing on an established socket); **amplification** — `history=1000` × many topics on one subscribe frame is a bandwidth amplifier, bounded by E17's ≤10 topics per subscribe frame rule and the history cap.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — transport. One downstream contract: `confirm` must reach the client unmodified, because the data-table alternative (SCR-045) states "forming" versus "closed" in text for each bar, and that text is only as honest as this flag.

## Performance notes
Throttle 250 ms per §6.1; WS→screen p95 ≤250 ms (US-MKT-005) and the R1 exit criterion of tick→screen p95 <100 ms for last-trade applies to the `trades`/`ticker` topics rather than `bars`, but the bars path must not consume the shared budget: coalescing is mandatory, not optional. Binary kind 4 keeps per-bar overhead low at `history=1000` snapshots.

## Observability
`ws_topic_subscriptions{topic="bars"}`, `ws_bars_frames_total`, `ws_bars_coalesced_updates_total`, `ws_bars_resyncs_total`, `ws_bars_subscribe_rejected_total{reason}`, `ws_publish_latency_seconds{topic="bars"}`.

## Definition of Done
Per §4.2: conformance tests generated and green; a deliberate breaking change fails CI; coverage ≥85%; `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1/§14.3 matches the implementation; load test recorded; Security engineer review comment; QA sign-off; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T05** — the read path supplying snapshots.
- **E12-T03** — the emit routing supplying deltas and the spec cap.
- **E17** — the frozen transport, sequencing, backpressure and auth handshake this topic rides on.

## Branch
`feat/e12-bars-ws-topic`

## References
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 topic catalogue and notes, §7 snapshot+delta, §8 throttling/coalescing, §9 revocation, §14.3 `BarsBatch`, §16 conformance matrix
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` param convention

title: Design QA of the built bar modes, series rendering and their states
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA a default-on Done gate for net-new UI: "built screen compared against design spec (spacing/tokens/type/color/states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer; discrepancies either fixed or filed as follow-up Bug with `priority/*` set".

E12 needs this more than most epics, because most of what it delivers is **drawn by a renderer rather than composed from DOM components**. A token drift in a React button is caught by visual regression; a candle body that is one pixel too wide at 3 px spacing, a wick that disappears below a certain zoom, an aggregated mark that does not match the specified geometry, or a forming-bar treatment that is invisible at 1 s — none of those are caught by anything except a designer looking at the built product against the E12-D06 geometry rules on the reference hardware.

This ticket runs that pass at the end of the epic's build window (Sprint 08, after the Sprint 05–08 stories land) against the handoff pack from E12-D12.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- A design-QA pass over every E12 surface in the built application: `SCR-030` series states, `SCR-031` General tab, `SCR-041`, `SCR-042`, `SCR-045`, `SCR-047`, `SCR-048`.
- **Geometry verification** against E12-D06: body width, wick width, minimum mark height, zero-range bar, gap treatment and the aggregated mark, sampled at every step of the density ladder (≥8 px, 4–8 px, 2–4 px, 1–2 px, <1 px), captured as screenshots on the reference machine at 2560×1440.
- **Per-mode verification**: candle, hollow candle, OHLC bar, line, area, baseline, Heikin-Ashi, equi-volume, delta-volume × time, tick, volume, range, delta, Renko and P&F — sampled per the risk-based matrix agreed with QA rather than exhaustively, with the sampling rationale recorded.
- **State verification**: forming vs closed, LOD-aggregated with its indicator, partial-history boundary, gap, rebuilding with progress and cancel, empty (all four `SCR-047` reasons), error (all three `SCR-048` classes).
- **Token/spacing/type audit** of the DOM surfaces in both themes and both densities, against the handoff pack's token manifest.
- **Copy audit**: every mode description, validation message, empty-state and error-state string matches the approved copy exactly — including the catalogue's fixed strings ("Needs recorded ticks", "No USDT perpetual matches 'xyz' — v1 supports linear perpetuals only.", "Values below one tick are not allowed.").
- **Motion verification** against E12-D10, including the reduced-motion path.
- A findings list with severities; each finding fixed within the epic or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*` label and a named owner, per the DoD.
- A sign-off record on the E12 epic ticket enumerating what was checked, what passed and what was deferred.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of bar construction (does a 500-tick bar actually close after 500 trades) — that is the engineering and QA tickets' job; this pass is about whether the built result matches the design.
- Performance benchmarking as a gate (owned by the E12 perf work and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13) — though this pass records anything visibly janky as a finding.
- Footprint, profiles, indicators and drawings (their own epics' design QA).
- Backend, API and WS verification.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E12 surface is compared against its spec
  Given the built application is available on the reference machine
  When the design-QA pass is executed
  Then SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-047 and SCR-048 are each compared against the handoff pack
  And a pass or fail with evidence is recorded per surface

Scenario: Geometry matches the specified rules at every density
  Given the density ladder from E12-D06
  When the built chart is sampled at each step
  Then measured body and wick widths match the specified formulas within the stated tolerance
  And the aggregated mark below one pixel spacing matches the specified appearance

Scenario: A discrepancy is fixed or filed, never absorbed (edge)
  Given a discrepancy is found that cannot be fixed before the epic closes
  When it is triaged
  Then a Bug is filed with a priority label, an owner and a reference to the specific spec line it violates
  And the E12 epic sign-off record lists it as a known deferral rather than omitting it

Scenario: Copy has drifted during implementation (failure)
  Given a validation message in the built product differs from the approved copy
  When the copy audit runs
  Then the difference is recorded verbatim, both versions shown
  And either the build is corrected or the catalogue is updated with CDO approval, so the documentation and the product agree

Scenario: The forming bar is invisible on fast intervals (failure)
  Given a one-second interval on a busy symbol
  When the forming-bar treatment is inspected in the built product
  Then it is distinguishable from a closed bar without relying on motion or colour alone
  And if it is not, a P1 finding is raised against the implementing story
```

## Technical notes / design
- Run on the **reference machine at 2560×1440**, the configuration `SCR-030`'s budgets are stated against, and in all the runtimes R1 cares about (Chromium and the Electron shell). A design-QA pass on a designer's laptop at a different DPR measures nothing about the geometry rules, which are DPR-sensitive.
- Verify device-pixel-ratio handling explicitly (`CMP-180` owns DPR); a rule that is correct at DPR 1 and wrong at DPR 2 is a real and common defect in canvas renderers.
- Use real recorded fixtures, including one quiet symbol and one busy symbol, so the sparse and dense cases are both seen.
- Sample rather than exhaust: the full cross-product of chart types × bar modes is large, so agree a risk-based matrix with QA (every bar mode at least once; every chart type at least once; the highest-risk intersections — Renko, P&F, equi-volume, delta-volume — explicitly).
- Measure, do not eyeball, for geometry: capture screenshots and measure pixels against the formulas, with a stated tolerance.
- Where the built product is *better* than the spec, say so and update the spec — design QA is a two-way gate, not only a compliance check.

## Test plan
- Execute the pass against the handoff pack surface by surface, recording evidence (screenshots, measurements) per check.
- Re-run the E12-D11 screen-reader script against the built product in collaboration with QA/SDET; deviations are findings here as well as in the QA tickets.
- Verify the Storybook states listed in the handoff manifest actually exist and match, since they are the visual-regression baseline going forward.
- Verify axe-core is green on the touched DOM surfaces (a DoD requirement for the consuming stories) and record it.
- Reduced-motion pass: confirm no information is lost and no suppressed transition leaves an inconsistent end state.
- Both themes, both densities, and the Electron floating-panel case (`SCR-027`) for the popover surfaces.

## Security notes
- Verify that RBAC-gated affordances behave as designed in the built product: the "Record this symbol" action is absent for manager/viewer and the explanatory copy is present instead.
- Verify that error states expose no internal detail (no stack traces, hostnames or upstream URLs) and that correlation ids contain no account identifiers or tokens.
- Perform the pass against a demo/test account only; no live keys or live account data are used, and screenshots attached to findings are scrubbed of account context.

## Accessibility notes
- Re-verification of the E12-D11 script against the built product is part of this pass; findings are raised against the implementing stories.
- Check the non-negotiables in the built product: visible focus everywhere, no hover-only functionality, no colour-only direction or state encoding (verified in greyscale), disabled menu items focusable and announcing their reason, and `SCR-045` reachable from the chart panel header rather than buried in settings.
- Confirm announcement throttling in practice on a 1 s interval — the worst case for flooding.
- Any a11y finding that prevents a user from reading chart data is P0 and blocks the epic's Done.

## Performance notes
- This is not the performance gate, but visible jank, dropped frames during mode switches, or transitions that fail to drop under load are recorded as findings and cross-referenced to the E12 perf work and `SCR-046` diagnostics.
- Confirm that the aggregation indicator's stated level agrees with the diagnostics overlay's visible-bar/aggregation values, since the handoff pack requires them to agree.

## Observability
- Verify the analytics manifest was implemented: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed`, `chart.symbol_changed`, `chart.settings_changed`, `chart.empty_state_shown` with `{reason}`, `chart.error_shown` with `{code, correlationId}`, `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`, and the rebuild start/complete/cancel events — each fires at the designed trigger with the designed properties.
- A missing or mis-propertied event is a finding, because an unmeasured rebuild duration means the 10 s budget cannot be policed in production.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) and the §3.2 `design-qa` gate.
- Pass executed across all seven surfaces with evidence attached.
- Every finding fixed or filed as a Bug with `priority/*` and an owner; none absorbed silently.
- Copy audit differences resolved in either direction, with `14-screens-catalogue.md` updated where the product legitimately diverged.
- Sign-off record posted on the E12 epic ticket listing checked/passed/deferred.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done** — required before the E12 epic can be marked Done.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D12 (the handoff pack this pass tests against).
- Requires the E12 frontend stories from Sprint 05–08 to be merged and deployable to the QA environment; if any are incomplete at Sprint 08, the pass covers what exists and the remainder is explicitly deferred with a named follow-up.
- Coordinates with the E12 QA tickets (shared screen-reader script and state matrix as oracles).

## Branch
`design/e12-design-qa` — findings, evidence and any catalogue corrections; no application code (fixes land on the implementing stories' branches).

## References
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 (design-qa, a11y, QA sign-off)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-027, SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-046, SCR-047, SCR-048
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-180, CMP-181, CMP-220, CMP-222, CMP-226
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 (benchmarks and performance gates)
- E12-D06 (geometry rules), E12-D10 (motion), E12-D11 (a11y pack), E12-D12 (handoff pack)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)

title: Publish the bar-semantics reference and ADR addendum for downstream epics
body:
## Context
Six epics downstream of E12 (E13 indicators, E18 footprint, E19 profiles, E23 CVD, E26 replay, E37 rule node-graph) will each make assumptions about what a bar *means*: when it opens and closes, what `confirm` guarantees, whether a rebuild can change history under them, what happens at the recording boundary, and whether non-time bars are wall-clock comparable. Today that knowledge is distributed across `21-database-schema.md` §4.8, the `BarsBatch` schema, two OpenAPI descriptions and the heads of the five people who wrote the builders — which is exactly the shape of risk **R10 Key-person** and a reliable source of R7 data-accuracy bugs.

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 also requires epic docs to reflect *shipped* behaviour, not the original proposal, wherever implementation diverged. E12 diverged in at least the rebuild-strategy decision (`E12-S12`) and the details settled during `E12-Q02`/`E12-Q04`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A single normative reference `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` addendum (or a new `docs/plan/25-bar-semantics.md`, whichever the Architect prefers — decided in review) covering, per bar family (time, tick, volume, range, delta, renko, plus the Heikin-Ashi transform):
  - exact open/close conditions, including the inclusive/exclusive boundary convention and overshoot-splitting rules;
  - what `t_ms`, `close_t_ms` and `open_source_ts` mean per family and which are populated;
  - empty-interval, late-trade, duplicate and out-of-order semantics;
  - `confirm` semantics and the forming-bar contract ("a client MUST NOT treat it as closed");
  - `build_version` and rebuild semantics: when history can legitimately change, how consumers detect it, and what they must invalidate;
  - the recording boundary: `recording_started_at`, the `no_data_recorded` 422, and why REST klines are never substituted for non-time bars;
  - which fields are null before recording starts (delta, CVD, min/max delta) and why.
- The **consumer guarantees table** from `E12-X04`'s consumer note, folded in as the canonical version so there is one place to read it.
- An ADR addendum recording the rebuild/cache-invalidation decision as built (extending `E12-S12`'s ADR), including the alternatives rejected and the measured numbers from `E12-Q05` that justified the choice.
- Doc corrections where the implementation and the plan diverged: `21-database-schema.md` §4.8, `22-api-openapi.yaml` descriptions, `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.3 notes, `24-internal-schemas.md` BarSpec/Bar — each updated to as-built, with the change noted in the PR description.
- Cross-links added from the E13/E18/E19/E23/E26/E37 epic tickets to the reference.

## Out of scope
- Writing new builder behaviour; this is documentation of what exists. Any divergence discovered that looks like a *bug* rather than an undocumented decision is filed as a defect, not documented as intended.
- Operator runbooks for recording/retention (E16).
- User-facing help content (E48/E49 docs epics).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every bar family is fully specified
  Given the merged reference document
  When it is checked against the six bar families plus the Heikin-Ashi transform
  Then each has open/close conditions, timestamp field semantics, edge-case handling and confirm semantics
  And each statement is traceable to a golden fixture case in E12-Q02

Scenario: Docs match the shipped implementation
  Given the as-built corrections to 21-, 22-, 23- and 24- documents
  When the contract suite E12-Q04 runs
  Then no documented field or behaviour contradicts the implementation

Scenario: Failure case - an undocumented divergence is a defect not a doc edit
  Given the author finds the volume builder closes bars at >= threshold while the plan says >
  Then a defect is filed against the owning ticket
  And the reference is not quietly written to match the code

Scenario: Edge case - a downstream engineer can design without asking
  Given an E26 replay engineer reads the consumer guarantees table
  Then they can determine whether a rebuild can change bars under a paused replay
  And the answer is stated explicitly rather than implied
```

## Technical notes / design
- Every normative statement should name the fixture case that demonstrates it (`E12-TC-*` or the golden pair), so the document is verifiable rather than assertive — this is what stops it drifting the moment someone changes a builder.
- Keep it a reference, not a tutorial: tables and precise conditions, no narrative walkthroughs that will rot.
- Decide document placement in review; the deciding factor is whether bar semantics belong to the engine design (client-side view) or deserve their own backend-facing document. Record the decision in the PR.

## Test plan
- Doc-lint (link check, heading structure) in CI.
- Review by the Architect, the E12 tech lead and one engineer from a downstream epic (E18 or E26) — the downstream reviewer is the real test: if they can design against it without asking a question, it works.
- Cross-check every documented claim against `E12-Q02` goldens and `E12-Q04` contract cases; any claim without backing evidence is removed or turned into a test.

## Security notes
- The document restates the data classification (public market data) and the evidence-integrity guarantee signed off in `E12-X04`, so a future author does not weaken bars handling on the assumption that it is "just chart data".
- Explicitly documents that there are no bar checksums (per ADR-0005) and what that means for consumers that need integrity assurance — an unstated absence is how false assumptions form.
- No secrets, endpoints or credentials in the document; fixture references are by name, not by URL.

## Accessibility notes
- Follows repo docs conventions: proper heading hierarchy, tables with header rows, no colour-only encoding, mermaid diagrams paired with a text description so diagram content is available to screen-reader users.

## Performance notes
- Includes the measured rebuild and throughput figures from `E12-Q05` as the documented expectations, so downstream epics size their own work against real numbers rather than guesses.

## Observability
- Documents the metric and log-field names a consumer or operator should watch when bars look wrong (`bars_gap_detected_total`, `bars_rebuild_total`, `build_version` in logs), so debugging a downstream data question starts from a known place.

## Definition of Done
- Reference merged at the agreed location; ADR addendum merged in `27-adrs/`.
- As-built corrections landed in `21-`, `22-`, `23-`, `24-` docs; divergences that were bugs filed as defects instead.
- Reviewed by Architect, E12 lead and a downstream-epic engineer.
- Cross-links added from the six consumer epic tickets.
- Doc-lint green; every normative claim traceable to a fixture or contract case.
- Changelog fragment: N/A — no user-facing effect (stated explicitly per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §7.2).

## Dependencies
- `E12-Q02` (goldens as evidence), `E12-Q04` (contract truth), `E12-X04` (consumer note and sign-off), `E12-S12` (rebuild ADR to extend).

## Branch
`docs/e12-k02-bar-semantics`

- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines`, `/market/bars`

title: Chaos scenarios for bar building: feed gaps, store outages and clock skew
body:
## Context
Bar builders are fed by a live exchange connection and write to a store; both fail routinely. Bybit drops WS connections, returns 5xx, rate-limits with `10018`, and occasionally delivers prints out of order; QuestDB restarts; the host clock drifts (US-MKT-009 alarms above 500 ms). The planning brief lists chaos/failover tests as non-negotiable, and `04-security-program.md` W6/O9 treat exchange responses as untrusted input.

The specific danger for E12 is not a crash — it is **quiet corruption**. A gap in the tape that is not surfaced produces bars that look plausible and are wrong, and those bars become the evidence base for footprint, CVD and replay. This ticket injects the failures and asserts that every one of them either self-heals with correct data or is *visibly* marked, never silently absorbed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A chaos harness (`tests/chaos/bars/`) built on a controllable fake-Bybit WS/REST server plus container-level fault injection for the store, with scenarios:
  1. **WS disconnect mid-bar** — connection drops while a volume bar is half-full; on reconnect assert the builder resumes correctly from the store or marks the affected window as gapped.
  2. **Sequence gap in the trade stream** — a deliberate gap; assert detection, resubscribe/backfill of the missing window, and that the resulting bars either match the golden or are flagged partial. No silent fill.
  3. **Out-of-order and duplicate prints** — a print older than the last processed one and a duplicate `trade_id`; assert the documented ordering/dedup semantics and volume conservation.
  4. **Exchange 5xx and `10018` rate-limit during backfill** — assert exponential backoff with jitter, that the partial result stays usable and interactive (US-MKT-008 scenario 3), and that no reconnect storm trips the 500-connections/5 min IP limit (W6/`SR-039`).
  5. **QuestDB restart / write failure** — assert writes buffer or fail loudly, no bar is acknowledged as persisted when it was not, and recovery replays the buffered window exactly once (no duplicate bars — dedup per `E12-T02`).
  6. **Clock skew** — host clock jumped forward and backward by 2 s and 2 minutes; assert time-bar boundaries follow exchange-time offset (US-MKT-009), that a backward jump does not emit a bar with a `t_ms` before its predecessor, and that the drift alarm fires.
  7. **Mid-rebuild interruption** — kill the process during a renko rebuild; assert no partially-written `build_version` is served and the rebuild restarts cleanly.
  8. **Delisted / halted symbol** — symbol status leaves `Trading` mid-session; assert the delisted banner and that builders stop rather than emitting empty bars forever.
- For each scenario: expected user-visible outcome on the chart (marker, banner, stale badge), expected metric/alert, and expected log line — all asserted, not just described.
- A `chaos-report.md` template recording run date, build, scenario, observed behaviour, and any gap filed.

## Out of scope
- Recorder retention/compaction failures (E16) and replay determinism (E26).
- Order-path chaos (E45 owns reconciliation/failover for trading).
- Kernel/network-level fault injection beyond container controls.
- Fixing what is found: defects are filed against the owning child ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A tape gap is never silently filled
  Given the fake exchange omits 30 seconds of prints from the stream
  When the builders process the surrounding window
  Then the gap is detected and the window is backfilled or marked partial
  And bars covering the gap are never emitted as if complete

Scenario: Store restart does not duplicate or lose bars
  Given QuestDB is restarted while bars are being written
  When the system recovers
  Then the persisted bar set equals the golden for that window exactly once
  And no bar was reported to clients as confirmed before it was durable

Scenario: Failure case - backward clock jump
  Given the host clock jumps 2 minutes backwards
  When time bars continue to be built
  Then no bar is emitted with an open time earlier than the previous bar
  And the clock-drift alarm is raised and visible on the health screen

Scenario: Edge case - rate limited backfill stays usable
  Given the exchange returns 10018 for every third kline page
  When a 30-day backfill runs
  Then backoff with jitter is applied and the chart stays interactive with partial data
  And the loading affordance states that older bars are still arriving

Scenario: Edge case - interrupted rebuild leaves no half-written series
  Given the process is killed at 60 percent of a renko rebuild
  When it restarts
  Then no client is served bars from the incomplete build_version
  And the rebuild resumes or restarts and ultimately matches the golden
```

## Technical notes / design
- Fault injection is deterministic and scripted (fake exchange with a scenario DSL), not random; randomised soak is a later E45 concern. Deterministic chaos is reproducible chaos, which is the only kind worth gating on.
- Reuse the golden fixtures from `E12-Q02` as the ground truth every scenario is compared against — the point of chaos testing here is "do we still equal the golden, or do we visibly say we can't".
- Scenario 6 needs the container clock manipulated (`libfaketime` or a clock-provider seam), never the host clock.
- Each scenario asserts three layers: data (bars vs golden), UX (marker/banner state via the `E12-Q03` probe), and ops (metric/alert/log).

## Test plan
- Run the full set nightly on staging-like infrastructure; a subset (scenarios 2, 3, 6) runs on PRs touching ingestion or builders because they are fast and catch the highest-frequency regressions.
- Each scenario must first be demonstrated to *fail* against a deliberately naive implementation (e.g. a builder without gap detection), proving the assertion has teeth.
- Results recorded in `chaos-report.md` and rolled into `E12-Q08`.

## Security notes
- Scenarios 2, 3 and 4 are availability/integrity threats from a semi-trusted external system (`04-security-program.md` AC-08, O9, W6); results are shared with `E12-X01`'s STRIDE model as mitigation evidence.
- Assert that malformed exchange payloads (wrong types, absurd sizes, negative prices) are rejected at the boundary with a typed error and a counter, never fed into a builder — untrusted-input handling per `SR-040`.
- The fake exchange must never be reachable from a production config; the harness asserts the endpoint override is test-only.

## Accessibility notes
- Every degraded state this ticket exercises must be perceivable non-visually: the partial-history marker, stale badge and delisted banner are asserted to be announced in a live region and to carry text, not colour alone — degraded states are exactly where colour-only signalling tends to creep in.

## Performance notes
- Assert that recovery paths do not blow budgets: post-reconnect catch-up must not exceed the steady-state CPU budget (#11) by more than 2x for more than 30 s, and must not stall the render loop below the 30 fps floor (budget #2).
- Backoff timings are asserted to be bounded (no unbounded retry storm) and jittered.

## Observability
- Each scenario asserts a specific signal: `ws_reconnect_total`, `ws_topic_gap_total`, `bars_gap_detected_total`, `backfill_rate_limited_total`, `clock_offset_ms`, `store_write_failed_total`, `bars_rebuild_aborted_total`.
- Gaps in observability discovered here (a failure with no signal) are filed as tickets — an unobservable failure mode is itself a defect.

## Definition of Done
- All eight scenarios implemented, passing, and each demonstrated to fail against a naive implementation.
- Nightly job wired; PR subset wired.
- `chaos-report.md` from one full run attached.
- Any missing metric/alert/UX affordance filed with a priority and linked here.
- Findings handed to `E12-X01` and `E12-Q08`.
- Demo: scenario 2 (tape gap) shown live at sprint review, including the user-visible marker.

## Dependencies
- `E12-T02` (persistence/dedup/build_version), `E12-T06` (bars WS topic), `E12-Q02` (goldens), E17 (WS lifecycle), E16 (recorder), US-MKT-009 clock offset service.

## Branch
`chore/e12-q06-bars-chaos`

## References
- `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` (chaos/failover non-negotiable)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (chaos layer)
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` AC-08, O9, W6, SR-038, SR-039, SR-040
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-MKT-008, US-MKT-009, US-CHART-003

title: Accessibility audit of bar-mode, series and interval surfaces
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes WCAG 2.2 AA default-on for every UI surface with no "it's a chart, a11y doesn't apply" exception, and `05-accessibility-standard.md` is the normative reference. E12 introduces surfaces that are genuinely hard: a WebGL canvas with no DOM (`CMP-180`/`CMP-181`), a menu whose options change availability based on recording depth (`SCR-042`), a long-running cancellable rebuild, and a "forming vs closed bar" distinction that is conveyed visually by a subtle outline.

E11 provides the DOM-mirror layer and the `SCR-045` data-table alternative; E12 must prove that every bar type and series type it adds is actually represented there, and that its chrome is operable and announced. This ticket is the audit that produces that proof — axe-core automation plus the manual screen-reader passes that automation cannot replace.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated axe-core sweep** in CI over the E12 surfaces: `SCR-041` quick-switcher, `SCR-042` interval/bar-mode menu, `SCR-043` scale context menus (series-relevant items), `SCR-044` go-to-date, `SCR-045` data-table alternative, `SCR-047` empty state, `SCR-048` error state, plus `CMP-199` legend, `CMP-220` IntervalPicker, `CMP-221` ChartToolbar, `CMP-222` ChartTypeToggle, `CMP-029` skeleton.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** on NVDA + Chrome and VoiceOver + Safari/Electron, scripted and recorded, covering:
  - switching series type and hearing the new type announced (US-CHART-002 NFR: "each type has an accessible name in the type selector");
  - opening `SCR-042`, hearing which bar modes are unavailable **and why** ("tick bars unavailable: recording starts 4 September") rather than a bare disabled control;
  - hearing rebuild progress and being able to cancel it from the keyboard, with completion announced;
  - reading a bar row in `SCR-045` for each of the six bar families and confirming non-time bars expose both open and close time;
  - the forming-bar state being announced as text ("bar forming, 42 seconds to close"), never conveyed by outline alone.
- **Keyboard-only traversal** of every E12 journey: no mouse, including interval hotkeys, quick-switcher, type toggle, days-to-load control, rebuild cancel, and escape-to-close semantics on every menu; focus order and visible focus states checked against `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- **Contrast and non-colour-encoding checks** for the series palettes in light and dark themes: up/down candles, baseline above/below, Heikin-Ashi bodies, volume sub-pane bars, partial-history marker — each must meet contrast requirements and carry a non-colour cue in the accessible representation.
- **Reduced-motion** verification: with `prefers-reduced-motion`, series transitions and rebuild progress animation degrade to non-animated states without losing information.
- An audit report listing every finding with WCAG SC reference, severity, and the ticket filed; blocking findings (anything that makes a bar mode unusable or a value unavailable non-visually) must be fixed before epic sign-off.

## Out of scope
- Auditing the engine's core a11y layer itself (E11 owns `SCR-045`'s architecture); this ticket audits E12's *contribution* to it and files against E11 if the substrate is at fault.
- Drawing tools (E14), indicators (E13), layouts (E15) a11y.
- Full-app audits — E43/E46 own the epic-spanning sweeps.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E12 surface passes automated checks
  Given the axe-core sweep runs in CI over the listed screens and components
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations
  And any moderate violation carries a filed ticket and an agreed disposition

Scenario: Every bar family is readable without sight
  Given a screen-reader user opens the SCR-045 data-table alternative
  When they read a row for time, tick, volume, range, delta and renko series
  Then each row exposes open time, close time where applicable, OHLC and volume as text
  And the forming bar is identified as forming in text

Scenario: Failure case - an unavailable bar mode explains itself
  Given tick bars are unavailable because recording is shallower than the requested window
  When a screen-reader user focuses that option in SCR-042
  Then the reason is announced along with the disabled state
  And the user is offered the available window rather than a dead end

Scenario: Edge case - keyboard-only rebuild cancel
  Given a renko parameter change has started a long rebuild
  When the user tabs to the cancel affordance and activates it with the keyboard
  Then the rebuild is cancelled and the outcome is announced in a live region
  And focus returns to the control that started the rebuild

Scenario: Edge case - reduced motion loses no information
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is enabled
  When a series type is switched and a rebuild runs
  Then no animated transition plays and progress is still conveyed as text or a static indicator
```

## Technical notes / design
- Automated checks run against the same fixture-backed staging profile as `E12-Q03`, reusing its page objects so a screen's route is defined once.
- Manual passes follow a written script with expected utterances, so two testers produce comparable results and a regression is recognisable; recordings are attached.

- Regression guard: the keyboard-only journeys are encoded as Playwright specs contributed back into `E12-Q03`, so they run continuously rather than only at audit time.

## Security notes
- The accessible data-table alternative exposes the same market data as the canvas and no more; the audit explicitly checks it does not surface fields the RBAC scope would otherwise withhold (e.g. delta/CVD on a symbol without recorded tape must be absent, not null-rendered as 0).
- Screen recordings from manual passes are reviewed for incidental disclosure (account names, tokens in the URL bar) before attachment.

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket *is* the a11y work; the standard is WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
- Verify the DOM-mirror layer stays windowed for the series sizes E12 introduces: at 100 k bars the accessible table must not materialise 100 k rows, and the audit measures its node count and update cost so a11y does not become the thing that breaks budget #1.

## Observability
- axe-core results are published per build so violation counts trend over time rather than being a one-off snapshot.
- Manual pass outcomes are recorded in the QA run log consumed by `E12-Q08`.

- axe-core sweep green (zero serious/critical) and wired as a required check.
- Both manual screen-reader passes executed, recorded and attached.
- Audit report merged with every finding carrying a WCAG SC id, severity and disposition; all blocking findings fixed or explicitly waived by the CDO with reason.

title: Exploratory charters, E12 regression pack and epic QA sign-off
body:
## Context
Scripted tests find the failures we thought of. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires an **epic-level** regression and exploratory pass before an Epic can be Done — not merely the sum of child-ticket QA — and §8 requires a recorded sign-off. E12's risk profile makes this more than ceremony: bar semantics interact combinatorially (bar type × parameter × recording depth × symbol precision × theme × replay), and the combinations nobody wrote a case for are precisely where an off-by-one hides.

This ticket runs time-boxed exploratory charters against a release-candidate build, assembles the durable regression pack that future epics will re-run, and produces the QA sign-off artefact that gates E12 Done and feeds the R1 exit review.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (90 minutes each, session-based test management notes recorded per charter):
  1. *Parameter abuse* — extreme and silly bar parameters: `tick:1`, `vol:0.00000001`, `range:1` on a wide-tick symbol, `renko:atr:14` on a symbol with 3 days of history, `param` at exactly 24 characters. What does the UI do? What does the API do?
  2. *Precision & exotic symbols* — symbols with unusual tick/lot sizes and very high or very low prices; check rounding, axis labels, renko brick alignment to tick size, and that no value is rendered with float artefacts.
  3. *Switching storm* — rapid symbol/timeframe/bar-mode switching, including switching mid-rebuild and mid-backfill; hunt for stale data bleeding between symbols, orphaned subscriptions and leaked GL resources.
  4. *History boundary honesty* — every combination of recording depth vs requested window vs bar type; the charter's question is "can I make the app show me data it does not have, or hide data it does have?".
  5. *Cross-feature interference* — E12 bars under E13 indicators and E14 drawings where already available: do drawings re-anchor by timestamp after a rebuild (US-CHART-004 scenario 3), do indicators recompute on type switch?
  6. *Theme, density and locale* — light/dark, compact/comfortable, non-English number formats and a non-UTC display timezone against the configured day boundary (US-CHART-009).
- **Regression pack**: the subset of `E12-Q01` cases plus exploratory-derived cases that must be re-run for every future change touching bars — packaged as a tagged suite (`@e12-regression`) runnable in one command, with a documented expected runtime and an owner.
- **Bug triage & rollup**: all defects found across `E12-Q01`..`E12-Q07` collected with severity, status and the child ticket they belong to; the sign-off states explicitly that no P0/P1 remains open against E12's scope.
- **QA sign-off document** (`qa/signoff/e12.md`): per-story pass/fail, coverage numbers per touched package against the ≥85 % backend / ≥80 % frontend thresholds, perf numbers vs budgets, a11y status, chaos results, open risks and any accepted deviations — with named signatories (SDET + E12 tech lead) and date.
- Contribution of E12's rows to the R1 exit-criteria evidence pack.

## Out of scope
- Fixing defects found (filed against the owning tickets).
- Security sign-off (`E12-X04`) — referenced in the QA document, owned separately.
- Full-train regression across all R1 epics (E46/release management owns that).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All six charters are executed and recorded
  Given a release-candidate build of E12
  When each charter is executed for its full time-box
  Then session notes record the areas covered, bugs found, issues and time split
  And every bug found is filed with severity and owning ticket

Scenario: Epic sign-off states the truth about coverage and budgets
  Given qa/signoff/e12.md is prepared
  Then it records per-story pass/fail, package coverage percentages, measured perf numbers against budget ids, axe-core status and chaos results
  And any item that is not green carries a named disposition rather than being omitted

Scenario: Failure case - an open P0 blocks sign-off
  Given an open priority/p0-critical defect against bar values
  When sign-off is attempted
  Then sign-off is refused and the epic cannot move to Done
  And the blocking defect is named in the document

Scenario: Edge case - the regression pack is actually runnable by someone else
  Given an engineer who did not build the pack
  When they run the @e12-regression suite from the documented command
  Then it completes within the documented runtime and reports per-case results
  And no step requires undocumented local setup

Scenario: Edge case - exploratory finds an uncovered combination
  Given charter 4 discovers a history-boundary case no scripted test covers
  Then a new case is added to qa/plans/e12-bars-and-series-test-plan.md and to the regression pack
  And its automation is filed as a follow-up ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Charters follow session-based test management: charter statement, time-box, areas covered, test notes, bugs, issues, and a session debrief — this keeps exploration accountable without scripting it.
- Run against a release-candidate build with fixture-backed *and* real recorded data; some defects (precision, exotic symbols) only appear against real instrument metadata.
- The regression pack must be tagged rather than copy-pasted, so a case fixed in the main plan is automatically fixed in the pack.
- Timebox discipline matters: six charters is nine hours of tester time and is deliberately scoped to fit one SDET-week alongside the sprint's other QA load.

## Test plan
- This ticket is itself a test-execution ticket; its verification is the recorded artefacts: six session sheets, a green regression-pack run, and a completed sign-off document reviewed by the E12 tech lead.
- The regression pack is proven by a clean-machine run by a second person.

## Security notes
- Charter 1 (parameter abuse) overlaps the abuse cases in `E12-X02`; findings are cross-posted there rather than duplicated, and anything that looks like an injection, traversal or resource-exhaustion vector is escalated to Security immediately rather than filed as a normal defect.
- Sign-off explicitly references `E12-X04`'s security sign-off status; QA sign-off alone does not clear the epic.
- Any exploratory session touching real recorded data uses staging with a `marketdata:read`-only account; no live environment, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8.

## Accessibility notes
- Charter 6 includes at least one screen-reader-assisted pass so a11y is exercised in exploration, not only in the scripted audit.
- The sign-off document records the a11y status from `E12-Q07` verbatim, including any CDO waiver, so a reader does not have to chase it.

## Performance notes
- Charter 3 (switching storm) is deliberately adversarial about resource leaks; the tester watches the diagnostics overlay (`SCR-046`) and backend metrics during the session and records any monotonic growth, escalating to `E12-Q05` for a measured run.
- The sign-off records measured numbers against budgets #1, #2, #5, #6, #7, #8, #13, not a pass/fail claim without evidence.

## Observability
- Every session sheet records the build sha, environment and fixture set so a finding can be reproduced months later.
- Sign-off results and the regression-pack run feed the R1 exit-criteria evidence pack and the release checklist in `07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Definition of Done
- Six charter sessions executed and recorded; all findings filed.
- `@e12-regression` pack tagged, documented, proven on a clean machine by a second person.
- `qa/signoff/e12.md` merged with named signatories and zero open P0/P1 against E12 scope.
- Uncovered combinations found by exploration added to the test plan with automation follow-ups filed.
- R1 evidence-pack rows contributed.
- Demo: sign-off walkthrough at the sprint review, including any accepted deviations stated out loud.

## Dependencies
- All of `E12-Q02`..`E12-Q07`; `E12-X04` for the security status referenced in the sign-off; a release-candidate build of E12's stories.

`chore/e12-q08-signoff`

title: Select bar mode and parameters with a cancellable rebuild and history markers
body:
## Context
This Story is where the backend builders become a product feature. **US-CHART-003** ("Given I select 'volume bars, 1 500 contracts'…") and **US-CHART-004** ("When I change the brick or range size, then the series rebuilds from stored prints **with a progress indicator** and drawings re-anchor by timestamp") both terminate here, and both carry the NFR **"rebuild is cancellable; parameters persisted per chart template"**.

It is also where the product's honesty rules become visible. Two facts must be stated in text, never inferred: **where tick-accurate history begins** (US-CHART-003 scenario 3: "an explicit partial-history marker shows where tick data begins") and **that the x-axis no longer means clock time** for non-time-aligned modes (CMP-220's a11y contract: bar modes are "a separate labelled group with an explanatory note, since they change the meaning of the x-axis").

## Scope / Deliverables
- SCR-042 interval / bar-mode menu built on CMP-220 IntervalPicker + CMP-041 Menu: the time ladder, then a separately labelled bar-mode group (tick / volume / range / delta / renko) with the explanatory note and a CMP-069 InfoPanel describing what each mode does.
- Parameter entry per mode (trades per bar, base volume, ticks, delta threshold, brick size) with validation against the documented bounds from E12-T01/S02/S03/S04, showing the limit in the message when a value is rejected.
- Rebuild flow: changing a mode or parameter registers the new spec, shows determinate progress while the series rebuilds from stored prints, and **can be cancelled** — cancellation stops the backend rebuild (the mechanism chosen by ADR-0014) and restores the previous series.
- Drawings re-anchored by timestamp across the rebuild (they must not move).
- Partial-history marker: an explicit, text-stated boundary on the chart and in the empty/partial state (SCR-047) naming the timestamp where tick-accurate data begins, plus the `no_data_recorded` path when the whole window predates recording.
- Persistence of the bar mode and its parameter per chart via `chart_settings.bar_mode` (Postgres, E12-T02), restored on reload.
- Feature-flag gating for renko/range (`30-release-roadmap.md` §12 rung 2) so the descoping switch is a flag, not a code change.

## Out of scope
- Chart templates (US-CHART-012) and workspaces — E15 (this Story persists per-chart settings; templates compose them).
- The builders themselves (E12-S02/S03/S04) and the rebuild backend mechanism (E12-T03/T05).
- Footprint settings — E18.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Selecting a volume bar mode
  Given a BTCUSDT chart
  When I select "volume bars" with 1500 contracts
  Then the series rebuilds from stored prints with determinate progress
  And on completion the chart shows volume bars and the mode is persisted for that chart

Scenario: Rebuild is cancellable
  Given a rebuild is in progress
  When I cancel
  Then the rebuild stops within a second
  And the previous series is restored unchanged
  And no partial series is persisted or displayed

Scenario: Parameter bounds are explained
  When I enter a tick count below the documented minimum
  Then the value is rejected with a message stating the minimum
  And no rebuild is started

Scenario: Partial history is stated in text
  Given the recorder holds 3 days of prints and the view spans 30 days
  When I select tick bars
  Then bars are built for the available window
  And a marker states in text the timestamp where tick data begins
  And that statement is available to assistive technology

Scenario: Whole window predates recording
  Given the entire requested window is before recording began
  When I select a non-time bar mode
  Then the chart shows an explicit state explaining that tick-accurate data does not exist for this window
  And it offers to switch to time bars, which can be sourced from exchange klines

Scenario: Drawings survive the rebuild
  Given three drawings on the chart
  When the bar mode changes
  Then each drawing remains anchored to its original timestamps and prices

Scenario: Bar modes are presented as a distinct group
  Given the interval menu is open
  Then bar modes appear in a separately labelled group with an explanatory note
  And the note states that they change the meaning of the x-axis
  And the whole menu is operable by keyboard alone
```

## Technical notes / design
- Cancellation must propagate end to end: UI cancel → subscription teardown → backend rebuild cancellation (ADR-0014's mechanism). A UI-only cancel that leaves the backend grinding is a resource leak disguised as a feature.
- The previous series must be retained in memory (not evicted) while a rebuild is in flight so cancellation can restore it instantly without a refetch; the memory governor (E11-S15) must be told about this temporary retention.
- Rebuild progress is determinate where the total is known (trades to process) and switches to indeterminate with an explanation rather than a fake percentage when it is not.
- The renko/range feature flag gates the *menu entries*, so a descoped build simply does not offer them rather than offering them and failing.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: parameter validation per mode, persistence round-trip, flag gating, progress-state machine including cancel.
- **E2E** (Playwright + Electron): select each bar mode, change a parameter, cancel a rebuild mid-flight, confirm drawings unmoved and the previous series restored; verify the partial-history marker on a truncated fixture.
- **Integration**: cancellation verified to stop backend work (assert the rebuild metric stops advancing).
- **a11y**: axe-core on SCR-042 and SCR-047; keyboard-only operation of the menu and parameter entry; screen-reader pass confirming the bar-mode group label, the explanatory note and the partial-history statement.

## Security notes
Parameters entered here become `param` on a topic and an endpoint, so client-side validation mirrors the server-side whitelist (E12-T01) — but the server remains authoritative; the client check is UX, not a control. Bounds exist specifically to prevent the CPU/storage-exhaustion cases documented on E12-S02/S03/S04, and rejecting client-side keeps well-behaved clients from ever issuing them. Persisted `chart_settings.bar_mode` is validated against the CHECK-constrained enum on read, so a tampered row cannot select an unsupported renderer.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-220's contract is binding and is largely an accessibility contract: the menu button's accessible name includes the current interval ("Interval: 15 minutes"); bar modes form a separate labelled group with an explanatory note because they change the meaning of the x-axis. Parameter inputs have visible labels, are announced with their units, and validation errors are associated with the input via `aria-describedby` and stated as text including the limit. Rebuild progress is announced politely once at start and once at completion — not continuously. The partial-history marker and the no-data state are text, reachable by keyboard, and present in the SCR-045 data table, never colour-only. Reduced-motion is respected by the progress affordance.

## Performance notes
Menu open and parameter entry are instant (<50 ms). Rebuilds are bounded by the 10 s / 1M-print NFR of US-CHART-003/004 measured by E12-T04; cancellation takes effect within 1 s. Retaining the previous series during a rebuild must not breach the per-pane 512 MB GPU budget — if it would, the governor sheds the retained copy and cancellation falls back to a refetch, with that behaviour documented.

## Observability
`bar_mode_selected_total{mode}`, `bar_rebuild_started_total`, `bar_rebuild_cancelled_total`, `bar_rebuild_duration_seconds{kind}`, `bar_param_rejected_client_total{reason}`, `partial_history_markers_shown_total`. Mode-selection counts tell the Owner whether the descopable renko/range rung is actually used.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario automated; coverage ≥80%; cancellation verified end to end; axe-core green plus a keyboard-only and screen-reader pass on SCR-042; design-QA pass against the SCR-042 spec and CMP-220; QA sign-off; demoed (switch to volume bars, cancel a rebuild); feature-flag state recorded for `bars.renko` and `bars.range`; PR merged via the merge queue.

title: Add series-rendering scenarios to the engine benchmark CI gate
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criterion 1 requires that the frame budget be **"met and enforced in CI"**, with regressions >10% failing the build. E11-T06 builds the harness and makes it a required check; this Task adds E12's scenarios to it so that a series-rendering regression — the most likely kind, since series code changes most often — is caught by the same gate rather than discovered during a demo.

It is deliberately small and deliberately last: it locks in the numbers the rest of the Epic produced.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Benchmark scenarios registered in the E11-T06 harness: candle series at 5k / 50k / 100k bars across LOD tiers L0/L1/L2; OHLC bar, line, area and Heikin-Ashi series at 100k bars; the volume sub-pane enabled; a forming-bar update storm (20 updates/s over 60 s); a symbol/interval switch loop (100 switches) asserting stable GPU memory and zero context recreations.
- Baselines recorded per scenario on the reference hardware, committed alongside the harness.
- CI gating consistent with E11's policy: >10% regression fails, and a baseline change requires an explicit reviewed commit stating the reason.
- Backend counterpart: the bar-build and rebuild throughput numbers from E12-T04 published into the same dashboard so engine and builder performance are read together.
- A short runbook section describing how to reproduce a failing benchmark locally and how to interpret the `FrameStats` attribution.

## Out of scope
- The harness itself, the reference-hardware definition and the required-check wiring — **E11-T06**.
- The determinism/throughput harness — **E12-T04**.
- Load testing of the WS fan-out — E17/E46.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Series scenarios run in CI
  Given a pull request touching packages/chart-engine
  When CI runs
  Then every E12 benchmark scenario executes and reports p95 frame time, draw calls and GPU memory

Scenario: A regression fails the build
  Given a change that increases candle-series p95 frame time by more than 10 percent against the baseline
  Then the required check fails and names the scenario, the baseline and the measured value

Scenario: Switch-loop leak is caught
  Given a change that leaks GPU memory across symbol switches
  When the 100-switch scenario runs
  Then the memory-stability assertion fails
  And the failure names the growth per switch

Scenario: Baseline changes are deliberate
  Given a legitimate performance change
  When baselines are updated
  Then the commit contains the new baselines and a stated reason
  And CI rejects an implicit baseline rewrite
```

## Technical notes / design
- Reuse E11-T06's harness, reference-hardware profile and reporting format exactly; a second benchmark system with its own conventions is how perf gates get ignored.
- Scenarios must be deterministic: seeded synthetic datasets, fixed viewport sizes and fixed DPI, or the gate produces flaky failures and is disabled within a month.
- The 100-switch memory scenario is the one most likely to catch a real bug, because re-bind leaks are invisible in a single-shot benchmark.

## Test plan
The Task is test infrastructure. Its own verification is a deliberate-regression run: a seeded patch that slows the candle path by 15% must fail the gate, and a seeded per-switch leak must fail the memory assertion. Both are run as part of accepting this Task.

## Security notes
Benchmark fixtures are synthetic or public market data only — no keys, no account data, no recorded authenticated sessions. Benchmark artefacts published to CI must not include screenshots or dumps that could carry account context.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — CI infrastructure, no UI. Benchmark reports are plain text/tabular and readable without colour, so a CI log conveys the failure without relying on red/green alone.

## Performance notes
This Task *is* the performance gate for E12. Budgets enforced: p95 ≤16.6 ms (budget #1), ≥55 fps at 100k bars, ≤512 MB GPU per pane, ≤18 draw calls steady-state per pane, ≤200 ms symbol/interval switch, zero context recreations. The harness itself must complete within the CI time budget or be split into PR-gate and nightly tiers, matching E12-T04's policy.

## Observability
Results published to the same Grafana/CI dashboard as E11's engine benchmarks and E12-T04's builder throughput, so one view answers "is charting getting slower?" across both halves of this Epic.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2: scenarios registered and green; baselines committed; deliberate-regression and leak seeds both demonstrably caught; runbook section merged; before/after evidence attached (this Task has an observable effect, so a demo of a failing gate is required); PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S09** — LOD tiers must exist to be benchmarked.
- **E12-S11** — the switch loop scenario needs the re-bind path.
- **E11-T06** — the harness and the required-check wiring this Task extends.

title: Abuse cases: parameter fuzzing, resource exhaustion and data-integrity attacks
body:
## Context
`E12-X01` enumerates what could go wrong; this ticket tries to make it go wrong. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires a manual abuse-case check for security-relevant work, and the two E12 REST endpoints are the epic's widest attack surface: they accept a free-form `param` string, an unbounded-looking time window, a `limit`, a `bar_type` enum and a symbol, and they can trigger an expensive rebuild over millions of prints.

The threat that matters most is not classic injection — it is **cheap request, expensive server**: one crafted `GET /market/bars?bar_type=tick&param=1&from=…&to=…` can ask the backend to construct tens of millions of bars, and a loop of parameter changes can start a rebuild storm that starves ingestion and, through it, the trading surfaces. The second is **evidence integrity**: can an attacker (or a bug) get the system to serve bars that do not match the recorded tape, without saying so?

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Parameter fuzzing** of `/market/klines` and `/market/bars`: property-based and dictionary fuzzing over `symbol`, `interval`, `bar_type`, `param`, `from`, `to`, `limit`, `price_type`, `include_open`, `include_delta` — covering SQL/QuestDB-ILP metacharacters, path traversal, unicode/overlong forms, null bytes, negative and absurd numerics, inverted ranges (`from > to`), far-future and pre-epoch timestamps, `param` at and beyond the documented 24-char max, and `renko:atr:<huge>`. Assert: typed 400/422 with a documented error code, never a 500, never a stack trace, never an unbounded allocation, never a query that outlives its deadline.
- **Resource-exhaustion battery**: maximal-window requests per bar type; `tick:1` over a month; concurrent identical expensive requests (cache-stampede); a rebuild storm from rapid parameter flapping; the slow-WS-consumer case from `SR-073`. Assert documented caps are enforced server-side, that rejection is cheap, that one abusive session cannot degrade another session's p95 beyond budget #13, and that **ingestion message loss stays zero** throughout (budget #5) — the non-negotiable invariant.
- **Authorization probes**: unauthenticated request, session without `marketdata:read`, and a session whose permissions were revoked mid-stream while subscribed to `bars.*` — assert denial on REST and topic revocation on WS per `23-ws-protocol.md` §9, with no data frame after revocation.
- **Data-integrity attacks**: malformed/hostile upstream responses via the fake exchange (negative price, absurd size, wrong types, duplicated `trade_id`, timestamps far in the future) — assert boundary rejection with a counter, never ingestion into a builder; and attempt to serve bars from an incomplete `build_version` by interrupting a rebuild.
- **Debug-surface check**: confirm the test probe, diagnostics JSON island and any fixture-server override are absent or inert in a production build.
- An abuse-case report listing each attempt, the observed behaviour, the verdict, and a filed ticket for every failure; anything that yields a 500, a hang, cross-session degradation or a wrong-but-silent bar is `priority/p0-critical`.

## Out of scope
- Auth/session attacks themselves (E09's abuse cases), key handling (E27), order-path abuse (E32/E34).
- WS envelope/framing fuzzing (E17 owns the transport; this ticket fuzzes the `bars` topic's parameters and subscription semantics).
- Fixing findings — filed against the owning ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No input produces a 500 or a stack trace
  Given the fuzzing battery runs against /market/klines and /market/bars
  When several thousand crafted requests are sent
  Then every response is a documented 200, 400, 422 or 503 with a documented error code
  And no response body contains a stack trace, SQL text or internal path

Scenario: An expensive request is refused, not served slowly
  Given a request for tick bars with param=1 over a 30 day window
  Then the request is rejected with a documented limit error before significant work is done
  And the rejection costs less than the documented cap in CPU time

Scenario: Failure case - abuse must not touch ingestion
  Given a sustained abusive load of maximal-window bar requests plus a rebuild storm
  When the battery runs for 10 minutes
  Then ingestion message-loss counters remain zero
  And a concurrent well-behaved session's REST p95 stays within budget 13

Scenario: Edge case - permission revoked mid-subscription
  Given a session subscribed to bars.BTCUSDT.time.1 loses marketdata:read
  Then the topic is revoked per the WS protocol and no further bars frame is delivered
  And the revocation is audited

Scenario: Edge case - hostile upstream payload never reaches a builder
  Given the fake exchange emits a trade with a negative size and a year-3000 timestamp
  Then the print is rejected at the boundary with an incremented invalid-response counter
  And no bar in the affected window differs from the golden
```

## Technical notes / design
- Fuzzing runs against the fixture-backed staging profile with a schema-aware fuzzer seeded from the OpenAPI spec, so it generates *plausible* inputs that reach real code paths rather than being rejected at the router.
- Every expensive-request case asserts both the *outcome* (rejected) and the *cost* (server CPU/wall time attributable to the request), because a rejection that costs as much as the work is not a defence.
- Reuse `E12-Q06`'s fake exchange for the upstream-integrity cases and `E12-Q05`'s load harness for the exhaustion battery — this ticket contributes the adversarial scenarios, not a third copy of the infrastructure.
- Caps enforced must be exactly the numbers agreed in `E12-X01`; a discrepancy between the model and the implementation is itself a finding.

## Test plan
- Manual abuse session (the `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requirement) by the Security engineer plus an SDET, recorded.
- Automated regression subset: the highest-value cases (a representative fuzz corpus, the three exhaustion cases, the revocation case) promoted into CI so the defences do not silently rot.
- Each defence must be demonstrated to fail when removed — e.g. drop the `limit` cap and confirm the case turns red.

## Security notes
- This ticket *is* the security testing; findings feed `E12-X04` sign-off and the `E12-X01` residual-risk table.
- Runs exclusively against staging with a dedicated low-privilege account; a guard refuses execution against any host outside the staging range. Never against live — an abuse battery against the live trading stack is an outage.
- Any finding with exploitation potential beyond E12 (e.g. a generic API validation gap) is escalated to the programme level in `04-security-program.md` rather than closed locally.
- Findings are reported through the internal channel described in `SECURITY.md`; no details in public commit messages until fixed.

## Accessibility notes
- Verify that error responses surfaced to the UI by rejected/abusive inputs render as the accessible error state `SCR-048` with a text explanation, not a silent empty chart — a security control that degrades into an unexplained blank screen is an a11y defect too.

## Performance notes
- The exhaustion battery is measured, not merely attempted: attacker cost vs server cost is recorded per case, and the cross-session impact is quantified against budgets #5, #11 and #13.
- Results are contributed back to `E12-Q05`'s baselines so the defences have a performance regression story as well as a security one.

## Observability
- Assert that every rejection increments a labelled counter (`api_request_rejected_total{endpoint,reason}`) and emits a structured log with the offending parameter — without echoing the raw hostile value unescaped into logs (log injection).
- Assert an alert fires when rejection rate or rebuild rate crosses the threshold, so a real attack is visible rather than merely survived.

## Definition of Done
- Full battery executed; report merged at `docs/plan/security/abuse-cases/e12-bars.md`.
- Every failure filed with severity and owner; no open P0 at `E12-X04` sign-off.
- Regression subset wired into CI; each defence demonstrated to fail when removed.
- Caps reconciled with `E12-X01`; the model updated if reality differs.
- Security engineer review comment posted on this ticket.
- Findings presented at the security review; no public demo.

## Dependencies
- `E12-X01` (threat list and agreed caps), `E12-T05`, `E12-T06`, `E12-Q05`/`E12-Q06` infrastructure, E09 RBAC, E17 WS revocation.

## Branch
`chore/e12-x02-abuse-cases`

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-040, SR-042, SR-054, SR-073, O8, AC-08
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, §8
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines`, `/market/bars`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §9 revocation, §10 error catalogue
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #5, #11, #13
- `/SECURITY.md`

2. docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md (persistence/domain schemas)
