title: SAST/DAST rules and CI security gates for the bar and market-data surface
body:
## Context
A threat model and an abuse session are point-in-time. What keeps E12's properties true in six months, when five other epics are editing the same modules, is automation. `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA, secrets scanning and DAST (OWASP ZAP) as standing gates; `04-security-program.md` `SR-054` goes further and explicitly requires a **lint/Semgrep rule flagging any Bybit client call site lacking an explicit `category`**, with `ci-gate` as its verification method.

E12 is the first epic to make heavy use of the Bybit market-data client (kline backfill in `E12-S05`) and the first to write bars to the store, so it is the right place to land those rules.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Custom Semgrep rules** in `.semgrep/` targeting this surface:
  1. `bybit-category-required` — any Bybit client call without an explicit `category="linear"` fails (`SR-054`, `ci-gate`).
  2. `no-float-prices` — flags float arithmetic or `float()` on price/size/turnover fields in builder and store code; decimals only, matching the wire contract in `23-ws-protocol.md`.
  3. `no-raw-sql-interpolation` — flags f-string/`%`/`+` construction of QuestDB/Postgres query text in market-data modules; parameterised queries only.
  4. `unbounded-query-window` — flags a store query built from request parameters without passing through the shared window/limit clamp helper.
  5. `no-debug-probe-in-prod` — flags the diagnostics probe/test-clock seams outside test-only modules or without the build-time guard.
  6. `untrusted-exchange-response` — flags exchange payload fields consumed without passing through the validation layer (`SR-040`).
- **Bandit/CodeQL configuration** for the `M7`/`M8` packages with the relevant query packs enabled and a documented, justified suppression policy (each `# nosec`/suppression must carry a reason and an owner).
- **DAST (OWASP ZAP) profile** for the market-data endpoints: authenticated scan against staging covering `/market/klines` and `/market/bars`, with a tuned rule set (no false-positive noise from expected 422s) and a baseline that fails CI on new High/Medium alerts.
- **SCA and secrets scanning** coverage confirmed for any new dependency introduced by E12 (decimal libs, compression, parquet writers) with pip-audit/npm audit gating and a licence check for the fixture data manifest.
- **CI wiring**: all of the above as required checks on the relevant paths, with runtimes short enough to stay required; nightly full CodeQL/ZAP runs.
- A short `docs/plan/security/ci-gates-e12.md` explaining each rule, its rationale, how to fix a violation, and how to request an exception — rules nobody understands get suppressed, which is worse than no rule.

## Out of scope
- Writing the runtime validation/clamping code itself (owned by `E12-T05`/`E12-S05`); this ticket enforces its use.
- Container scanning (Trivy) and dependency policy at programme level (E43/DevSecOps).
- Pen-test (E43/E44 pre-live).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The category rule catches a real omission
  Given a Bybit kline call is written without category="linear"
  When the Semgrep gate runs in CI
  Then the job fails naming the file, line and SR-054
  And the message explains why the default must not be relied on

Scenario: Float prices are rejected in builder code
  Given a builder computes a bar high using float arithmetic
  Then the no-float-prices rule fails the build
  And the fix guidance points at the decimal contract in 23-ws-protocol.md

Scenario: Failure case - DAST finds a new High alert
  Given a change removes the window clamp on /market/bars
  When the nightly ZAP scan runs against staging
  Then a new alert is raised above the baseline and the job fails
  And the alert is triaged within the documented SLA

Scenario: Edge case - suppressions are visible and justified
  Given a developer adds a suppression to pass a rule
  Then CI requires an inline reason and an owner
  And unjustified suppressions fail the gate

Scenario: Edge case - rules do not drown the build in false positives
  Given the rules run over the existing codebase at merge time
  Then the total false-positive count is zero after tuning
  And each rule's precision is recorded in ci-gates-e12.md
```

## Technical notes / design
- Write each rule with a positive and a negative test case in `.semgrep/tests/`; a rule without tests is untrustworthy and will be deleted by the first person it annoys.
- Scope rules by path so they are strict where they matter (`M7`/`M8`, market-data API) rather than globally noisy; a global rule with exceptions everywhere teaches people to ignore it.
- Tune ZAP against the documented error behaviour so that legitimate 400/422 responses from `E12-X02`-style inputs are not reported as findings.
- Keep required-check runtime under ~3 minutes; push CodeQL's full analysis to nightly.

## Test plan
- Rule unit tests (positive/negative) in CI.
- Retro-detection check: run the rules against the commit history of `M8` and confirm they would have flagged at least one real past issue or, if none exists, record that explicitly.
- Seeded-violation PR demonstrating each of the six rules failing; evidence attached.

## Security notes
- The gates are the deliverable. Their purpose is to make `E12-X01`'s mitigations durable rather than aspirational.
- Secrets scanning must cover the fixture bank and benchmark artefacts, which are the plausible accidental-commit vectors in this epic.
- The DAST profile authenticates with a dedicated low-privilege staging account whose credentials live in the CI secret store, never in the repo; rotation is documented.

## Accessibility notes
- N/A for the gates themselves. Gate failure output is plain text with file/line/rationale so it is usable in a terminal or by a screen reader; no reliance on colour in CI annotations.

## Performance notes
- Required checks ≤3 minutes combined; nightly jobs unbounded but monitored.
- Rules are written to avoid pathological regex backtracking (a linter that hangs CI is an availability problem of our own making).

## Observability
- Gate outcomes are tracked over time (violations caught, suppressions outstanding, ZAP baseline drift) and reviewed in the security sync, so "green" is verified rather than assumed.
- New-dependency SCA findings route to the DevSecOps queue with severity-based SLAs.

## Definition of Done
- Six Semgrep rules merged with tests; Bandit/CodeQL config landed; ZAP profile and baseline committed.
- All gates wired as required checks on the correct paths plus nightly full runs.
- Seeded-violation evidence attached for every rule.
- Zero false positives on the current codebase; precision recorded.
- `docs/plan/security/ci-gates-e12.md` merged and linked from `04-security-program.md`.
- Security engineer review comment present; no demo required (shown at the security sync).

## Dependencies
- `E12-X01` (which threats need standing enforcement), `E12-T02`, `E12-S05` (the code the rules constrain), DevSecOps CI infrastructure, E17 for the staging DAST target.

`chore/e12-x03-security-gates`

title: Security review and sign-off for E12 bar builders and series
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires, for any epic carrying the `security` label, that the STRIDE model be finalised, findings triaged (fixed or accepted with Owner sign-off) and a sign-off comment posted by the Security engineer before the epic can be Done. §8 makes that non-skippable.

E12's security story is unusual and worth stating plainly at sign-off so that later epics inherit an accurate assumption rather than a vague one: **the bars this epic produces will be treated as ground truth by the order-flow, replay, journal and rule-engine epics, including rules that place live orders.** Signing off E12 means asserting that a bar served by the system either matches the recorded tape or is explicitly marked as not doing so.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A white-box security review of the E12 implementation against the `E12-X01` model: read the builder fan-out, persistence/dedup/`build_version` path, backfill client, the two REST handlers and the WS publisher, checking each modelled control is actually present in code and actually reachable.
- Verification that every mitigation row in the threat model has landed: input caps enforced server-side at the agreed numbers, decimal-only arithmetic, parameterised queries, explicit `category=linear`, exchange-response validation, bounded WS queues, `build_version` provenance in `meta`.
- Triage table of every finding from `E12-X02` (abuse cases), `E12-X03` (gate output), `E12-Q06` (chaos integrity findings) and any SAST/SCA/secrets result: fixed, accepted with Owner sign-off, or deferred with a dated ticket.
- **Evidence-integrity assertion**: a written statement, backed by `E12-Q02` golden results and `E12-Q06` chaos results, that served bars match the tape or are marked partial/gapped — this is the sentence downstream epics will rely on.
- A **consumer note** for E13/E18/E19/E23/E26/E37 stating exactly what guarantees they may assume (deterministic rebuild, `build_version` provenance, `confirm` semantics, `recording_started_at` honesty) and what they must not assume (no checksums per ADR-0005; non-time bars are not wall-clock aligned).
- Updated residual-risk section in `docs/plan/security/threat-models/e12-bars.md` reflecting what was built rather than what was proposed, plus a `32-risk-register.md` update if anything changed.
- The Security-engineer sign-off comment on the E12 epic ticket, with date, build sha and named signatory.

## Out of scope
- Pen-testing (E43, pre-live gate R4) — this review is internal and does not substitute for it, which the sign-off states explicitly.
- QA functional sign-off (`E12-Q08`), which is a separate, also-required gate.
- Security of consumers (E13/E18/E23) beyond issuing the consumer note.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every modelled control is verified in code
  Given the threat model's mitigation table
  When the reviewer walks the implementation
  Then each control is confirmed present, reachable and covered by a test
  And any control that is absent or unreachable is filed as a blocking finding

Scenario: All findings are triaged before sign-off
  Given findings from X02, X03 and Q06
  Then each is marked fixed, accepted with Owner sign-off, or deferred with a dated ticket
  And no finding is left untriaged

Scenario: Failure case - an open P0 blocks the epic
  Given an unfixed finding that lets the API serve bars diverging from the tape without marking them
  When sign-off is attempted
  Then sign-off is refused, E12 cannot be Done, and the finding is named in the refusal

Scenario: Edge case - a control was implemented differently than modelled
  Given the implementation enforces the window cap at the store layer rather than the handler
  Then the reviewer verifies the alternative is equivalent or stronger
  And the threat model is updated to describe what was actually built

Scenario: Edge case - downstream epics get an accurate guarantee
  Given the consumer note is published
  When an E18 engineer reads it
  Then the guarantees and non-guarantees are stated explicitly enough to design against without asking
```

## Technical notes / design
- Time-boxed to two days of review plus a one-hour walkthrough with the E12 tech lead; the goal is verification of specific modelled claims, not an open-ended code read.
- Use a checklist derived directly from the model's mitigation column so the review is reproducible and its absence of findings is meaningful.
- Where a control is claimed to be tested, follow the link to the actual test and confirm it asserts the control rather than merely exercising the path — a test that would pass with the control removed is not evidence.

## Test plan
- Verification is documentary plus spot-execution: the reviewer independently runs the `E12-X02` regression subset and one `E12-Q06` chaos scenario against the release-candidate build rather than trusting the report.
- Re-run of SAST/SCA/secrets on the RC build immediately before sign-off, so the sign-off refers to the shipped artefact.

## Security notes
- The sign-off comment must state the data classification (public market data), the evidence-integrity assertion, the explicit exclusion of pen-test coverage, and the conditions that would invalidate the sign-off (new bar type with a new parameter shape, account-scoped data entering the bars path, a privileged rebuild operation being added).
- Accepted risks require the Owner's written acceptance, recorded in the ticket, not a verbal nod.

## Accessibility notes
- Confirms one a11y-adjacent security property: security-driven rejections surface as the documented accessible error state (`SCR-048`) with a text reason, so a control never manifests as an unexplained blank chart.

## Performance notes
- Confirms the agreed caps did not silently break legitimate usage: a 30-day backfill and a 100 k-bar load still succeed within budgets #13 and #1 with the controls enabled — verified from `E12-Q05` baselines taken with the controls on.

## Observability
- Confirms the detection signals specified in `E12-X01` exist and alert: rejection counters, rebuild-rate alerting, `exchange_response_invalid_total`, `bars_gap_detected_total`, and that log fields carry `build_version`.
- Any modelled threat still lacking a detection signal blocks sign-off or is explicitly accepted.

## Definition of Done
- Review completed against the checklist; all findings triaged; blocking findings fixed and re-verified.
- Threat model residual-risk section updated to as-built; `32-risk-register.md` updated if needed.
- Consumer note published and linked from E13, E18, E19, E23, E26 epic tickets.
- SAST/SCA/secrets re-run clean on the RC build.
- Security-engineer sign-off comment posted on the E12 epic with date, build sha and signatory; Owner acceptance recorded for any accepted risk.
- Findings presented at the security review slot.

## Dependencies
- `E12-X01`, `E12-X02`, `E12-X03`, `E12-Q06`; a release-candidate build of E12; `E12-Q08` runs in parallel and is referenced, not blocking.

## Branch
`chore/e12-x04-security-signoff`

## References
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2, §3.2, §8
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` O8, SR-040, SR-042, SR-054, SR-073
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/` ADR-0005 (no checksums rationale)
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.8 `build_version`
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `meta.sources`, `meta.recording_started_at`
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3
